author: Maríangeles Guerrero
title: Sastre sin fumigaciones: “Lo que debería venir es la agroecología para las futuras generaciones”
content:
Por Mariángeles Guerrero


Desde Santa Fe


Siete líneas en una hoja membretada de la Corte Suprema de la Nación pusieron punto final a la batalla judicial que emprendieron, en 2018, vecinas y vecinos de la localidad de Sastre y Ortíz (Santa Fe). Los jueces Horacio Rosatti y Carlos Rosenkrantz desestimaron un reclamo de la municipalidad y convalidaron la decisión que ya había tomado la Corte santafesina: se deben establecer mil metros de distancia para las fumigaciones terrestres en relación a toda esa ciudad. El ministro Ricardo Lorenzetti se excusó de intervenir. Tras conocer el fallo, Sonia González, una de las impulsoras de la causa, pide: “Que no se dude ante la salud”. Asegura que ahora irán por la reforma de la ordenanza local, de acuerdo a lo establecido en los sucesivos fallos favorables que tuvo el expediente.


Sastre y Ortiz es una ciudad de 6.000 habitantes ubicada en el sudoeste santafesino, zona núcleo del agronegocio. A lo largo de la provincia, pueblos y ciudades conviven a diario con las avionetas y los mosquitos. Santa Fe cuenta con una ley obsoleta, que data de 1995, cuando aún no se había aprobado la soja transgénica en Argentina. La soja modificada genéticamente implicó un mayor avance de la frontera agrícola y un mayor uso de herbicidas, principalmente el glifosato. Pese a urgir una actualización, la Legislatura provincial cajoneó varios proyectos de reforma impulsados desde 2010 por organizaciones socioambientales.


En 2018, Zoe Giraudo tenía dos años y un diagnóstico: linfoma linfoblástico tipo T. Estaba internada en Rosario pero, al momento de poder regresar a su casa para continuar los tratamientos de quimioterapia desde allí, los médicos advirtieron a la familia: no podía estar cerca de los venenos. En la localidad ya se venían reuniendo vecinos para intentar que el Concejo local y de que la intendenta, María del Carme Amero, tome alguna medida preventiva ante los mosquitos que fumigaban a menos de cien metros de las viviendas. A fin de ese año se presentó el amparo colectivo que ahora concluyó en la última etapa procesal posible con una nueva sentencia a favor.


La demanda se presentó contra la Municipalidad tras varios intentos de diálogo con el Ejecutivo y el Concejo para que se reformara la Ordenanza Municipal 951/2004, que fijaba el límite de fumigación a solo cien metros a partir de la finalización del área urbana. En el juicio se presentaron como terceros interesados la provincia y una decena de productores. Si bien en 2020 el juez Francisco Hail, de Rafaela, dio la razón a los vecinos, la municipalidad apeló. Y siguió apelando hasta llegar a la Corte Nacional.


Desde la Capital Federal se puso fin al litigio alegando que el último recurso de queja presentado por la Municipalidad de Sastre carece de “fundamentación autónoma”. Cuando refiere a esta falencia, el máximo tribunal indica que una queja determinada no cuenta con un relato prolijo de los hechos y una crítica ordenada al fallo que se busca impugnar. En este caso, el de la Corte de Santa Fe.


El fruto de la lucha colectiva


En el contexto de una provincia donde se plantea la tensión entre salud y modelo productivo y se priorizan los intereses de los grupos concentrados que están detrás del glifosato, de los transgénicos y del monocultivo de commodities, vecinas y vecinos iniciaron un camino que no abandonaron. Y lograron un fallo que ahora implica un precedente relevante para las localidades de Santa Fe y para otros pueblos fumigados del país. Hoy Zoe Giraudo tiene 10 años y su mamá siente que, con esta resolución, deja de cargar una mochila que llevó por años. “Estamos orgullosos como grupo y yo como mamá, porque siento que hice un montón por mi hija”, dice González.


—¿Cómo comenzó la movilización en Sastre?

—La lucha de los vecinos empezó hace muchísimo tiempo, porque había muy pocos vecinos que estaban tratando de alejar estos venenos que ya se sabía que hacían mal. En 2018, una vecina que vive a una cuadra vio un mosquito que estaba fumigando a 70 metros de su casa. Y coincidió con el tiempo en que yo tenía a Zoe, mi nena, internada en Rosario. Esa vecina empezó a buscar soluciones: yendo a la municipalidad, a juntar firmas, a levantar publicaciones en las redes. Zoe se estaba atendiendo con los mejores médicos, pero al final no tenía resguardo con respecto a los venenos. Ellos se juntaron como vecinos, juntaron firmas, fueron al Concejo Municipal y nada. No hubo soluciones. Eso pasó en marzo. Los vecinos …

author: Rizomatica
title: Comunicado Público de los Presos políticos mapuche de la Franja lavkenche condenados en el Caso Grollmus
content:
COMUNICADO PÚBLICO


Frente a las exuberantes condenas y tras un viciado proceso declaramos:


Mari mari pu machi, pu lonko, pu werken, kom pu che.


El día de hoy nos dirigimos a la sociedad en general, a todos y todas quienes nos han brindado su apoyo y respaldo en este proceso denominado “CasoGrollmus».


Actualmnente a nosotros como comuneros mapuche se nos ha condenado a penas que marcarán un precedente como obscenamente políticas, se nos condena por decisión política, por ser mapuche que vivimos y recuperamos nuestro territorio.


Tras el gigantesco despliegue comunicacional, y tras el espectáculo montado por el Ministerio Público y la PDI, la familia Grollmus demanda al estado en busca de indemnizaciones y reparaciones.


La fiscalía con el aval del tribunal logró su objetivo: condenar a una pena que ponderada resulta en 1055 años de prisión contra nosotros.


La prensa vociferó la sentencia y el poder político respaldo, claridad absoluta.


Les decimos, su ocupación contra nuestro pueblo y su territorio apenas tiene 143 años. Nuestro pueblo resistió al imperio español casi 300 años.


Hoy Chile soberbio y republicano nos condena a más de 1000 años. Por el único motivo de luchar por nuestra soberanía, por nuestro buen vivir y dignidad. Lo anterior tendrá la más necesaria respuesta: continuar con el legado de nuestro pueblo, luchar por nuestra dignidad y libertad.


Los Grupos de Tarea y la BIPE de la PDI recorre los penales de forma morbosa buscando testigos a quienes poner corbata de protegido y sin rostro.


Solo por cuatro relatos de estos “testigos» se dictó sentencia y veredicto. Nuestro territorio se militariza y vuelven a saquear nuestros recursos naturales, vuelven las concesiones mineras, CMPC y Mininco cual mecenas entregan dinero y donaciones a Postas y Escuelas.


Queremos manifestar nuestro agradecimiento por todo el respaldo de nuestros hermanos y hermanas en otros territorios y ciudades.


No renunciaremos jamás a la lucha por un debido y objetivo proceso.


Nos movilizaremos por nuestra libertad y juicio justo.


Finalmente los invitamos a sumarse a la próxima movilizaciónarticulada en distintos territorios para este 12 de octubre, Día de la resistencia de nuestros pueblos.¡


NULIDAD Y LIBERTAD!¡


NO MÁS TESTIGOS PROTEGIDOS!


¡UNIDAD EN EL WEYCHAN!


¡LIBERTAD A TODOS LOS PRESOS POLÍTICOS MAPUCHE!


Presos Políticos Mapuche del Caso Grollmus de la Franja Lavkenche, CP Biobio, CERECO Coronel, Cárcel Llancahue de Valdivia.

author: anred
title: Claudio Katz: «hay que construir la izquierda para derrotar a Milei»
content:
Tras la repercusión de la Marcha de la Bronca, Claudio Katz analizó el rol de la izquierda en la coyuntura actual, donde juegan cada vez más fuerte dos variables: el retroceso de Milei y un potencial estallido económico. Las incógnitas sobre el peronismo, la apuesta del establishment a perpetuar el esquema de ajuste, explotación laboral y saqueo del país que logró establecer durante la actual gestión, la impunidad de la Corte Suprema y la agresividad del imperialismo estadounidense en la región son datos ineludibles del escenario presente ante los cuales la izquierda deberá plantearse nuevas tácticas y compromisos, consideró Katz, si quiere llegar al gobierno y disputar el poder.

Por Indymedia Argentina.


Indymedia: – ¿Cómo ves el papel de la izquierda luego de la Marcha de la Bronca?


Claudio Katz:

 – Está cumpliendo un papel muy positivo ante todo en la acción callejera. La marcha fue un éxito

 por la

 concurrencia y el impacto de un acto político, que traspasó la resistencia social y democrática a los atropellos de Milei. Contrastó frontalmente con la capitulación de la CGT que deja pasar el ajuste.


La movilización alcanzó el nivel más alto de una convocatoria de 

la izquierda. Superó lo conseguido con la “Plaza del No” en los años 90 y con las grandes concentraciones que en el pasado articulaba el 

PC. Exhibió un nivel de politización muy superior a las marchas piqueteras e ilustró nuevamente cómo gravita la izquierda en las coyunturas de inmovilidad del peronismo.


Esa indefinición del justicialismo se vio por ejemplo cuando ganó Alfonsín, durante el neoliberalismo de Menem o en la época de Alianza. Actualmente, vuelve a aflorar por momentos y por eso hubo cierta presencia de militantes o simpatizantes del peronismo en la marcha. Igualmente te diría que el dato más significativo fue la centralidad de Myriam 

Bregman. La movilización consolidó su protagonismo y la consiguiente incidencia de la izquierda en las próximas elecciones.


Indymedia: – 

Pero cuál es la proyección electoral efectiva de Myriam, porque las encuestas resaltan una imagen muy positiva sin equivalencia en la intención de voto…


Claudio Katz: – Hay infinitas especulaciones sobre esa relación y no tiene mucho sentido obsesionarse con el tema, cuando falta más de un año para la elección. El número de votos que lograría el FIT-U depende de escenarios muy 

abiertos con dos variables centrales: el retroceso de Milei y un potencial estallido económico, que podría repetir lo ocurrido tantas veces en la Argentina.


Foto: 

Nicolas Solo ((i))


Nadie sabe si el gobierno podrá sostener el tipo de cambio hasta el 2027. La recesión, la pobreza y el endeudamiento podrían desencadenar el mismo tipo de rebelión que sepultó a De la Rúa o la protesta masiva que derrotó a Macri. No cabe duda que la izquierda estará en la primera línea de ese eventual estallido.


Pero en cualquier caso su crecimiento dependerá de lo que suceda con el peronismo y en ese campo hay varios cursos posibles de división o cohesión y de amoldamiento conservador o resurgimiento progresista.


Por el momento se verifica una gran fractura en el justicialismo, entre corrientes de adaptación y crítica al modelo que la clase dominante apuntala con Milei. En general predomina la postura de no decir nada a la espera de lo que más conviene. Pero mientras tanto, un fascista como Cúneo participa del espacio de Kicillof, que a su vez emite mensajes de adaptación tipo Alberto Fernández y elude comentarios básicos de denuncia del genocidio de Palestina. Pero lo que haría como presidente es un misterio. Conviene recordar que nadie imaginaba el giro progresista de Néstor y Cristina antes del 2001 y sería un error ignorar la recomposición que logró el peronismo al calor de la gestión kirchnerista.


Indymedia: –

 ¿Por qué importa ese dato?


Claudio Katz: – Porque conforma el escenario en el que actúa la izquierda. Desconociendo ese hecho es muy difícil desenvolver estrategias para derrotar a Milei, revertir el ajuste y reconquistar los derechos populares. Ese camino transita por llegar al gobierno y disputar el poder, mediante frentes comunes y acuerdos de lucha con los sectores dispuestos a reconstruir el país, apostando a un gobierno que en sus primeros días de gestión revierta de un plumazo todo lo hecho por Milei.


Foto: 

Nicolas Solo ((i))


Ese es el eje el debate actual. Si derogaremos o no de inmediato las leyes laborales, el RIGI, los Glaciares o la impunidad de la Corte …

author: Comunizar
title: Revista Crítica Anticapitalista 6 – La Comuna, la clase y la lucha de clases
content:
PRESENTACION


¿Qué relación existe entre la Comuna como forma política de la emancipación social y la clase, entendida ésta no como categoría positivizada y sociológica, sino en su carácter dual y contradictorio? ¿Es la Comuna una manera de entender la clase y la lucha de clases en clave no identitaria, no positivizada? ¿La oposición entre Comuna y clase es algo derivado de una concepción anti-dialéctica de la lucha de clases? En ese campo ¿a qué dialéctica nos referimos? ¿A la dialéctica hegeliana orientada a la síntesis estatal como forma política de la identidad? ¿A la dialéctica negativa que la cuestiona? ¿La lucha de clases, entendida en clave dialéctica no-identitaria, permite entender la Comuna como proceso contradictorio de disolución de la clase? ¿Implica esto un desafío a nuestro concepto de proletariado y a la idea de revolución calcada en el canon leninista?

author: Wanessa Celina
title: A “bancada” anti-indígena que vai às urnas neste domingo
content:
Nas duas últimas legislaturas no Congresso Brasileiro, 370 deputados e senadores foram responsáveis por propostas de lei que enfraquecem os direitos indígenas — e 270 deles disputam reeleição neste ano. Ao todo, esses políticos atuaram em 252 projetos, a maioria incidindo negativamente sobre o direito à terra para esses povos.


As informações são baseadas em um levantamento da

Agência Pública

 a partir da nova plataforma lançada pelo Conselho Indigenista Missionário (Cimi), o

Congresso Anti-Indígena

.


Entre os projetos de lei que afetam os indígenas, estão propostas que buscavam anular decretos de demarcação de territórios e outros que alteram a Constituição Federal, para que as decisões sobre a demarcação sejam feitas pelo Congresso Nacional — justamente onde estão os políticos que atuam contra a demarcação de mais terras.


Para Cleber Buzatto, missionário do Cimi Regional Sul, essa atuação mostra que o principal interesse é impedir as demarcações e também explorar as terras.


“Isso demonstra uma articulação dos setores anti-indígenas, seja do ponto de vista político, mas, também, dos grupos econômicos que têm interesses sobre as terras, portanto, se organizam e atuam de forma bastante enfática e violenta contra os direitos indígenas no Congresso Nacional por meio de um conjunto amplo de partidos e parlamentares”, explica Buzzatto.


Entre 513 deputados e deputadas federais eleitos em 2022, apenas cinco se autodeclaram indígenas, menos de 1% do total. Como a

Pública


mostrou

, neste ano, o movimento indígena lançou 47 pré-candidaturas para tentar mudar esse quadro

.

 “É importante que os próprios povos [indígenas] consigam acessar espaços nessas casas legislativas, especialmente no âmbito da Câmara dos Deputados, que é onde tem mais candidatos indígenas disputando as vagas, até para que essa diretriz seja coerente com a defesa de fato dos direitos e dos interesses dos projetos de vida e futuro dos povos indígenas”, afirma.


Atualmente, segundo dados do Cimi, 291 propostas legislativas que impactam os direitos indígenas tramitam no Congresso Nacional. Entre elas, 204 têm efeitos negativos, segundo o levantamento.


PL, de Bolsonaro, é o principal partido a votar em propostas anti-indígenas, aponta levantamento


A partir da análise de mais de 41 mil votos, a plataforma identificou, dentre os partidos políticos, 19 que votaram sempre ou quase sempre em projetos que vão contra os povos indígenas. Apenas oito partidos votaram favoravelmente.


O Partido Liberal (PL), do candidato à presidência Flávio Bolsonaro, fica em primeiro lugar tanto entre os partidos cujos políticos mais propuseram propostas anti-indígenas, quanto entre os parlamentares que mais votam em projetos contrários aos direitos desses povos. São 95 proposições e 6.630 votos desfavoráveis segundo a classificação do Cimi. Em seguida, está o MDB, com 47 proposições, e o Partido Progressista (PP), com 42. Já entre os partidos cujos políticos tiveram mais votos em projetos contrários aos direitos indígenas, após o PL, está o PP, com 3.232 votos, e, em terceiro lugar, o União, com 3.063.


Por outro lado, o Partido dos Trabalhadores (PT), do presidente e candidato Lula, é o que mais teve propostas e votos em projetos classificados como favoráveis aos indígenas, com 4.971 a favor e 71 proposições. Em seguida, está o PSB, com 1.127 votos a favor, e o PDT, com 1.114 votos. O PCdoB, mesmo com apenas 11 deputados na Câmara, tem 100% dos votos direcionados a pautas consideradas favoráveis aos indígenas. Após o PT, entre os partidos que mais propuseram propostas favoráveis, estão o Psol, com 31 propostas.


Políticos que fizeram mais propostas com efeitos negativos aos direitos indígenas, segundo o levantamento


Deputado federal Marcos Pollon (PL-MS)


Candidato à reeleição para deputado federal pelo Mato Grosso do Sul, o deputado tem um total de 26 propostas classificadas como contrárias aos direitos indígenas, sendo 24 delas sobre o direito territorial dos povos tradicionais. O deputado é o terceiro-secretário da Frente Parlamentar

Invasão Zero

, grupo criado em 2023 que defende o direito à propriedade contra o Marco Temporal.


Entre as principais propostas do deputado está o PL 2145/2023, que altera o “Estatuto do Índio” para impedir o reconhecimento de determinadas áreas como de ocupação tradicional. author: Unknown
title: 46 countries call for executions in Iran to be halted
content:
In a report published on 1 October 2026, the Iran Human Rights Organization reported that 46 countries had called for a halt to the rising number of executions in the Islamic Republic of Iran.


According to the report, a joint statement presented by the representative of Liechtenstein at the 63rd session of the United Nations Human Rights Council on 30 September 2026, was signed by 46 countries.


The statement said that at least 31 protesters had been executed since the crackdown on protests in December 2025 began. It also noted that dozens of people, including women and children, were at risk of execution.


Citing findings by UN experts, the signatory countries emphasized that the death penalty in Iran was being used to instill fear, suppress dissent, and restrict the freedoms of peaceful expression and assembly.


The joint statement also raised concerns about secret trials, violations of fair trial guarantees, torture and ill-treatment, enforced disappearances, and forced confessions.


The 46 countries called on the Iranian authorities to immediately end the use of the death penalty.

author: groundxero
title: A Tale of Irony: The Sijimali Story from Odisha
content:
Vedanta’s Sijimali bauxite mining project has thrown Odisha’s Rayagada and Kalahandi districts into the eye of a storm. The predominantly tribal communities living in the villages at the foothills of Sijimali are opposing the project and the State has come down heavily on them.


 


Dr. Sankalpa Satapathy


 


Vedanta Limited’s Sijimali bauxite mining project aimed at supplying bauxite to the Lanjigarh refinery has thrown Odisha’s Rayagada and Kalahandi districts into the eye of a storm. The predominantly tribal, Kui speaking Kondh and Paraja communities have strongly opposed the project and the State has come down heavily on them. The violent clashes between the villagers and police personnel on April 7, 2026 were only the tip of the iceberg. The resistance has been ongoing for years now.


 


For the people living in the villages at the foothills of Sijimali, the mountain range, the forests, the streams are not just resources to be used but an integral part of their lives, an ecosystem that pervades every aspect of their lives. The dense deciduous forests along with non-timber produce, traditional ancestral lands, non-human dwellers and the watershed that these forested mountain range harbour, sustain traditional livelihoods and support the local economy. During lean agricultural seasons, families survive on wild food such as tubers, roots, fruits etc. They rely on deep traditional ecological knowledge built over centuries and transmitted through generations in orally codified forms which emphasize sustainable use rather than exploitation to maintain ecological balance. Indigenous community driven techniques and practices harvest, store, and manage rainwater and groundwater, protect trees, soil, and wildlife and use medicinal herbs, roots, leaves and barks for treatment of illnesses. They are culturally and traditionally deeply linked to these forests believing that their deity “Tij Raja” resides in the mountains. They get everything from the mountains and do not buy anything from outside adhering to Gandhi’s concept of self-sufficiency, Swadeshi and Gram Swaraj which focused on village independence, local production and simple living.


 


Beneath these forests lies an estimated reserve of 311 million tonnes of bauxite which is fundamental for the smooth running of the Vedanta Lanjigarh refinery to drive

“growth and development of the region”

. To reach the bauxite, the communities have to be displaced, the forests have to be felled and the mountains have to be dug in a large open cast mine. In short, the entire ecosystem has to be disrupted and destroyed. Felling forests in the mountain range leads to washing off of the rich top soil which is held together by the tree roots. These forests “catch” rain and refill underground aquifers, elevating water tables and nourishing local streams. Losing forests reduces local humidity and rain making the region hotter and drier.


 


The soil erosion, disruption of the local water cycle, destruction of natural wind and dust barriers turn fertile land dry and barren, leading to desertification. Ironically, India has ratified major UN environmental treaties like the UN Convention to Combat Desertification in 1996 and the Paris Agreement in 2016. After data confirmed that July 2023 was the hottest in recorded human history, the Secretary General of the United Nations, Antonio Guterres declared that “the era of global warming has ended, the era of global boiling has arrived”. It was in the same year 2023 that the auction of bauxite mining lease for Sijimali by the government of Odisha was won by Vedanta Ltd which as explained before, if comes to fruition will lead to desertification and add to the already soaring summer temperatures in Odisha.


 


Both the districts, Rayagada and Kalahandi, are designated as Scheduled Areas and fall under the Fifth Schedule of the Constitution which exists to protect indigenous tribal communities, preserve their unique culture, and prevent their economic exploitation. A Tribes Advisory Council (TAC) with mostly tribal members is mandatorily set up to advice on tribal welfare in these areas. This raises the question that if all necessary legislative procedures were followed why are the tribals up in arms in dissent against the state and why is there a military buildup in the areas? Why are there allegations from the tribals that the signatures on the Gram Sabha documents are in English whereas the people of the region write in Odia or …

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Labnotes | Ang kontradiksyon ng renewable energy transition sa Pilipinas
content:
The 54MW Pililla Wind Power Project in Pililla, Rizal is operated by Vena Energy. Photo by Chantal Eco

Sa kalagitnaan ng krisis sa klima, ibinibida ng gobyerno at ng mga malalakihang korporasyon ang transition sa renewable energy bilang solusyon — na ang mga solar, wind farm, at iba pa ay susi sa mura’t malinis na enerhiya. Pero habang kinakalbo ang mga kabundukan para itayo ang wind turbines, solar panels, at mga dambuhalang dams, ang bill ng kuryente—palagi pang tumataas!

Ang mga dapat itanong: sino ang may-ari ng mga planta, sinu-sino ang may kontrol ng transmisyon at distribusyon, at para saan ba talaga ang Electric Power Industry Reform Act o EPIRA?

Patuloy ang pagdami ng mga wind at solar farm sa Pilipinas. Noong 2022, 1,530 megawatt (MW) na kuryente ang mula sa solar, at nadoble ito noong 2025 sa 3,003 MW. Umaabot na ngayon sa 3,892 MW (3.9 GW) ang kapasidad mula sa solar, habang ang wind farm o kuryenteng mula sa hangin ay nananatili sa 427 MW lamang.

Sinasabing malinis at mas mura ang kuryenteng nagmumula sa modernong teknolohiyang Renewable Energy (RE) tulad ng solar at wind farm. Ang RE ay teknolohiyang gumagamit ng mga likas na yamang halos di-nauubos tulad ng araw, hangin, at tubig. Mahigit 22 porsyento ng kuryente sa bansa ang galing sa RE — nagmumula ito sa geothermal plants (9.1%), hydroelectric dams (8.7%), solar farm (2.2%), wind farm (1.1%), at iba pang planta ng enerhiyang hindi umaasa sa petrolyong rekurso.

Sinasabi na kapag nagtayo ka ng RE tulad ng solar farm, ito ay mas mura kaysa sa paggamit ng coal power plant na karaniwang itinatayo ngayon ng mga pribadong korporasyon sa enerhiya. Nasa P2.99 kada kilowatt-oras (kWh) lamang ang gastos sa kuryente kapag solar ang gamit, habang PHP3.50/kWh naman kapag hangin ang gamit. Malaking mura ito kumpara sa paggamit ng karbon o coal na may presyong PHP3.80–5.50/kWh, o sa imported na diesel na umaabot sa PHP15–28/kWh. (Tingnan ang Talahanayan 2.) Hindi na rin bumibili ng panggatong tulad ng langis, diesel, o coal ang mga pribadong kumpanya upang paganahin ang kanilang mga planta, dahil tuloy-tuloy at libre ang suplay ng rekurso tulad ng hangin at araw.

Kung kaya ito ang paborito ngayon ng gobyerno at ng mga monopolyong korporasyon sa enerhiya tulad ng MERALCO at First Gen ni Manny Pangilinan, ng Aboitiz Power ng mga Aboitiz, San Miguel Global Power ni Ramon Ang, Prime Infrastructure ni Enrique Razon, at ACEN ng mga Ayala. Sinasabi ng mga korporasyon na magpapababa ito ng singil sa kuryente. Sa ilalim ng Philippine Energy Plan 2023–2050 ng gobyernong Marcos Jr., layunin nitong pataasin ang suplay ng kuryenteng nagmumula sa RE hanggang 35 porsyento sa 2030 at 50 porsyento sa 2050. Sa kasalukuyan, tumaya ang DOE sa 16,337 MW na solar farm at 5,377 MW ng wind farm na proyekto sa buong bansa — lahat ng ito ay pag-aari ng mga pribado at dayuhang korporasyon.

Kung mura ang teknolohiyang RE, bakit patuloy pa ring tumataas ang singil sa kuryente? Bakit hindi nakikinabang dito ang mga mahihirap at maliliit na konsumer? Sa kasalukuyan, nagbabayad ang mga konsumer ng P13 hanggang PHP16 kada kWh sa mga distributor ng kuryente. Ang Pilipinas ngayon ang may pinakamahal na singil sa kuryente sa Asya, habang isa naman ito sa mga bansang may pinakamababang minimum wage sa rehiyon. Mahal na ang kuryente, mababa pa ang kita ng mga ordinaryong pamilyang Pilipino.

Kailan lamang pinayagan ng Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) ang MERALCO na magdagdag ng singil sa kuryente. Kalakip dito ang pagtaas ng FIT-All (Feed-in Tariff Allowance) mula P0.2011 patungong P0.3359 kada kWh. Ayon sa batas, garantisado ng gobyerno ang pagbayad sa mga korporasyon para sa kanilang mga proyektong RE sa loob ng 20 taon — dagdag na mabigat na pasanin sa mamamayan sa loob ng dalawang dekada.

Hindi pa rito natatapos ang pangongotong ng mga kumpanya sa elektrisidad. May nakaambang dagdag na singil sa tinatawag na GEA-All o Green Energy Auction Allowance, na nagpopondo sa mga inaprubahang proyektong RE ng gobyernong Marcos — ilan sa mga ito ay nabanggit na sa itaas. Ibig sabihin, ang mamamayan mismo ang pinagkukuhanan ng puhunan para sa pagtatayo ng mga bagong proyektong RE. Mamamayan ang magpopondo sa mga proyektong ito, at sisingilin pa tayo ng mahal na presyo ng kuryente. Ginigisa tayo sa sarili nating mantika!

author: rti_admin
title: From Inheritance to Inquiry: The Courage to Question
content:
A society becomes dynamic not when everyone thinks alike, but when people possess the freedom and courage to question, debate and rethink what they have inherited. Every generation receives beliefs, customs, institutions and social practices from the past. Some enrich human life; others may perpetuate inequality simply because they have acquired the authority of tradition. The true measure of a mature society, therefore, is not how faithfully it preserves its inheritance, but how intelligently it examines it. In the Indian context, this becomes particularly important when we reflect upon caste, religion and patriarchy. These are not merely abstract concepts. They influence family life, marriage, social status, personal choices and opportunities. Yet meaningful discussion of them is often displaced by sentiment, identity politics, unquestioned authority or fear of disagreement. What India needs is not less tradition or less faith, but more reasoned discourse about their social consequences.

I. Caste, Religion and Patriarchy: Examining the Inherited Order

Caste is one of the most enduring forms of social stratification in India. It historically connects social status with birth and influences occupation, marriage, social interaction, and access to resources. B. R. Ambedkar’s Annihilation of Caste remains a foundational challenge to a social order in which birth becomes the basis of hierarchy. His analysis also highlighted endogamy—the practice of marrying within the group—as a mechanism through which caste boundaries are reproduced. The fundamental question is simple: Can the circumstances of one’s birth legitimately determine one’s dignity, status or opportunities? Modern India has transformed caste through constitutional equality, education, democratic politics, social mobility and affirmative action. Yet caste continues to influence matrimonial choices, political mobilisation, social networks and community identities. The challenge, therefore, is neither to deny caste nor to reduce it to a political slogan, but to understand how an inherited hierarchy adapts to modern conditions.

Religion raises a different but equally important question. Religion has provided meaning, morality, community and spiritual consolation to millions. It cannot simply be dismissed as superstition. A democratic society must protect freedom of belief. But freedom of belief must coexist with freedom of inquiry. When religious claims influence public behaviour or decisions concerning health and human welfare, they necessarily become open to discussion. The growing influence of charismatic spiritual figures and the wider “Baba culture” makes the question of authority especially relevant. Spiritual guidance may be valuable, but spiritual status should not automatically confer unquestionable authority. Patriarchy presents a third dimension of inherited social organisation. Traditional gender roles have often assigned authority, responsibility and freedom differently to men and women. Simone de Beauvoir demonstrated how social expectations can transform biological difference into unequal social possibilities. The question is not whether men or women are superior. It is whether gender should predetermine freedom, dignity, security and opportunity. Caste, religion and patriarchy frequently intersect within the family, marriage and community, where identities and expectations are transmitted across generations.

II. India’s Own Tradition of Questioning

The call for reasoned discourse should not be presented as an imported Western idea. India possesses a long and diverse intellectual tradition of questioning, argument and dissent. The Buddha challenged unquestioned authority and encouraged inquiry into suffering, conduct and knowledge. His intellectual approach placed emphasis on understanding rather than merely accepting claims on the basis of authority or tradition. The Charvaka or Lokayata tradition represents another striking strand of Indian intellectual history. Its materialist and sceptical orientation challenged metaphysical claims and questioned religious authority. Although much of what is known about Charvaka comes through its critics, its historical presence demonstrates that Indian thought included vigorous disagreement about religion, knowledge and reality. The Upanishadic dialogues similarly reveal a culture in which fundamental questions about existence and knowledge were explored through intellectual conversation.

title: Workers dismissed from Amed City Hospital construction site launch strike
content:
At the construction site of the City Hospital, currently under construction in the Peyas (Kayapınar) district of Amed, 90 members of the Construction, Road and Highway Workers’ Union employed by the main contractor and subcontractor were dismissed.


Workers who launched a strike outside the hospital construction site in protest against the dismissals received visits of support from the Amed Labor and Democracy Platform and representatives of political parties. During a statement outside the site, a banner reading “The world will belong to labor” was displayed, and protesters chanted slogans including “Gürbağ, don’t be mistaken, don’t push our patience to the limit.”


Speaking at the gathering, Sabahat Sever, co-chair of the Amed No. 2 Branch of the Genel-Iş Union, affiliated with DISK, said they stood in solidarity with construction workers who had joined a union and were fighting for their rights by exercising their constitutional rights.


Sever stated that the rights violations at the construction site were inseparable from the working conditions faced by workers across the country. She said workers were struggling for humane working conditions and wages that would allow them to make a living.


Pointing to the heavy toll imposed on the working class by capital’s pursuit of profit and the lack of oversight, Sever said workers at construction sites, mines, factories and hospitals were being employed under conditions of insecurity, pressure and low wages.


Noting that the necessary measures to prevent fatal workplace accidents were not being taken, Sever said the existing system aimed to cheapen labor and leave workers unorganized.


Workers' demands


Stating that the Amed Labor and Democracy Platform supported the struggle of the dismissed workers, Sabahat Sever listed their demands as follows:


-The immediate reinstatement of all dismissed workers.


-Full payment of unpaid wages and other outstanding entitlements, and reimbursement of unjustified wage deductions.


-An end to pressure and dismissals targeting workers for union organizing.


-Respect for workers’ trade union rights.


-The provision of humane working conditions and an end to violations of workers’ rights.


-Necessary action against those responsible for preventing workers from exercising their rights and committing violations of those rights.


Following the statement, construction workers also said they would continue their protest until their demands were met. The gathering concluded with slogans.

author: groundxero
title: The revolutionary act of womanly love
content:
Ashley Tellis

 thinks Karthik Subbaraj’s

Dorothy

, currently making waves in Tamil Nadu, is, like some other of his films, a feminist cult classic


 


Karthik Subbaraj’s

Dorothy

 ushers in the return of Tamil cinema but, more importantly, will go down in history as one of popular Tamil cinema’s most powerful feminist films. At the heart of it, like his earlier film

Iraivi

, and arguably many other of his films, is a critique of Tamil patriarchy from the position of the feminine, this time occupied in the world not just by women but also by certain sexual minorities. That he combines this deftly with a critique of caste and class in the Tamil heartland makes it an even more powerful exposé of Tamil patriarchy.


 


At the heart of Subbaraj’s vision is the idea of woman as goddess (

Iraivi

 means goddess), a very powerful trope in Tamil Nadu. Subbaraj’s genius is not just that he exposes the hollowness of the worship of woman as goddess in Tamil Nadu by showing how woman (and woman-identified subjects, which include

aravanis

, effeminate gay men and trans women) are actually treated but also to wield the affective power of the goddess figure in Tamil Nadu to work against sexual oppression, caste violence and class inequality, in a very grounded, material sense that actually has nothing to do with goddess worship.


 


Sexual Oppression: The feminist heart of

Dorothy


 


At the heart of the film is an

aravani

1

 who has been in denial of her

aravani

ness all her life, not least because of the terrifying violence her misogynist, classist and casteist family (comprising only of men – a father and two much older brothers) will visit upon her should she reveal it, but also because she is terrified of losing the love of her life, her childhood friend, whom she plays male buddy to all her life just to keep him close. That he, the love of her life, is of a lower caste than her (as with all Tamil cinema, actual castes are never mentioned in the film, especially when they are most at play – one of the curiosities of Tamil cinema) makes her eventual transgression even more delicious.


 


However, when things get out of hand, she explodes, becomes herself and the first words she utters while beating up her hideous brothers and father are, “Not ladyboy (what they insult her with, in her sari) but woman!


 


This identification with woman and wanting to be a woman is not the North American and Western European (including, especially, British) transgender claim to

be

 woman, with its entitlement, abuse and nastiness, increasingly visible in India too, in the fledgling transgender movement here. It is an identification

with

 women, with the position of woman in culture, woman as placeholder for different kinds of violences, all of which are contested in the film.


 


Indeed, images of dead, violated and violable women float through the film: the murdered mother, the murdered (and possibly raped) sister and the eponymous figure, who is so beautiful, she is likened to a doll (also possibly raped and definitely murdered) – all three women’s murders passed off as suicides; the lower caste woman who comes to ask for her pawned jewellery back so she can conduct her daughter’s marriage who is threatened with rape; the woman beaten by her father and mother for entertaining a boy at home. All the women in the film are under siege.


 


Yet these women, through, and perhaps because, of their oppression, identify with other figures claiming the placeholder woman. It is a precarious claim, to a very precarious position and the women see the utter bravery and the sheer madness of it. It is what they have themselves.


 


There is a very interesting verbal Freudian slip of the tongue in the film where the word the lover wants to use for women is ‘acceptance’ but he instead says the ‘arrogance’ of women. He is immediately corrected but the word is actually appropriate because Subbaraj actually believes women are arrogant, and should be arrogant, about their values of empathy, warmth, love, acceptance, anti-casteism, anti- marginalisation of any kind, anti-violence and anti-murder, even when murder seems so powerfully called for (as in a key moment in the film, and the ability to love the unlovable i.e. men.


 


Of course, the lover is using the word for the protagonist, who is not a woman but she identifies as one. She is one of the many figures that constitute the figure woman in the film and in the world. She …

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: First Person | Losing a home
content:
Screenshot from Baterno's footage.

Losing CMFR feels a lot like losing a home.

I’ve seen many posts about the closure of the Center for Media Freedom and Responsibility (CMFR), and what it means to Philippine journalism.

But to me, it is deeply personal.

Losing CMFR feels a lot like losing a home.

For over 13 years, the center has been the foundation of everything I’ve built in my career. I joined CMFR simply wanting a job experience that would look good on my resume. Never intended to stay because, as a young adult from the Visayas, the goal was to eventually go mainstream.

But a rocky love-hate relationship with my superior during my early years at the organization challenged me to prove my worth as a staff writer. What started as a constant need to prove myself turned into a genuine appreciation for the work and a deeper understanding of why it mattered.

Before I even realized it, I had become deeply involved in its advocacy — tracking threats and attacks against journalists, assessing news reports on various issues, and conducting comprehensive research on media coverage.

CMFR opened doors for me to travel across the Philippines and the world, expand my network, and meet incredible people. But most importantly, it gave me a space to discover stories that I would often draw inspiration from for my own creative side hustles.

Over the years, I built relationships with my colleagues and my bosses. Work no longer felt like work. The office had become a home, and the staff had become my family.

When people ask me how I feel about the closure, I tell them I’m fine. I already knew months prior, so I had time to process everything.

Imagine waking up one morning and realizing you are no longer doing the work that defined your life for more than a decade. It’s the abrupt end of a 13-year relationship, and it’s going to take time to truly move on.

There is nothing I can do about its folding. CMFR tried, and I’d like to believe we — especially our boss, Ma’am Melinda Quintos De Jesus — did everything we could to keep it going.

To many, CMFR may be viewed as a lesson learned or a valued organization that should have lasted, but unfortunately didn’t. But to me, it will always be a home I am forever grateful to have been a part of.

So here’s to the memories, the lessons, the people, the stories, and the years that CMFR gave me.

Closing this chapter with a bittersweet “cheers” to that home.

title: Edukasyon sa kuko ng komersyalisasyon
content:
Sa mga pamantasang dapat sana’y pugad ng mapagpalayang kamalayan, lalong sinisiil ang mga kabataang estudyante sa kasalukuyang kalagayan ng pagkakait sa sa edukasyon bilang batayang karapatan at sa halip ay garapalang inilalako bilang kalakal.

Sa kaibuturan, iisa ang bumubuhay sa krisis na ito: ang marahas na komersyalisasyon at neoliberal na reistruktura ng edukasyon. Sa walang-patumanggang pagyakap sa mga Kanluraning modelo, ganap na isinubasta ang silid-aralan sa interes ng pandaigdigang merkado.

Nababawasan ang diin sa paghubog sa mag-aaral bilang kritikal na tagasuri ng lipunan. Sa halip, unti-unti silang itinutulak upang umakma sa merkado bilang tagakonsumo at nakareserbang lakas-paggawa para sa umiiral na sistema. Ramdam ito sa patung-patong na bayarin, kakapusan sa mga pasilidad, at sa unti-unting pagliit ng mga demokratikong espasyo sa loob ng mga kampus.

Ayon sa Artikulo 14, Seksyon 5 ng ating Saligang Batas, malinaw na dapat itakda ang “pinakamataas na prayoridad sa badyet” para sa edukasyon. Ngunit sa kabila nito, patuloy namang kinakaltasan ang pondo para sa mga pampublikong pamantasan, partikular sa mga State Universities and Colleges (SUCs).

Sa panukalang ₱7.2 trilyong 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP), naglaan ang Department of Budget and Management (DBM) ng ₱141.09 bilyong alokasyon para sa mga SUCs sa buong bansa.

Gayunpaman, hindi ramdam ng mayorya ang sinasabing dagdag-pondo. Ayon sa 2027 NEP, 43.46% o 49 sa 113 SUCs ang nakatakdang makatanggap ng mas mababang budget.

Sa Kamaynilaan, nangunguna sa listahan ng may pinakamalaking panukalang budget cut ang University of the Philippines (UP) System na umabot sa ₱2.95 bilyon. Kabilang din sa may malaking bawas ang Philippine Normal University (PNU) na nasa ₱394.9 milyon at ₱291.8 milyon sa Polytechnic University of the Philippines (PUP).

Sa UP Manila, classroom shortage ang pangunahing problema ng mga estudyante.

“Danas na danas naming mga estudyante ang kakulangan sa espasyo kung saan may mga ilang klase, online na lang dahil walang classroom. Sa course namin ay apat na baitang ang naghahati-hati sa iisang classroom. Bukod dito, nahihirapan rin kami mag-organize ng event na magpapaigting sana sa aming mga kampanya hindi lamang dahil sa burukrasya bagkus pati na rin wala talagang espasyo para pagganapan nito, sabi ni Patricia Jutie, Chairperson ng College of Public Health Student council.

Bukod sa kakulangan sa espasyo, tampok din sa ilalim ng administrasyong Marcos Jr. ang usapin ng malawakang korupsyon at maanomalyang paggastos ng pamahalaan hinggil sa flood control at iba pang infrastructure projects.Isa rito ang renovation ng Rizal Hall ng College of Arts and Sciences sa UP Manila, na ipinagawa ng Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) sa St. Timothy Construction Corporation, isang kumpanyang konektado sa mag-asawang Discaya. Hindi natapos ng contractor ang naturang proyekto.

Sa ilalim ng administrasyong Marcos Jr., nananatiling malaking bahagi ng pambansang paggasta ang inilaan sa imprastraktura. Para sa 2027, itinutulak naman ng administrasyon ang ₱643.95 bilyon para sa DPWH, ₱113.05 bilyon o 21.29% na mas mataas kaysa sa 2026 GAA.

“Kung titingnan natin ang UP Manila, kasama rin sa budget nito ang Philippine General Hospital (PGH). Hindi lang siya isyu ng mga estudyante; issue siya ng mamamayan. Sino ba ang mga nakikinabang sa ating hospital? Mga mamamayan natin na nangangailangan ng mapagkalingang health care system sa bansa,” saad naman ni Kabataan Partylist UPM chairperson Querobin Acsibar.

Espasyo rin ang usapin sa Philippine Normal University (PNU) at Polytechnic University of the Philippines (PUP).

“Sa loob ng pamantasan, maraming isyung kinakaharap ang mga estudyante. Isa lang po dito ang kakulangan sa espasyo, hindi matapos-tapos na imprastraktura, at lahat ng ito ay lumulundo sa kakulangan sa budget sa edukasyon,” ani Adleann Biol, Vice Chairperson ng PNU USC-Central Student Council.

“Sa kasalukuyan, mahigit 100,000 na iskolar ng bayan ang hindi nakapasok sa PUP dahil sa kabaratan ng budget sa pamantasan. Dagdag dito, ang North Wing na mahigit apat na taon ng tinatry na i-build, yung aming main academic building kung saan nakakaranas ang mga estudyante ng kakulangan sa student spaces at academic organization spaces na labis na pinapanawagan ng mga kabataan noon pa man hanggang ngayon,” ani Michael Dave Bolima, Secretary General ng PUP Sentral na Konseho ng Mag-aaral.

author: Danica Rachel
title: Protest called against October arms fair in Perth
content:
The Land Forces Exposition 2026, to be held at the Perth Convention and Exhibition Centre on 6-8 October, will be a three-day extravaganza of exhibitions, talks and luncheons, where the main topic of conversation is how best to kill people. More than 20,000 weapons company executives, politicians and military personnel from around the world are expected to attend.

We have to protest against this outrageous celebration of death and destruction.

Photos from the 2024 event on the front page of the

Land Forces website

 are enough to make you ill. A smiling representative of Anduril, a company specialising in AI-powered warfare, shows off a battle drone. A live demonstration of a robot dog, presumably designed to carry autonomous weapons, takes place on the exhibition floor. A drone as big as a car hangs from the ceiling.

Lockheed Martin, the world’s biggest arms dealer—and builder of the F-35 fighter jets Israel uses to bomb Gaza—will have its latest death machines on display. As will Elbit Systems, Israel’s biggest weapons company.

Senior executives from Anduril and BAE Systems will speak on a panel discussing “the realities of Ukraine, Iran and other current conflicts”. Today’s bloodshed used as a case study to make tomorrow’s killing more efficient. What could those “other conflicts” be? Israel’s invasion of Lebanon? One assumes that there’s much these monsters have learned from Gaza, too.

Lockheed Martin and BAE will be joined by Babcock, Boeing, Honeywell, Northrop Grumman and Thales. Aside from all having had significant roles in providing Israel’s weapons for use in Gaza, they are all on the exclusive list of companies involved in creating nuclear weapons.

The list goes on, and on, and on. More than 650 companies will have exhibits on the floor, all of them dealing in weapons, military hardware or AI systems for warfare.

To say the state Labor government is rolling out the red carpet for this smorgasbord of warmongers would be an understatement. It is going above and beyond to keep conference-goers comfortable by pouring $11.5 million into security.

Special legislation gives police the power to set up checkpoints, stop and search anyone for any reason, and ban anyone they like from a significant section of Perth’s CBD, including a major train and bus station, for ten days surrounding the event.

Police Minister Reece Whitby said of the laws: “We saw the scenes that occurred when Land Forces was held in Melbourne in 2024, and we do not want to see anything like that here in Perth”. Whitby was referring to the

protest by 1,500 people

 against the last iteration of this festival of death.

None of this—the war profiteering, the authoritarian police powers, the increased drive towards a world of total war—should pass without protest.

So a coalition of anti-war and Palestine solidarity organisations has called a demonstration against Land Forces on 6 October, 5pm, at Yagan Square in the Perth CBD. We need as many people as possible to make it clear that we reject Land Forces and everything it represents.

author: AWSM
title: Why I Won’t Vote ~ A SYMPOSIUM #1
content:
Anarchy 37, March 1964, Why I Won’t Vote

Voting : “The instrument and symbol of a freeman’s power to make a fool of himself and a wreck of his country”

The saying that ” only a fool would put a loaded gun into the hands of an idiot ” is an especially apt analogy of government. An idiot (usually well-meaning) considers himself clever enough to run the affairs of a large number of people by taking a seat in parliament. A large number of people, acting like fools, vote for his party’s policy then spend the next few years grumbling about the results. The error in approach is that the voter thinks that he will get what he voted for. If he could vote for those who in fact control the country, say the Governors of the Bank of England, the directors of the industrial corporations and those behind the ministries, the illusion of democracy would be more understandable.

The real centres of power lie far beyond the people’s influence at elections. These remain constant whatever Party is ” in power “. In the terms of centralised ” democracy ” the only possible argument to justify voting is that marginal benefits may be gained. The state only incidentally attends to the well-being of its subjects. Its main concern is its power relation to other states, of which the most perfect expression is in war.

I am on the side of people anywhere who are prepared neither to live nor die for something that in the long run can only militate against survival and the conditions that make life worth living. Our immediate action must, by its nature, be to oppose that pathetic gesture, voting. It must be direct and direction. We can learn to live as free men and women only by organising against the condition we are in.

The Tenants Association, Consumers Association, and Direct Action in industry all provide opportunities for people to experience directing their own lives in positive ways towards positive ends.

Only by direct involvement in society can the individual hope to transform himself and his world. Freedom cannot be given, it must be taken; and the free society can only grow from experiments in the problems (ethical and organisational) of community.

Voting does not, and cannot, mean government by consent. By voting, one acts on the assumptions that certain men are fit to govern, and that a majority is necessarily right. Also should the state, acting in the name of a (frequently fictitious) majority, declare war, the individual loses the right to live, if he ever had it.

To me, voting is complicity with the State and a negative action, therefore I do not vote.

author: James Plested
title: Victorian Socialists’ election campaign in full swing
content:
The Victorian state election will take place in just over two months, on Saturday 28 November. The Victorian Socialists’ campaign is now in full swing, with local campaign activity taking place daily across Melbourne and regional Victoria.

The scale of the campaign—with VS candidates set to run in all 88 lower house seats and all eight upper house regions across Victoria—is beyond anything the socialist left in Australia has attempted for generations (if ever). Even just a few years ago, a statewide campaign like this would have been unthinkable. That it’s happening at all is something of a breakthrough.

Between 1 June and 19 September, VS volunteers knocked on more than 80,000 doors, already well on track to reach the 2022 campaign total of around 190,000. The party received around 2,000 requests for campaign signs to be put on front fences and in yards, eclipsing the 2022 total of 1,000, with hundreds of orders a week still coming in. More than 2,400 people donated to the campaign, and almost 1,800 registered for a party event. 

New branches are springing up everywhere. Wherever they do, we’re finding people who want to get involved. VS events in places like Pakenham, a suburb on the far south-eastern fringe of Melbourne—more than 50 kilometres from the CBD—are attracting many new faces. And we now have active branches in regional centres including Geelong, Warrnambool, Ballarat and Bendigo, and the beginnings of branches in Shepparton, Wodonga and Warragul. 

We’re accustomed to being almost completely overlooked by the mainstream media, but the sheer size of our campaign this time means we’re increasingly difficult to ignore.

ABC News reported

 on the VS campaign launch on 1 August, and Channel 9 reported on our “all-in” Footscray doorknock on Sunday 16 August, which was attended by more than 350 volunteers. VS candidate for the Northern Metro upper house region Omar Hassan has become something of a regular fixture on talkback radio 3AW’s morning show with Tom Elliot—most recently on the topic

“what is socialism?”

VS candidates in the regions are attracting particular attention.

Hera Sheppard,

 in the seat of

South-West Coast

 (comprising Warrnambool, Port Fairy, Portland and surrounds), has been featured in several articles in the

Warrnambool Standard

, including the front cover. An

author: AWSM
title: Errico Malatesta – Vote? What For?
content:
George: This beer’s not too bad, is it?

Jack: Yes, it’s alright, but what a price!

George: Shocking – especially when you remember what things used to cost. Still, you can’t wonder with all these taxes. It costs you twice as much to live as it used to. They put up the price of some things, and say you can do without them. But you can’t do without bread, and food, and clothes – you have to pay the rent all the same, and then there are the taxes on this and the rates – on our wages too! What a life! And it’s our own fault! If we wanted to we could alter things. The working class has the remedy in its own hands.

George: Easy enough! You’ve got a vote?

Jack: What’s that got to do with it?

George: Have you, or haven’t you?

Jack: Well, I’m entitled to a vote – but I never make use of it.

George: There you are! You’ve got a vote, but you just won’t take the trouble to use it, and then you wonder why things are so bad. You deserve all you get, honestly! People like you are responsible for all the trouble in the world!

Jack: Alright, alright, keep your hair on! Just tell me what’s the good of voting?

George: It’s obvious. Who makes the laws? The M.P.’s. Elect good M.P.’s and you get good laws.

Jack: Good councillors and good M.P.’s? We’ve heard that for a long time. But you’d have to be deaf, dumb, and blind not to notice it’s the same stooges that always get in. Oh, it’s wonderful to hear them when they’re after votes at election time. They pat you on the back, ask after the wife and kids, kiss the baby, promise you railways, bridges, work, cheap bread, less taxes, higher wages, protection – absolutely everything! And once they get in, they’re no better than anyone else. Goodbye promises! The wife and kids may starve, there’s no more or less work than before, the whole town can be falling to pieces for all they care. They’ve other things to think about than your troubles! Then a few years later they start the ballyhoo again. It doesn’t matter what colour the party is: they’re all the same. As soon as they’re elected, they forget all about you. They’re in their clubs and at their select dinners, and they don’t even trouble to come and have a look at you until the next election.

George: That’s correct! But why elect the rich? Don’t you know that the rich only live on the work of the masses? So how do you expect them to worry about the masses? All they think of is getting as much out of the ordinary man as they can.

Jack: Now you’re talking! But it’s not only the rich. There’s the other type, who want to get elected so they can become rich.

George: That’s true. So don’t let’s vote for them. Let’s elect workers, experienced friends of ours, as you might say, and then we won’t be fooled.

Jack: Oh, we’ve got some of your “experienced friends” in now, and they’re no different from our acknowledged enemies! Anyhow, what do you mean, “let’s elect – let’s elect.” As if we – you and me – could do as we like!

George: But it’s not only us two. If each one of us tried to convert other people and they would do the same, labour would have a majority, and we could elect whoever we liked. And that’s when we could form a government of the workers, and then . . .

Jack: And then it would be a paradise – I mean for those who were in Parliament! You’re arranging things a bit too quickly! Those in command always have the majority. The rich are always in power. Just imagine a poor worker, perhaps with an ill wife and four hungry kids, and you tell him to risk his job and get thrown out of his house to starve; just to give his vote to a candidate his master doesn’t like. Just try and convince those poor devils who can be thrown out of work by their boss whenever he likes. They’re never free; if they want to be free, they don’t want to waste their time voting – just take what they need.

George: But if we didn’t do that, no-one would vote. We couldn’t go to the workers and ask them to vote for our party, and say at the same time that votes were useless.

Jack: That’s just it! And on top of that you have to make election promises you know you can’t keep. And then you have to stand in with the Government, and mix with the well-to-do, and all the rest of it. As soon as any of your men are elected they have to kow-tow to the people you admit are the opponents of the workers. So why the hell talk about propaganda when the first thing you do is to counteract propaganda?

George: But you must admit, it’s an advantage to have our own men with …

author: Tom Bramble
title: What’s the deal with productivity?
content:
The bosses are trying to convince workers that lower corporate taxes, fewer regulations and workers’ rights, and less union power would be good for real wages. What they really want is more profits at the expense of the working class.

For years, business lobby groups have decried what they call Australia’s “productivity crisis”. They don’t say workers are producing less than they used to; they say they aren’t increasing production as quickly as before and aren’t keeping pace with overseas productivity growth.

It’s true: growth in workers’ hourly output has slowed over the past decade, and Australian workers don’t produce as much value for the bosses as American workers. But the bosses argue that this means living standards are held back, and prices rise more than they otherwise would, contributing to the cost-of-living crisis.

They say that government regulations (rules about wages, hours of work, health and safety standards, construction standards, environmental protections and professional and occupational registration requirements) and trade unions are preventing business investment. Their solution is “deregulation”, “slashing red tape”, “more competition”. These are simply code words for attacking the working class.

Let’s break this down. First, what is productivity? The simplest definition is “output per hour”. For BlueScope Steel, it could be tonnes of steel produced per hour per worker. For a childcare centre operator, it could be the number of children in care per worker per day. Lift those and productivity rises.

But who benefits? Does the steel worker or childcare worker see their wage rise automatically if they get more done? Of course not. In the first instance, all the money made from extra production by every group of workers goes to the capitalists, not the workers. Workers’ standard of living depends on how much they fight for. And that applies across the whole economy.

The bosses say some of the additional money coming in from workers’ extra effort will come back through higher wages and maybe more jobs. They argue: “a rising tide lifts all boats”. Is that true, though?

First, productivity in Australia may have slowed in the past couple of decades, but it has still risen. Yet household living standards are no higher than they were in 2012. There is no indication that workers are seeing any of the higher value they produce in the form of higher real wages.

A starker example is the United States, which bosses always point to as the high-productivity benchmark, where output per worker is higher and rising faster. In that country, workers’ share of national income is now at its lowest since World War Two—the productivity gains have gone to the capitalists, who have grown ever wealthier at workers’ expense.

Take things down another level. Even if bosses shared a cut of the higher revenue from increased productivity with workers, or unions successfully struck to extract a higher wage, bosses would still be ripping off workers.

All wealth ultimately comes either from the world’s natural resources or from human labour. You only have to see what happens when workers go on strike to see the truth of this—nothing gets produced, not a wheel turns, the childcare centres lie empty. All the machinery, all the factories, all the railway lines can only be put to good use if workers labour on them. And these in turn are the product of previous generations of workers’ labour.

What the capitalists call productivity should really be called exploitation: the extraction of value from the worker over and above the cost of their reproduction, i.e. what is necessary to get them to come to work each day in the form of wages. They call it profit; in fact, it’s theft from the worker.

This theft lies at the heart of capitalism. It explains why the workers labour their whole lives and have not much more than their home to hand on to their kids, and often not even that. While their employer has significantly expanded their operations at the workers’ expense. Some of the bosses may blow the money on a more self-indulgent lifestyle, but personal greed doesn’t get to the heart of it.

Every boss is driven to extract more from their workers, i.e. to lift productivity, because if they don’t, their rivals will, and they will be undercut and go out of business. The winner is the boss who can exploit their workers the most. That’s why every boss in every country demands that governments make it easier for them to rip off their …

author: Emma Black
title: Strangulation: How did attempted murder become normal?
content:
A 16-year-old woman from Sydney’s northern beaches died in hospital in late August after reportedly being strangled during consensual sex with her partner. The tragedy has sparked a long-overdue reckoning with the consequences for young women of the pornification of sex and the normalisation of sexual violence that has come with it.

In recent years, sexual strangulation has gone from being a relatively marginal phenomenon to an everyday sexual practice. In Australia, 61 percent of young women report having been strangled during sex, according to a

2024 survey

 of thousands of 18- to 35-year-olds. Men are most likely to be the stranglers. There is no safe way to strangle someone. According to David Corlett and Marie Crabbe, founders of anti-strangulation advocacy group Breathless:

“Potential 

consequences

 [of strangulation]

range from

 neck pain to loss of bladder and bowel control, headaches, memory loss, seizures, brain damage, stroke and, as seems to be the case with the young woman from the northern beaches, death. The risks and consequences are cumulative, so the more someone is strangled, the more likely they are to suffer harm.”

Only a tiny percentage of middle-aged and older adults have engaged in sexual strangulation, but among young people it’s become commonplace. Maree Crabbe, who is also the director of

It’s Time We Talked

, says strangulation wasn’t an issue before about 2019. But things have changed dramatically since then. “In recent years, we’ve been hearing it’s become normal for young people of all backgrounds, socioeconomic groups, cultures, sexual orientations”, she recently told the

Sydney Morning Herald

.

So how did a potentially deadly act become a normal sexual practice?

The main driver is pornography.

Recent research

 found more than 60 percent of 18- to 35-year-olds had encountered sexual strangulation depicted in pornography. One study comparing the content in the most popular pornography across the two and a half decades to 2024 found that sexual strangulation has gone from almost non-existent to featuring in 15 percent of scenes.

Pornography has become the de facto sex education system for millions of young people. And strangulation is just the latest trend in an industry that maximises profits by selling more extreme depictions of violent and degrading treatment of women.

A landmark 2010 study of best-selling pornographic videos, published in the journal

Violence Against Women

, found that 88 percent contained physical aggression, while 49 percent of scenes contained verbal aggression. Perpetrators were usually male, whereas targets were overwhelmingly female. Targets most often showed pleasure or responded neutrally to the aggression.

So the vast majority of mainstream pornography, whether it depicts strangulation or not, reinforces the idea that violence and humiliation are not only permissible, but pleasurable for women. The pornography industry has “blood on its hands” for propagating this sort of violent content, according to Chanel Contos, founder of

Teach Us Consent

.

An example of how normalised strangulation during sex has become came from this year’s Eurovision song contest.

Romania’s 2026 song entry

 “Choke Me” repeats the words “choke me” 30 times in three minutes. The song also contains the lyrics “It’s hard to breathe in” and “make my lungs explode”.

Many mainstream commentators

emphasise

 the importance of avoiding “kink-shaming” when addressing the issue of sexual strangulation with young people. This dresses up the prioritisation of men’s sexual gratification over women’s safety as sex-positive open-mindedness. And it wilfully ignores the fact that sexual desires and practices are not simply a matter of individual preference; they are shaped and constructed in a society where women are not equal to men, and enormous profit can be made from sex by companies competing for market share.

The reality is that people’s sexual inclinations have not radically changed on their own over the last 50 years, such that the majority of men now enjoy inflicting harm on women. Market forces have pushed things in this direction. In an attempt to be more sensational and attract market share, pornography companies have taken the male-dominant trope that underpins the construction of mainstream heterosexuality and pumped it up to a new extreme. This has shaped attitudes to sex and sexual desire, which in turn further reinforces the business model. And …

author: Mag
title: Nicht nur Hessen: Polizei überprüft psychisch erkrankte Menschen – auf dem Weg zum „Register für psychisch kranke Gewalttäter“?
content:
Dossier


„

Die hessische Polizei geht systematisch alle Personen in ihren Datenbanken durch, bei denen sie einen Hinweis auf eine „Psychische und Verhaltensstörung“ gespeichert hat. Damit will sie Risiken für Gewalttaten erkennen und etwa Gefährderansprachen oder Überwachung planen. Um Betroffene zu unterstützen, bräuchte es andere Maßnahmen.

„Psychisch Auffällige, Vielschreiber, Gewalttäter“ lautet der Name einer Taskforce, die es seit Februar 2025 beim hessischen Landeskriminalamt gibt. (…) Einen PSYV-Vermerk gibt es aktuell zu rund 1.600 Menschen in Hessen, schreibt das dortige Innenministerium auf Anfrage. (…) Laut Robert-Koch-Institut erhielten im Jahr 2023 40,4 Prozent der Erwachsenen in Deutschland eine Diagnose für eine psychische Störung

…“ Aus dem

Beitrag von Anna Biselli vom 08.07.2025 in Netzpolitik


 („Hessen: Polizei überprüft 1.600 psychisch erkrankte Menschen“ mit weiteren Infos zu geplanten Stigmatisierungen – siehe mehr dazu wie auch beginnende Proteste in immer mehr Bundesländern:


Erneuertes Psychisch-Kranken-Gesetz in NRW soll nicht nur der Polizei, auch der  Ausländerbehörde Informationen über Klinikeinweisungen von Geflüchteten liefern


„

Ein neues Gesetz in Nordrhein-Westfalen soll nicht nur der Polizei mehr Informationen über Menschen liefern, die in eine Klinik eingewiesen wurden. Auch die Ausländerbehörden sollen mehr über Geflüchtete in Psychiatrien erfahren – damit sie Abschiebungen besser planen können.


Nordrhein-Westfalen will sein Psychisch-Kranken-Gesetz (PsychKG) erneuern. Darin geht es zum einen darum, wann Menschen unfreiwillig in eine psychiatrische Klinik eingewiesen werden können. Zum anderen aber auch um Hilfsangebote und Unterstützung für Menschen mit einer psychischen Erkrankung. Das ist in Deutschland auf Ebene der Bundesländer geregelt.


In NRW wie in anderen Bundesländern steht allerdings noch ein anderes Thema im Mittelpunkt der Diskussionen: der Austausch von Daten über Menschen, die in eine Klinik eingewiesen werden. Insbesondere dann, wenn die Einweisung wegen einer festgestellten Fremdgefährdung erfolgte, also weil die Sorge besteht, dass eine Person aufgrund ihres Zustands anderen gefährlich werden könnte. Und in NRW geht es auch um Abschiebungen.


Am Donnerstag sprachen im Gesundheitsausschuss des Landtags Sachverständige über den Gesetzentwurf. Zahlreiche Stellungnahmen von Kliniken, sozialpsychiatrischen Diensten, Verbänden und Betroffenen äußerten Sorgen.


Eine Klinikeinweisung ist keine Strafmaßnahme


„Hier bekommt die Polizeibehörde in medizinisch psychiatrischen Zusammenhängen ein erweitertes Mitentscheidungsrecht über den Datenfluss bis hin zur Entlassung“, schreibt etwa die Freie Wohlfahrtspflege NRW. Sie ist eine Arbeitsgemeinschaft, der unter anderem das Rote Kreuz, die Caritas und die Arbeiterwohlfahrt angehören. Eine Klinik-Unterbringung nach dem PsychKG sei „keine strafrechtliche Maßnahme“. Die Kritik der Freien Wohlfahrtspflege bezieht sich auf eine neue Regelung, wer bei der Entlassung einer zuvor zwangseingewiesenen Person von den Kliniken informiert werden muss. Neben Vertrauenspersonen oder dem sozialpsychiatrischen Dienst soll künftig in bestimmten Fällen auch die örtliche Polizei in Kenntnis gesetzt werden. (…)


Dass im Gesetz überhaupt der Eindruck erweckt wird, man müsse psychisch Erkrankten mit Gefahrenabwehrmaßnahmen begegnen, darin sehen viele Fachleute ein Problem. Das bediene, so die Freie Wohlfahrtspflege NRW, „das Narrativ der ‚gefährlichen psychisch kranken Gewalttäter’. Eine psychische Erkrankung und Gewalttaten stehen jedoch nur in einem geringen Umfang in einem direkten Zusammenhang.“ (…)


Die Ausländerbehörde soll immer wissen, wo eine geflüchtete Person sich aufhält, damit sie sie jederzeit abschieben kann. Fachleute sind empört.


Psychiatrische Kliniken sollten „nicht zu Orten werden, von denen aus regelmäßig Abschiebungen erfolgen“, schreibt dazu die Aktion Psychisch Kranke. „Die Krankenhäuser sollten geschützte Räume bleiben“, heißt es in der Stellungnahme des Vereins, in dem sich Bundestagsabgeordnete und Fachleute aus der psychiatrischen Versorgung zusammengeschlossen haben. (…)


Ärzt:innen sind keine Abschiebehelfer


Abschiebungen aus Krankenhäusern passieren schon heute. Bei einem Abschiebeflug nach Afghanistan im Juli 2025 waren mindestens drei der 81 Betroffenen unmittelbar davor in einer psychiatrischen Klinik. Anfang 2025 holte die Polizei einen suizidalen Geflüchteten aus einer Klinik in Osnabrück …

author: CNT Iruña
title: Informe de la situación del sector del metal en Navarra
content:
A lo largo del verano de 2026, CNT Iruñea ha realizado una encuesta anónima para conocer la situación laboral y las principales preocupaciones y problemas de las personas que trabajan en el sector del metal en Navarra.


El sector del metal representa aproximadamente la mitad del tejido industrial en Navarra y su convenio regula las condiciones laborales de más de 30.000 personas asalariadas. Por esta razón, es uno de los sectores que más consultas genera dentro de las asesorías laborales del sindicato.


Temporalidad e inestabilidad


La temporalidad, los contratos fijos discontinuos y la subcontratación continúan siendo importantes problemas en el sector

, los cuales generan una fuerte sensación de inseguridad e inestabilidad entre las plantillas.


Durante años, ha sido una práctica habitual el abuso de la contratación temporal por parte de las empresas del metal. Si bien la reforma laboral de 2021 puso nuevos límites a esta forma de contratación, ésta fue insuficiente para terminar con la precariedad, disponiendo los empresarios de otras fórmulas como el contrato fijo-discontinuo además de conservarse las baratas indemnizaciones por despido que estableció la reforma laboral de 2012.


Aun más, el vergonzoso acuerdo realizado entre la patronal del metal, CC.OO. y UGT ha abierto las puertas para que, durante 2026, las empresas navarras puedan llegar a ampliar los contratos temporales por circunstancias de la producción de 6 a 12 meses.


Salarios


En 2022, la patronal del metal se congratulaba por haber negociado un convenio para Navarra con los incrementos salariales desvinculados del IPC. CC.OO. y UGT, sindicatos firmantes de dicho convenio, se justificaban señalándolo como uno de los mejores del estado en materia salarial. La realidad que vive la clase trabajadora en esta comunidad se encuentra atravesada por el constante aumento del coste de la vida así como por la dificultad cada vez mayor en el acceso a la vivienda, una pérdida de poder adquisitivo a la cual se le une el deterioro de los servicios públicos.

No es de extrañar

, pues,

la alarmante cantidad de personas encuestadas que indican llegar con grandes dificultades a final de mes o, incluso, no llegar en absoluto

.


Destaca también, a su vez, el número de trabajadores que nos señalan que su categoría profesional no se corresponde con las funciones realizadas, práctica ésta extendida dentro del sector con la intención de rebajar salarios.


Jornada


Otra de las cuestiones por las que se alegró la patronal del metal tras la firma del actual convenio fue la de mantener la reducción de la jornada laboral fuera del debate, continuando no sólo con la gran “flexibilidad” que permitía el anterior convenio a las empresas, sino facilitándolo aún más si cabe. Bajo el eufemismo de flexibilidad, se esconde uno de los principales intereses de los empresarios del sector: disponer del tiempo vital de sus trabajadores en el máximo grado posible.


De esta forma, una cantidad importante de las personas encuestadas nos indica que su empresa aplica habitualmente la bolsa de horas o las horas del acuerdo para la competitividad,

siendo para CNT especialmente preocupante la cantidad de personas que han manifestado su total desconocimiento sobre esta cuestión o sobre el convenio en líneas generales, situación que les coloca en una situación de fuerte vulnerabilidad frente a los empresarios

.


Cuestiones como la dificultad para la conciliación laboral, el insuficiente tiempo de descanso durante la jornada y la no consideración de éste como tiempo de trabajo efectivo, el desacuerdo con el calendario laboral o las presiones para realizar horas extras también se reflejan en los resultados de la encuesta como importantes inquietudes.


Salud Laboral


Navarra, año tras año, se encuentra a la cabeza del Estado español en accidentes laborales

 con la industria en general, y el metal en concreto, como unos de los sectores más preocupantes. Aunque las empresas del sector suelen ofrecer una formación obligatoria sobre seguridad laboral a sus plantillas, es destacable el número de personas encuestadas que la consideran insuficiente o que no se corresponde con el modo de trabajar en el día a día de la empresa. También el de quienes sufren estrés o sobrecarga laboral, el de quienes consideran que no trabajan en unas condiciones laborales seguras y el de quienes piensan que, aunque su empresa cumpla con la normativa, existen riesgos para su salud.
