title: Antiimperialistische Aktionswoche 7. - 11. Oktober
content:
Aufruf zur Antiimperialistischen Aktionswoche


💥Vor fast einem Jahr sind in Bern tausende Menschen zusammengekommen, um ein Ende des Genozids in Gaza und ein freies Palästina zu fordern. Und die Schweizer Kompliz*innenschaft dabei zu konfrontieren. Der Widerstand auf den Strassen Berns war kräftig und gebündelt. Verständlich, nachdem wir in Lausanne, Genf, Basel, Zürich, Lugano, Bern und so vielen anderen Orten verschiedene Unis besetzt und bereits unzählige Demos und andere Aktionen organisiert hatten, die ungehört blieben. Während der Genozid weiterhin geläugnet wurde. Unsere Wut über den Genozid in Gaza, die Kolonisierung Palästinas und den Imperialismus liess entsprechend die Strassen beben und verschlug dem Staat die Sprache. Er hatte keine andere Wahl, als sein wahres Gesicht zu zeigen und zu versuchen unseren Widerstand gewaltsam im Keim zu ersticken. Er hatte keine andere Wahl, als am Rattenschwanz zu ziehen, der der Öffentlichkeit als Verschärfungen der Repressionsmassnahmen und der Roadmap für nationale Sicherheit präsentiert wird.


👉Ob in Lugano, Genf, Lausanne, Bern, Zürich oder Basel: Überall spüren wir die Gewalt des Schweizer Staats. Er beschützt mit Schlagstock und Gummischrott auf Ausbeutung beruhendes System. Er beschützt - indem er unseren Aufstand unterdrückt - die Interessen der Grosskonzerne, welche Rekordprofite am Krieg, am Genozid und der Vernichtung unseres Planeten und dem Leben von hundertausenden von Menschen erzielen.


❤️‍🔥Doch wir lassen uns davon nicht einschüttern und bilden weiterhin überregional Banden! Wir lassen uns nicht beeindrucken von ihrer Propagandamaschinerie, wir lassen uns nicht beeindrucken von Bullen, Geheimdienst und sonstigen Taugenichtsen. Wir lassen uns im Gegenteil vom unbeugsamen Widerstand gegen die koloniale Kontinuität und den Imperialismus beeindrucken. Und darum rufen wir auf zur Antiimperialistischen Aktionswoche:

Vom 7.10. - 11.10.2026, vom Mittwoch bis zur grossen Demo am Sonntag.


✊Wir richten uns mit diesem Aufruf an alle Gruppen, Kollektive, Netzwerke, Einzelpersonen und Organisationen überall in und ausserhalb der Schweiz! Wir richten uns an all jene, die so unglaublich wütend sind, wie wir. Die wütend sind auf den Zustand dieser Welt. Lasst uns kreativ werden, organisieren wir Workshops, Filmevents, Theater oder Vorträge zu Austerität, Repression, Militarismus, Genozid, Zionismus, Klimakrise oder Imperialismus und vieles mehr, um der westlichen Propagandamaschinerie die Stirn zu bieten. Denn entgegen der Aussagen von Alec von Graffenried, sind wir weder ein Sauhaufen noch herrscht in Gaza Frieden! Lassen wir die Fassade der heilen und ach so gutmütigen Schweiz weiter bröckeln.


🇵🇸Lasst uns kreativ, bunt, laut und kämpferisch sein.

author: Ruby Healer
title: Labor doubles down on US military alliance
content:
“American force posture in Australia is growing”, Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles declared on his visit to Washington, DC, this month. “Since we’ve come to government”, Marles said, standing alongside US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, “you can see a through line there of growing American force posture in Australia”.

It was a fairly straightforward summary of the Albanese Labor government’s attitude, followed up with promises of further integration between the Australian and US militaries. A shifting “force posture” will mean more American troop rotations, more US air and naval operations and more pre-positioning of military equipment like warplanes, fuel and munitions in Australia.

Agreements made by the Albanese government will ramp up co-operation on all fronts, with a newly

revitalised

 HMAS Stirling base near Perth set to host American nuclear-powered submarines and an estimated 2,300 US troops within five years. As America’s military machine looks ahead to an era of aggressive contest with China in the Asia-Pacific, Australia’s ruling class is desperate to make itself an indispensable part of US war planning.

Weapons trade regulations have also been

loosened

 under a bilateral agreement to help both countries access shared research to develop arms and surveillance systems. And, Marles promised ominously, “you will hear more from us ... in the coming months” about further arrangements to increase co-operation.

Of course, there’s nothing new about the Australian ruling class throwing itself into a military alliance with the United States. This is a long-standing arrangement pursued by every Australian government since the Second World War. Permanent joint intelligence and communications programs have run out of Pine Gap in the Northern Territory and the Harold Holt naval station in Western Australia since the 1960s.

Data

published

 by the

Guardian

 in early September revealed that American forces and weapons corporations control or make use of over 100 military facilities across the country. And Australia is one of the biggest recipients of US arms in the world, with around 85 percent of weapons purchased in 2021-25 coming from the US,

according

 to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute’s arms transfers database.

Hegseth himself

recalled

 during a separate love-in event with Marles last year: “We [the Australian and US militaries] fought shoulder to shoulder in every major conflict since World War One—from the Western Front, to Guadalcanal, to Vietnam, to Afghanistan”.

“During my time in Afghanistan”, he reminisced, “I served with members of the Australian military who were some of the finest”. We can only imagine the sorts of unconvicted war criminals who consorted with Pete Hegseth during the joint twenty-year occupation of Afghanistan.

The US alliance has long been a pillar of Australia’s foreign policy, but the current Labor government seems particularly eager to grovel to America. Just one month after Donald Trump’s inauguration, and before the current Australian and US defence ministers had even met for the first time, the Australian government arranged a

payment

 of US$500 million towards the Trump administration’s military budget.

“We’re really pleased that the first payment ... we’ve been able to make in the first couple of weeks of the Trump administration”, Marles told Hegseth ahead of their first formal meeting in February 2025. “We’re really pleased to make it in the first week of your tenure as the secretary of defence.”

In the meeting that followed, Marles

explained

 that Hegseth’s enthusiasm for military ties with Australia made sense, since “the whole idea of a free and open Indo-Pacific really has its origins during the first Trump Administration”.

You wouldn’t be wrong to interpret this behaviour as pathetic bootlicking. The Australian government is a simpering bunch of pro-American lowlifes. But the problem isn’t that our leaders are “weak” or being strong-armed into subservience. They run the twelfth largest economy in the world. Their armed forces outstrip those of any oceanic neighbours by a wide margin. The reality is that Australian capitalism is a willing and culpable participant in the world’s most powerful military coalition alongside America.

As former Labor Prime Minister Kevin Rudd recently

stated

, the “alliance with the United States remains a force multiplier for Australia’s defence needs”. With the help of its powerful …

title: Türkiye-Yunanistan gerilimi: Sadece bir sınır sorunu değil emperyalist planda yer kapma meselesi
content:
Seyit Aldoğan [email protected]

Atina- Son dönemde Ortadoğu, Doğu Akdeniz, Ege ve İran ekseninde gelişen ABD-İsrail savaşının yaygınlaşma eğilimi, bir anlamda Türk-Yunan ilişkilerini de tetikledi. Bu durum Türkiye basınında “Atina’da deprem”, “Atina gerilim istiyor”, “Yunanistan ve İsrail ablukası” benzeri manşetlerin atılmasına neden oldu. Karşılıklı restleşmeler, uyarılar ve milliyetçi söylemlerle düşmanlığı körükleyen değerlendirmeler havada uçuşuyor.

Dünyada emperyalist rekabetin kızışmasına, pazar paylaşımı mücadelesine ve emperyalist savaşların yaygınlaşma eğilimi içine girmesine paralel olarak, üzerinde yaşadığımız coğrafyada da enerji nakil hatları, hidrokarbon rezervleri ve deniz taşımacılığı gibi etkenlere bağlı olarak Türkiye-Yunanistan ilişkilerinde yeni bir gerginliğe doğru gidildiği görülüyor.

ABD ve onun bölgedeki vurucu gücü olan İsrail yeni bir yapılanmayı hedeflerken, bölgedeki gerici yönetimler pastadan pay kapmak, emperyalist sistemin bir parçası olarak varlıklarını sürdürmeyi güvence altına almak ve bölgesel çıkar dengeleri içinde daha iyi bir mevzi tutmak amacıyla dış politika, ticaret, silahlanma ve ittifaklarda yeni yönelimler içine giriyorlar. Bölge gericiliklerinin çıkarlarının farklılıklar göstermesi emperyalizme bağımlılıkla çelişmediği gibi, tersine bu bağımlılığı daha da güçlendiren birer etmen haline geliyor.

Bölgedeki gelişmelere bu perspektifle bakıldığında Türkiye ve Yunanistan arasında anlaşmazlık konusu olan sorunların klasik anlamda bir sınır sorunu olmaktan çıktığı açıkça görülecektir.

Rusya Karadeniz, Balkanlar ve Doğu Avrupa’dan abluka altına alınıyor. Yunan adalarına hava savunma sistemlerinin yerleştirilerek Ege kontrol altına alınmaya çalışılıyor. Doğu Trakya ABD-NATO üssüne çevriliyor. Öte yandan Doğu Akdeniz’de İsrail, Güney Kıbrıs ve Yunanistan arasında enerji nakil anlaşmasının yürürlüğe girmesi, Yunanistan’ın münhasır ekonomik bölge çerçevesi içinde uluslararası tekellerle yaptığı anlaşmalar, enerji rezervlerinin önemi, Ortadoğu’ya müdahalede bölgenin önem kazanması, Çin ve Rusya ile girişilen rekabet vb. gelişmeler Türkiye ile Yunanistan arasındaki sorunların artık klasik anlaşmazlıklar olmaktan çıktığını gösteriyor. Gelişmeler, Ege ve Doğu Akdeniz’i emperyalist yayılmacılık, paylaşım ve egemenlik rekabetinin açıkça görüldüğü alan durumuna getiriyor.

Yunanistan’da 1973 yılında yıkılan Albaylar Cuntası sonrasından bugüne kadar kurulan en işbirlikçi yönetim olan Kiryakos Miçotakis’nin Yeni Demokrasi (ND) hükümeti, Ege’de ve Doğu Akdeniz’de Yunan sermayesinin çıkarları doğrultusunda başta ABD, İsrail ve sonrasında AB ile, son derece stratejik anlaşmalar yapmış bulunuyor. Mısır, Lübnan, BAE, Suudi Arabistan ile askeri ve ticari ve teknik ilişkiler geliştirdi. Bu arada özellikle Fransız ve Alman tekellerinin çıkarlarının sözcülüğünü de yapıyor.

Erdoğan hükümeti ise ABD ve AB destekli İsrail, Yunanistan ve Güney Kıbrıs kesimi eksenine karşı Suriye’de sahip olduğu etkiyi, son süreçte Pakistan ve Suudi Arabistan ile kurulan “Mekke ittifakı”nı, ABD ve NATO politikaları ile tam bir uyum içinde olan tutumunu; Trump’ın övgüsünü kazanan İran ve Filistin politikasını, NATO politikaları çerçevesi içinde artan silahlanma harcamalarını kullanarak elini güçlendirmeye ve bölge ülkeleriyle kurduğu ekseni güçlendirmeye çalışıyor.

Kuşkusuz her iki ülkenin bağımlılığı daha fazla artıran bu tutumlarının ana nedeni sadece Türk-Yunan ilişkileri ve Ege-Doğu Akdeniz gibi sorunlarla açıklanamaz. Esas neden bölgede oluşan ya da oluşması olası olan dengelerden pay kapma yarışıdır. Türkiye’yi asıl kaygılandıran İsrail’in bölgede oyun kurucu duruma gelme planlarıdır. Örneğin “yavru vatan” ilan edilmesine ramak kalan Suriye’de İsrail’in etkisinin artması ve Colani hükümeti ile anlaşma masasına oturulması, Arap ülkeleriyle İbrahim anlaşmalarının imzalanması, Yunanistan’ın AB üyesi olarak Türkiye ile bölgesel çıkarlar üzerinden iş birliği yapan ülkeler ve tekellerle ekonomik, askeri ve ticari ilişkiler geliştirmesi Türkiye’nin yayılmacı politikaları önünde ciddi engeller oluşturuyor.

Son süreçte ise Yunanistan, Kıbrıs ve İsrail arasında çekilen elektrik hattı ve Türkiye tarafından hazırlanan “Mavi vatan” kanunu ve “deniz parkları” kararı, iki ülke arasında gerginliğin yeniden yükselmesine neden oldu. Yunan hükümeti “Mavi vatan” kanununun “hiçbir geçerliliğinin olmayacağını” savunurken, Dışişleri Bakanı Yorgos Gerapetritis defalarca “Yunanistan her türlü tahrike karşı koymaya hazırdır” …

title: Elecciones Brasil 2026, una batalla contra el imperialismo
content:
Las amplias elecciones que el próximo 4 de octubre tendrán lugar en Brasil, en las que se elegirán presidente, gobernadores y legisladores, son de importancia estratégica para nuestra Abya Yala y para todo el globo terráqueo. Brasil es el 5to país más extenso, está entre las 10 economías más grandes y demográficamente ocupa el séptimo lugar en el mundo.


Por otra parte, el Brasil de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, del Partido de los Trabajadores (PT), forma parte de los BRICS, quienes vienen abogando por un orden mundial más justo y equilibrado; su principal socio comercial es China, con una tendencia al crecimiento en su intercambio comercial; ha hecho fuertes críticas al ente sionista que, con la ayuda de los EE. UU., está ejecutando un genocidio contra el pueblo palestino. Todo lo anterior lo convierte en el principal objetivo del presidente Trump en el hemisferio. Ya le ha impuesto a las importaciones de EE. UU. desde Brasil, entre el 12.5 % y el 50 % de aranceles, lo que ha hecho descender las exportaciones brasileñas hacia los EE. UU. a sus niveles más bajos desde 1997, lo que ha afectado negativamente su economía, expresado esto, en el bajo crecimiento de su PIB durante 2026.


Trump y su secretario de Estado, Marco Rubio, se han estado pronunciando a favor de la candidatura de Flavio Bolsonaro y criticado ferozmente el juicio que se le siguió a Jair Bolsonaro, por el intento del golpe de Estado, llegando al extremo de tomar medidas coercitivas unilaterales contra el juez que llevó la causa.


La intromisión de los EE. UU. en los asuntos internos de otros países es bien conocida. En Nuestra América han derrocado decenas de gobiernos e instalado dictaduras militares, han desestabilizado gobiernos legítimos, han bloqueado e impuesto medidas ilegales e inhumanas contra pueblos enteros y han llegado a violar la soberanía de varios países con agresiones militares directas: México, Cuba, Haití, Nicaragua, República Dominicana, Panamá, Granada y Venezuela son ejemplo de ello. Han manipulado elecciones abiertamente, teniendo los últimos 18 meses los ejemplos de Honduras, Ecuador, Colombia y Perú, donde, de manera grotesca y descarada, han impulsado candidatos, amenazado a la población con bloquear el envío de remesas, amedrentado a los gobiernos y empresarios con elevar aranceles y han utilizado sus mecanismos de manipulación y desinformación contra amplios sectores de la población, utilizando técnicas como la Big Data, los algoritmos de las redes sociales y buscadores y la última tendencia que es el uso de la inteligencia artificial como una más de estas nefastas herramientas.


La injerencia de EE. UU. en los asuntos internos de decenas de países, ha quedado registrado en diversos libros, como los de William Blum (2005) y (2006), Guenther Roppel (2005) y Luis Suárez Salazar (2006) entre otros. En el caso brasileño ya en 1960 los militares, por presión de la embajada yanqui, exigieron y lograron la salida del presidente Quadros, quien pocos meses antes de ser destituido había otorgado la máxima condecoración, para autoridades extranjeras, al Che Guevara. En 1964 le darían un golpe de Estado al presidente Joao Goulart, poco después de anunciar la expropiación y redistribución de tierras privadas y la nacionalización de refinerías de petróleo y lograrían la destitución de la presidente Dilma Rousseffa del PT, a través de un impeachment, en 2016.


Por otra parte, el candidato con mayores posibilidades de disputar la presidencia a Lula, es el actual senador del Partido Liberal (PL), Flávio Bolsonaro. Como digno hijo de su padre, el ex presidente Jair Bolsonaro, viajó a Washington a reunirse con el secretario de Estado, para planear la campaña en contra de Lula, lo que resultó en la aplicación de aranceles del 50 % a importantes productos provenientes de Brasil, pretendiendo afectar a todo el pueblo de Brasil, con la intención de robarle apoyo al gobierno de Lula. Pocos días después de esta visita, llegó Rubio a declarar que, “Brasil no es amigo de Estados Unidos”, lo cual fue dirigido a genera malestar y angustia en las clases medias y altas del país.


Flavio Bolsonaro también visitó Tel Aviv, buscando el apoyo de Netanyahu y ofreció cambiar la embajada de Brasil a Jerusalem, en caso de ganar las elecciones. El apoyo sionista es muy importante, ya que tienen relaciones muy importantes con los grandes grupos económico-financieros que manejan la economía brasileña y mundial. También son un apoyo importante en el área …

author: ROAPE
title: The price of becoming your own boss in Uganda’s boda boda industry
content:
It is said that Uganda’s vast motorcycle-taxi industry employs more men than any other sector outside agriculture. In Kampala alone, Uganda’s rapidly expanding capital city, estimates suggests there could be upwards of

300,000 moto-taxi

 (or

boda boda

) drivers currently in circulation out of a daytime population of roughly four million workers and residents. Moving people and things from A to B is big business here – and there is big business too in the alleviation of

boda

 driver hardships.


Fuelled by global venture capital and facilitated by both

digital technologies

 and

loose


regulatory

 oversight, over the past 15 years a new regime of

‘for-profit poverty reduction’

 has coursed its way through the highways and back alleys of this thriving sector. Through Buy Now, Pay Later credit products targeted specifically towards the

boda

 market, a growing fleet of specialist asset financing companies offer drivers the chance to escape a long-running informal rental system (known locally as

kibaluwa

) by one day acquiring a motorcycle of their own. Or to use the aspirational phrasing of one of Uganda’s largest moto-taxi financiers, Tugende, to

‘be their own boss’

.


The companies plying these ‘hire-purchase’ loans talk routinely of

‘win-win’

 solutions, bringing together their own profit motive with a mission to alleviate poverty in a way that feels compelling and seamless. Chief business officers in the US celebrate fintech in Africa as a

‘goldmine’

 where the ‘opportunity is massive’. One European founder has been described as

‘making better returns financing motorbike sales’ than he ‘ever did arbitraging gold and silver’

 as a commodities trader.


Beyond the boosterism


But how do these schemes work beyond the boosterism? In

a new paper

 I ask exactly this, drawing on interviews and semi-randomised surveys with hundreds of Kampala’s

boda boda

 drivers

between 2020 and 2022

 to explore what the process of becoming one’s own boss actually looks like.


The first thing worth noting is the scale of asset finance. Out of 370 surveyed drivers, just over half had accessed their bike using a hire-purchase loan and were either paying this down at the time of research or had fully completed one. The majority of these loans were with a specialist lending company like Tugende, Asaak or Watu, confirming

other


reports

 from Kampala that there has been a significant shift in this direction away from the traditional

kibaluwa

 model in recent years. As one driver explained: ‘It is now companies running the system’.


The next thing to note is that fully paid-up ownership can really deliver. Comparing drivers’ income and expenditure data,

the research shows

 that, on average, owners increase their net weekly earnings by a remarkable 73% relative to those who rent. Accounting for this is the dramatic fall in operating costs when regular access payments are no longer required. Essentially, ownership allows

boda

 drivers to retain more of what they make.


The long, rocky road to ownership


This is only one part of the picture, however. Though impressive, there is much that this overall figure conceals in terms of what the road to full ownership consists of. ‘3 Ps’ define this: protracted, precarious and pricey.


First, the journey to ownership is

protracted

. To make hire-purchase arrangements economically viable for themselves, many drivers agree to lower their weekly loan repayments by spreading out instalments over timeframes as long as two years. During this entire time, drivers spend significantly more per week on motorcycle access than they otherwise would – 36% more, on average, relative to those in the traditional rental system.


Boda bodas at sunset in Kampala (copyright William Kane Olwit, 2018)


To cover this, drivers must work harder throughout the duration of their repayment plan, leading many to talk of the ‘pressure’ that life under hire-purchase entails. In addition to the potential risks this poses from a

road


safety

 perspective, some riders also seek wider sources of support simply to help them meet their weekly targets and eventually pay down the loan, including through philanthropy platforms such as GiveDirectly.


Second, becoming an owner is

precarious

. Once included in the hire-purchase economy, drivers face a constant threat of loan default and asset repossession. This is underpinned by the basic tension that exists between fixed repayment demands on …

author: Unknown
title: Nationale Demo - Smash Imperialism - 11. Oktober
content:
Bewegung 11. Oktober


Der Imperialismus hat seine Transformation in eine neue Phase begonnen. Die Hegemonie des von den USA angeführten imperialistischen Blocks läutet ihr eigenes Ende ein. Dies zeigt sich – um nur einige Beispiele zu nennen – in eskalierenden Angriffskriegen (Iran), Genoziden (Palästina, Sudan) und Ressourcenkriegen (Kongo). Ebenso werden im Stellvertreterkrieg zwischen der NATO und Russland in der Ukraine abertausende Leben von oftmals zwangsrekrutierten Arbeiter:innen für europäische und US-Interessen geopfert. Andernorts bestrebt das US-Imperium – wie sich in Kuba und Venezuela in äusserster Brutalität zeigt – verstärkt den absoluten Machtanspruch auf Lateinamerika, in US-Perspektive als eigene Einflusszone angesehen, auch "backyard" genannt.


Aus Angst unterzugehen, schlägt die Bestie wild um sich. Die materielle Übermacht schwindet immer mehr und der Hauptkonkurrent China – und damit auch viele Verbündete der Volksrepublik – gewinnt an globalem Einfluss. Die Kapitalist:innen schüren Krise um Krise: Sei es der unmittelbar bevorstehende Klimakollaps, die Faschisierung der westlichen Staaten, die zunehmende Überwachung durch KI und die aggressive Umverteilung von unten nach oben.


Die Lügen der herrschenden Klasse werden immer offensichtlicher. Sie versuchen uns für dumm zu verkaufen, indem sie uns erzählen, in Gaza gäbe es einen Waffenstillstand. Indem sie legitimen und notwendigen Widerstand als "Terrorismus" deklarieren. Indem sie Palästina als "Israel" bezeichnen. Damit versuchen sie den Status Quo aufrechtzuerhalten: Eine weisse Vorherrschaft, die es ihnen erlaubt, ungebremst Kapital anzuhäufen und ihr Territorium gewaltsam zu erweitern.


Im Kongo fördern multinationale Konzerne im Dienste westlicher Mächte seit über 30 Jahren Genozid, um das Land im Chaos versinken zu lassen. Durch aktive Destabilisierung lassen sich die Ressourcen leichter abbauen und das Land ausbeuten. Dasselbe geschieht im Sudan, wo ein sogenannter "Bürgerkrieg" befeuert wird, um die zahlreichen Bodenschätze auszubeuten.


Dies sind nur einige wenige Beispiele von zu vielen, die aufzeigen, dass Millionen von Menschenleben (vor allem Schwarzes und Braunes Leben) den Herrschenden scheissegal sind. Was zählt, sind kurzfristige Gewinne. Alles auf Kosten von Mensch und Natur.


Das US-Imperium agiert dabei mit einer militärischen Gewalt und einer Grösse, die alle bisherigen Ausmasse übersteigt. Weiter ist das US-Militär der mit Abstand grösste Einzelverbraucher fossiler Brennstoffe und damit der grösste Umweltverschmutzer der Welt.


Unsere individuellen Initiativen, die Umwelt zu schützen und zu respektieren, verenden im Angesicht der wütenden Bestie in völliger Bedeutungslosigkeit. Doch der Fokus auf individuelles Konsumverhalten offenbart einen tieferliegenden Mechanismus: Nachhaltiges Verhalten wird zum Massstab erhoben und wer davon abweicht, wird verurteilt. Die Logik dahinter: "Divide and rule"


So wird unser Fokus und unsere Energie auf die gegenseitige Kontrolle gelegt, anstatt die Tausenden von Bomben zu stoppen, die Mensch und Natur komplett zerstören. Symptombekämpfung wird als Lösung hochstilisiert; wertvolle Zeit, die wir im Kampf für Klimagerechtigkeit brauchen könnten, geht verloren.


Wir müssen endlich verstehen: Der Kampf gegen die globale Kriegsmaschinerie und der Kampf für Klimagerechtigkeit ist ein und derselbe Kampf!


Die bürgerliche Demokratie möchte uns klarmachen, dass wir mittels Abstimmungen etwas verändern können und verkauft uns, dass wir mit unserem individuellen Konsumverhalten die Natur "retten können". Demokratie gibt uns zu verstehen: "Alle Menschen sind gleich". Doch wenn wir genauer hinschauen, verstehen wir die bürgerliche Demokratie als Teil des Problems. Denn auch sie ist nur ein Mittel, das Volk zu unterdrücken und eines freien Lebens zu berauben und somit die Kapitalinteressen der herschenden Klasse zu befriedigen. Unter dem Vorwand der "Demokratsierung" (eigentlich "Zivilisierung") werden seit jeher Länder angegriffen, Überausbeutung legitimiert und Proteste gewaltsam niedergeschlagen. Die Aussengrenzen werden aufgerüstet, Menschen illegalisiert. Militarisierung und Aufrüstung wird auf Kosten der Gesundheit und Bildung vorangetrieben. Faschistoides Gedankengut schiesst wie Pilze aus dem Boden und zeigt sich in Form von Parteien, in Gesetzesvorlagen, in medialer Hetze, oder dem Antifa-Verbot. Der Diskurs wird mithilfe von liberalen Parteien schrittweise gegen rechts verschoben …

author: Publicación Abierta
title: Belo Horizonte, Brasil: barricada por cero desalojos y contra la ley de gentrificación
content:
Texto disponible en portugués y español. Fotos al final.


ES


El jueves 1 de octubre, la Avenida Antônio Carlos fue parcialmente bloqueada con neumáticos en llamas y una pancarta instalada en el Viaducto Senegal en protesta por las amenazas de desalojo de ocupantes de viviendas en el centro de Belo Horizonte y la Ley 574, que afectará al centro de la ciudad ampliado y a barrios como Concórdia y Lagoinha.


Los manifestantes bloquearon 3 carriles, causando retrasos en el tráfico y mucho ruido para denunciar un proyecto de ciudad donde la vivienda no es un derecho para todos, sino una mercancía que unos pocos venden y de la que se lucran.


El derecho a la vivienda y la función social de la propiedad, ambos garantizados por la Constitución, son atacados por la especulación inmobiliaria y una lógica urbana accesible solo a los ricos.


Como consecuencia, las ocupaciones de Maria do Arraial, en la Rua da Bahia, y Kasa Invisível, en la Av. Bias Fortes, así como las ocupaciones de São Paulo y Casa Rosa en la Rua Santa Catarina, corren riesgo de desalojo.


Para colmo, el alcalde Álvaro Damião (União Brasil) y la alcaldía de Belo Horizonte presentaron el Proyecto de Ley 574, que establece la denominada Operación Urbana Simplificada (OUS) para la Regeneración de Barrios del Centro. Bajo el pretexto de promover la “regeneración” y la “revitalización económica” del centro y la periferia, se trata claramente de un amplio paquete de beneficios para que las grandes empresas inmobiliarias especulen, construyan edificios en edificios de gran altura, aumenten los alquileres y desplacen a los residentes y la vida comunitaria de la zona.


¡UN DESALOJO MÁS Y LA CIUDAD SE PARALIZARÁ!


 


PT/BR


BELO HORIZONTE: BARRICADA POR DESPEJO ZERO E CONTRA A PL DA GENTRIFICAÇÃO


Dia 1 de outubro, quinta-feira, a Av. Antônio Carlos amanheceu parcialmente bloqueada com pneus queimando e faixa instalada no Viaduto Senegal

contra as ameaças de despejo de ocupações de moradia no centro de BH e a PL 574

, que vai afetar o centro expandido da cidade e bairros como Concórdia e Lagoinha.


Manifestantes bloquearam 3 faixas, causando lentidão e muito barulho para

 denunciar um projeto de cidade onde a moradia não é um direito de todos, mas uma mercadoria para poucos venderem e lucrarem.


O direito à moradia e a função social da propriedade, ambos garantidos na Constituição, são atacados pela especulação imobiliária e uma lógica de cidade acessível apenas para os ricos.


Como consequência disso,

 estão em risco de despejo

 as ocupações Maria do Arraial, na Rua da Bahia e a Kasa Invisível, na Av. Bias Fortes, ocupação São Paulo e a ocupação Casa Rosa na Rua Santa Catarina.


Para piorar, o prefeito Álvaro Damião (União Brasil) e a Prefeitura de Belo Horizonte apresentaram o

PL 574

 que institui a chamada

Operação Urbana Simplificada (OUS) dos Bairros do Centro

. Com a desculpa de promover a “regeneração” e a “dinamização econômica” da área central e pericentral. Porém, é obviamente

um grande pacote de benefícios para as grandes empresas do mercado imobiliário especularem

, verticalizarem os bairros, aumentando aluguéis e expulsando moradores e a vida comunitária da vizinhança.


A manifestação de trancamento da avenida realizada hoje por populares é também um chamado para que outras comunidades, grupos e movimentos se unam em torno da resistência contra os despejos, contra a gentrificação e por uma cidade onde caibamos a todes!


OCUPE TUDO!


MAIS UM DESPEJO E A CIDADE VAI PARAR!

Belo Horizonte, Brasil: barricada por cero desalojos y contra la ley de gentrificación

Indymedia Argentina Centro de Medios Independientes (( i ))

author: Daron Letts
title: Iqaluit’s low-barrier shelter to open in January
content:
Uquutaq Society’s new $40-million low-barrier shelter is slated to open in Iqaluit in January.


The new building is located downtown at 158 Nipisa St., near The Snack Restaurant.


Uquutaq Society’s emerging new three-storey facility includes 44 low-barrier shelter beds on the second floor and 13 single-room transitional housing units on the top floor. The main floor will be a warming centre during the day. (Photo by Daron Letts)


“This is a low-barrier site, meaning you don’t need to be sober or unimpaired [to enter],” said society CEO Laurel McCorriston in an interview in September.


Named by elders as Ullivik, which means “the place you wait for the tide,” the three-storey, 44-bed facility will offer

 16 beds for women, 24 beds for men and two rooms for

couples, which can also serve as private space for individuals in need of quiet or privacy.


The building includes an additional 13 single-occupancy transitional housing units on the top floor.


Currently, the only other low-barrier facility in the city is the society’s 17-cot overnight shelter at 534 Niaqunngusiariaq Road, which accommodates five women and 12 men nightly.


Last year, that shelter provided more than 6,000 overnight stays and served more than 800 meals of caribou, char and maataq.


“Ullivik provides a huge increase in services for people,” McCorriston said.


The first floor features a commercial kitchen, dining room, showers and a laundry —

part of a year-round warming centre that is accessible daily. It includes a self-contained room with sofas, armchairs and a television.


A first-floor balcony will serve as a smoking section, preventing guests from smoking in the streets, McCorriston said.


Ainiak Korgak was among the elders at Iqaluit’s Elders’ Qammaq last year who brainstormed names for society staff to choose from.


Frobisher Bay’s tides, among the biggest in the world, ebb and flow on a 12-hour cycle, making Ullivik an apt name for the new shelter, he said, in an interview Thursday.


Ainiak Korgak, among those at Iqaluit’s Elders’ Qammaq who brainstormed names for Uquutaq Society’s new $40-million low-barrier shelter. (Photo by Daron Letts)


Ullivik symbolizes “renewal,” Korgak said.


“The tide comes in and takes away your shortcomings,” he said. “That’s one way of looking at it.”


The new facility

developed “pretty fast,” McCorriston said.


The society applied for funding in February 2023.

Forgivable and repayable loans through the Canadian Mortgage and Housing Corp. covered a little more than half the cost. Indigenous Services Canada chipped in $13 million and the Qikiqtani Inuit Association contributed $1 million.


Reaching Home, a homelessness program managed by Housing, Infrastructure and Communities Canada, pitched in $500,000.


NDL Construction Ltd. is leading the build, originally scheduled for completion in December.


Uquutaq’s next initiative is the $27-million Butler Supportive Housing Project, located next to Capital Suites at 804 Aiviq Street, which will provide 32 additional single-occupancy supportive housing units. The long-term housing option includes support staff on site.


Piles were installed this summer and structural steel was added this month.


That federally funded project is expected to be completed by 2028.

author: anred
title: «Se vuelven a encender las calles» tras el fallo de la Corte que reactivó la extranjerización de la tierra
content:
El máximo tribunal dejó vigente la derogación de la Ley de Tierras impulsada por Milei mediante el DNU 70/2023. Organizaciones sociales, sindicales, campesinas, indígenas y políticas comenzaron a reunirse para responder en las calles. En Diputados, sectores de la oposición convocaron a una sesión especial para el 15 de octubre con el objetivo de rechazar el decreto. Por ANRed


La Corte Suprema de Justicia de la Nación volvió a poner en vigencia la derogación de la Ley 26.737 de Régimen de Protección al Dominio Nacional sobre la Propiedad, Posesión o Tenencia de Tierras Rurales, impulsada por Javier Milei a través del DNU 70/2023. El fallo, firmado por Horacio Rosatti, Carlos Rosenkrantz y Ricardo Lorenzetti, revocó la sentencia de la Cámara Federal de La Plata que había declarado inconstitucional el artículo 154 del megadecreto y había frenado la derogación de la denominada Ley de Tierras.


La decisión judicial no declaró constitucional el DNU ni resolvió el fondo de la discusión. La Corte fundamentó su resolución en una cuestión procesal: consideró que el Centro de Ex Combatientes Islas Malvinas (CECIM) La Plata, que había presentado la demanda, no tenía legitimación suficiente para llevar adelante esa acción colectiva. El propio tribunal aclaró que su decisión se limitó a la existencia de un caso judicial y a la legitimación de la organización demandante. Sin embargo, el efecto concreto es que vuelve a regir la derogación de la Ley de Tierras dispuesta por el artículo 154 del DNU 70/23.


La Ley 26.737 establecía, entre otras restricciones, un límite del 15% para la titularidad extranjera de tierras rurales. Con la derogación de esas disposiciones quedan sin efecto esas restricciones específicas.


El fallo llega además después de una jornada de movilización que, durante agosto, puso en el centro de la agenda la disputa por la tierra y la soberanía territorial.


La respuesta vuelve a las calles


El fallo produjo una rápida reacción. La CTA Autónoma y la CTA de las y los Trabajadores convocaron a movilizarse el

martes 6 de octubre a las 15 frente a la Corte Suprema

, junto a sindicatos, organizaciones sociales y otros sectores. ATE también anunció su estado de alerta y movilización.


En paralelo, comenzaron a multiplicarse las reuniones para organizar la respuesta. El

viernes 2 de octubre

, organizaciones que participaron de la denominada Marcha de la Bronca tienen previsto reunirse en Parque Lezama para discutir una movilización contra el fallo. Gabriel Solano anticipó esa convocatoria.


La reacción recupera así una consigna que ya recorrió el país durante agosto:

“La tierra no se vende, no se quema ni se desaloja”

.


El antecedente del 6 de agosto: extranjerización frenada, desalojos aprobados


El conflicto tiene un antecedente inmediato. El

6 de agosto

, mientras el Senado debatía la denominada Ley de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada, una jornada federal reunió a organizaciones campesinas, indígenas, ambientales, sociales, políticas, sindicales y de derechos humanos en distintos puntos del país.


La movilización central se realizó frente al Congreso, donde hubo radio abierta, festival cultural y un verdurazo. También se registraron acciones en numerosas ciudades y localidades del país. La consigna fue contundente:

“La tierra no se vende, no se quema ni se desaloja”

.


La presión social se produjo mientras el oficialismo intentaba conseguir los votos para avanzar con el proyecto. Finalmente, el Gobierno tuvo que retirar del texto el capítulo referido a la extranjerización de tierras. Ese retroceso fue señalado por las organizaciones convocantes y dirigentes de izquierda como resultado de la movilización.


Represión en el Congreso: tres personas detenidas por defender la tierra


La masiva movilización contra el proyecto de Ley de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada, que busca ampliar la extranjerización de las tierras y profundizar su privatización, terminó con represión.

pic.twitter.com/cRw7pDoUO8


— ANRed #30Años (@Red__Accion)

August 6, 2026


  


Pero hubo una diferencia fundamental:

la movilización logró frenar el capítulo de extranjerización, pero no consiguió impedir la aprobación de los artículos vinculados con los desalojos exprés

.


El Senado aprobó el proyecto de propiedad privada por 37 votos contra 33. La iniciativa estableció mecanismos destinados a agilizar los desalojos de inmuebles, viviendas, campos y terrenos considerados ocupados o usurpados.

author: Charlotte Reck
title: Spain’s Tenants’ Rights Protesters Win Reforms After 87-Year-Old Evicted
content:
Spain’s government has approved new measures to support tenants’ rights following widespread protests – but they need approval from congress and campaigners say they do not go far enough. 


Around 30,000 people marched through Madrid on Saturday, and

hundreds remained for days

 in encampments across the capital’s central plazas, after an 87-year-old woman was forcibly removed from her home of 70 years on a stretcher. 


Maricarmen Abascal was evicted after her rent rose from €500 (£428) to €1,650

and she was unable to pay

. Urbagestión – the investment firm that owns the property – has now been forced to allow her to return and pay €533 in rent.  


The eviction prompted the Madrid Tenants’ Union to draw up the Maricarmen decree, which calls for a law against evicting vulnerable individuals without offering them alternative housing. It also proposes curbing unjustified price increases, a freeze on rents and an automatic renewal of leases to prevent unjustified evictions. 


Spain’s Socialist Workers’ party-led coalition government approved the extension of rental contracts, the ban on evicting vulnerable renters and the regulation of seasonal and room rentals that interfere with the supply of affordable housing, although measures must now be approved in congress, where the coalition lacks a majority.


But the government has split its proposal into two decrees – the first is concerned with banning evictions and introducing regulations, while the second considers automatic lease renewals. While it is believed that the conservative Catalan and Basque parties will throw support behind the first decree, it is thought likely the parties will reject the second.


Alicia Del Río, a Tenant’s Union spokesperson, said splitting the proposals into separate decrees was “a tactic of tearing something into shreds so that all that’s left are scraps.” 


“The union demands the implementation of the Maricarmen decree in its entirety,” she

told the Guardian

. “They have to accept what people are demanding.”


Spain’s health minister Mónica García wrote on X:


“What a month ago was unimaginable has now been achieved thanks to social mobilisation, the encampment, that clamour from the streets that pushes forward and serves as a lever for change.”

 


She added: “Now, the challenge ahead of us is to defend these measures in congress.”

author: Unknown
title: Le 4ème n'est pas à vendre
content:
La militarisation de la ville, la financiarisation de l'habitat et du logement, la privatisation des espaces publics, la construction de frontières – tant formelles que symboliques –, les politiques de sécurité publique fondées sur le profilage racial et la criminalisation de la pauvreté constituent les fondements d'un urbanisme néolibéral et du néofascisme en tant que projet de ville.


À Marseille

, un nouveau rapport à la ville semble s'être imposé à marche forcée : gentrification, privatisation, évacuation de squats et augmentation exponentielle des loyers. Les conséquences retentissent dans tous les aspects de la vie quotidienne : habitant•es chassé•es du centre-ville par le tourisme de masse et des loyers prohibitifs, disparition de lieux emblématiques et multiplication de logements vacants.


Au sein du 4ème

, après les Airbnb, nous voyons apparaître les colivings, immeubles entiers destinés à la location à court et moyen terme à des tarifs prohibitifs pour la plupart d'entre nous, qui semblent être le nouvel eldorado de la spéculation immobilière.


Ceci n'est pas une fatalité mais bien un projet délibéré ayant pour but final l'enrichissement de holdings immobilières aux dépens des habitants et habitantes, qui voient s'envoler le prix du logement.


Par ailleurs, l'obsession de transformer chaque mètre carré de terrain en produit rentable empêche l'apparition de lieux propices à la solidarité et à la convivialité : locaux associatifs, jardins autonomes et partagés, équipements sportifs et jeux pour les enfants.


La financiarisation de l'habitat est l'affaire de nous toutes et tous.


Face aux problématiques du mal-logement, d'insalubrité, de la mise en péril, des charges et loyers exorbitants, répondons par une solidarité sans faille.


Comité antifasciste du 4ème

author: Isaac Nellist
title: Balmain meeting calls for public housing in Bays West, opposes Labor’s plan
content:
Bays West includes public land at Glebe Island, White Bay and parts of Rozelle and Lilyfield. Labor’ wants to hand this to developers to build high-rise apartments; it proposes only 10% be reserved for “affordable” or “essential worker” housing.

The 150-strong meeting was organised by the Better Future Coalition (BFC), comprising resident groups which oppose NSW Labor and the Labor-dominated Inner West Council’s (IWC) pro-developer planning schemes.

Many community and housing groups supported the meeting including Leichhardt Matters, Save Dully, Action for Public Housing, Save Marrickville, Hands off Glebe, Friends of Erskineville, Doing Density Better, Mosman Matters and others.

Judy Mundey, a long-time activist and barrister set the framework for discussion by outlining the historic decline in public housing across NSW and the consequent rise in homelessness, housing insecurity and expensive rents and house prices.

“It’s not as if the government is not aware we have a housing crisis; there is no shortage of announcements and promises … but almost all proposals involve the private sector.”

Mundey said there are “almost daily” reports on dodgy developers, to whom Minns is handing over public land.

“If we’re going to address the housing crisis, we need less privatisation of public land and more well designed public housing,” Mundey said.

“In opposition, Labor said any surplus land would be subject to a mandatory requirement for 30% of social, affordable and universal housing. But now in government, at Bays West, it has reduced that to 10% for affordable and essential worker housing.

“There is no commitment for public housing to be any part of the plan. This is a failure to utilise public assets to address the social injustice inflicted on so many, a failure to ensure a decent, safe, secure home, essential for health and wellbeing.”

Architect and urban designer Eddie Ma gave details about what is known about the Bays West plan. He said Minns had commissioned international architecture firms to make proposals.

Ma emphasised that the plans could be changed — for better or for worse. “It should be the community that decides what we do with Bays West, not the government and certainly not architects.”

Former independent Inner West councillor John Stamolis said that the inner west was one of the country’s highest density areas and that it was ridiculous for Labor to accuse people who want better planning of opposing any development. He said there needed to be more public housing now because of the security it brings.

Greens MP for Balmain Kobi Shetty said it was hard to know a lot about Labor’s plan as it has been vague. She said the Greens welcome Labor’s commitment to delivering the Glebe Island Bridge as an essential walking and cycling link.

Ben Radford, a town planner and Green Left journalist, MCed the meeting, which voted overwhelmingly to adopt a resolution opposing Labor’s plan, calling for community consultation and to add a sixth point calling for any housing at Bays West to be public.

BFC had invited Philippa Scott, Labor’s candidate for Balmain and deputy mayor of IWC, to come and listen to the concerns. She did not reply.

[Isaac Nellist is a member of the Better Future Coalition and is the Socialist Alliance candidate for Balmain in the NSW elections.]

author: Helmut Weiss
title: Gegen Mietpreisexplosion die Deutsche Wohnen & Co enteignen: Ein guter Anfang
content:
Dossier


Die Kampagne zur Enteignung der „Deutsche Wohnen“ ist ein guter Anfang. (Denn die Vonovia&Co sind ja auch noch da…). Mit Sicherheit wird in diesem Zusammenhang die Reaktion ihre übliche Gegenkampagne starten, des Bürgers Eigenheim sei in Gefahr – und Ältere werden sich vielleicht noch erinnern, dass es in der BRD auch einmal eine Sozialdemokratie gab. Die sich bei ihren, wie immer begrenzten, Schritten gegen den Vorwurf verteidigen musste, sie wolle dem „deutschen Arbeiter“ seine Villa im Tessin nehmen. Diese Aussicht kann und soll eine solche Kampagne also nicht verhindern oder auch nur beschränken. Denn Gründe dafür gibt es mehr als genug – von der unbeeindruckten Fortsetzung der Preistreiberei bei den Mieten durch große – und kleinere – Wohnungsgesellschaften, bis hin zur Stadt- und Baupolitik diverser Landesregierungen. Eine Entwicklung, die vielleicht Städte wie Berlin oder Frankfurt im Zentrum der Aufmerksamkeit haben mag – aber „das Böse ist immer und überall“, auch in Duisburg oder Niedersteppenbach. Zu den aktuellen Entwicklungen im Widerstand gegen den Mietenwahnsinn und dessen ungebrochene Fortsetzung siehe

die Kampagnenseite


 und hier:


Studie: Vergesellschaftung von Wohnbeständen: Ausgestaltung entscheidend für Finanzierbarkeit, Rechtssicherheit und Umsetzbarkeit


„Eine Vergesellschaftung großer Wohnungsbestände wird den Wohnraummangel in Deutschlands Großstädten nicht beheben. Dazu braucht es Neubau in großem Stil. Dennoch kann die Vergesellschaftung als ergänzendes Element sinnvoll sein, um das Bezahlbarkeitsproblem von Mieten zu vermindern, ergibt eine neue Studie am Beispiel der Situation in Berlin. Wichtig ist dabei aber erstens, dass der ohnehin angespannte Berliner Landeshaushalt nicht belastet wird und zweitens, dass die Vergesellschaftung so umgesetzt wird, dass nicht zugleich der Neubau leidet. Zu diesem Ergebnis kommen Prof. Dr. Sebastian Dullien vom Institut für Makroökonomie und Konjunkturforschung (IMK) der Hans-Böckler-Stiftung, Dr. Patrick Kaczmarczyk und Prof. Dr. Tom Krebs von der Universität Mannheim sowie Prof. Dr. Achim Truger von der Universität Duisburg-Essen. Die Ökonomen zeigen am Beispiel Berlins, dass die Vergesellschaftung von Wohnungen nicht nur sozialpolitisch sinnvoll, sondern – je nach Modell – auch wirtschaftlich und fiskalisch tragbar sein kann. Die bei einer Überführung von rund 210.000 Wohnungen in Gemeineigentum fällige Entschädigung für die privaten Wohnungsunternehmen veranschlagen die Forscher auf rund 13,5 Milliarden Euro. Bei kluger Ausgestaltung der Vergesellschaftung wäre das ohne Kürzungen im Berliner Landeshaushalt finanzierbar. Die Forscher haben drei verschiedene Modelle zur Vergesellschaftung von Wohnbeständen untersucht. Variante 1: Eine neu zu gründende Anstalt des öffentlichen Rechts (AöR) übernimmt die Wohnungen. Variante 2: Die sechs landeseigenen Wohnungsunternehmen (LWU) übernehmen die Wohnungen. Variante 3: Die sechs Wohnungsunternehmen werden in eine Anstalt des öffentlichen Rechts integriert und übernehmen die Wohnungen. Nach Analyse der Forscher ist Variante 2 am besten geeignet, um rechtliche, finanzielle und organisatorische Risiken einer Vergesellschaftung so weit wie möglich zu minimieren. (…)


Die Wohnungen könnten direkt oder über den Umweg einer vorübergehend eingerichteten AöR den sechs bestehenden LWU übertragen werden. Diese bewirtschaften bereits mehrere hunderttausend Wohnungen und verfügen über die notwendigen technischen und organisatorischen Kapazitäten, die natürlich ausgebaut werden müssten. Die Entschädigungen würden finanziert über zusätzliches, vom Land bereitgestelltes Eigenkapital der LWU sowie eine Fremdfinanzierung der jeweiligen Wohnungsunternehmen. Das Risiko, dass Ausgaben und Verschuldung der Wohnungsbauunternehmen zum Sektor Staat gerechnet werden, wäre deutlich geringer als bei Variante 1 mit einer dauerhaft errichteten zentralen AöR. Nach Einschätzung der Forscher ist das ein zentraler Vorteil des Modells. Hinzu kommt als weiterer Pluspunkt die Anbindung an die existierenden, erfahrenen Unternehmen. Diese würde auch das Risiko vermindern, dass der Wohnungsneubau durch organisatorische Überforderung leidet, weil die Senatsverwaltung vollständig mit dem Aufbau der AöR absorbiert ist. (…)


Nimmt das Land Berlin Kredite auf, um das Eigenkapital eines öffentlichen Unternehmens aufzustocken, steht der zusätzlichen Verschuldung ein finanzieller Vermögenswert in Form der Beteiligung gegenüber. Solche …

author: Amy Goodman
title: Eviction of 87-Year-Old Sparks Protest Encampment Over Spain’s Housing Crisis
content:
“We want to change the whole model of housing in Spain,” says Sabina Carrau of the Madrid Tenants’ Union.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

The eviction of 87-year-old María del Carmen Abascal Martín in Madrid, after an investment fund bought her apartment building and more than tripled her rent, has become a symbol of Spain’s rising cost of living and sparked nationwide protests against corporate greed and wealth inequality. Over 600 protesters are now camped outside Madrid’s regional government headquarters demanding new tenant protections.

“What we have is a lot of furious people, enraged people, that are demanding from the government and from the public institutions that they give us give us some sort of solution,” says Sabina Carrau, a spokesperson for the Madrid Tenants’ Union, which is supporting the “Maricarmen decree” named after Abascal, set to be debated by Spain’s government this week.

Housing in Spain, as in much of the world, “is really connected to tourism, really connected to having and buying a house to make a speculation,” says socialist parliamentarian Tesh Sidi, who is calling instead for the guaranteed right to housing and “the right to have an affordable life.” Sidi, the only Sahrawi member of the Spanish parliament, also comments on Spain’s colonial relationship to Western Sahara and the state of Sahrawi rights and self-determination.

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: Today we’re broadcasting from London, tomorrow Copenhagen, and the rest of the week from Berlin. But we’re turning now to the Spanish capital of Madrid. A protest encampment over the cost of housing and housing instability has entered its third day as over 600 residents are now camped in front of the regional government headquarters at the Puerta del Sol plaza to demand new protections for tenants. Tens of thousands of people marched in the streets of Madrid Saturday. Demonstrations are also occurring across Spain.

Protests began Wednesday over the eviction of 87-year-old María del Carmen Abascal Martín, referred to just as Maricarmen, who was forcibly removed from her home of more than 70 years after an investment fund bought her apartment building and more than tripled, or more, her rent. Police broke down the door of her home and removed Maricarmen, who is 87 years old, on a stretcher as hundreds of supporters gathered outside. She later released a video message to supporters from her hospital bed.

MARÍA DEL CARMEN ABASCAL MARTÍN: [translated] I have not been able to defend my home, but I have fought so others can learn to fight for theirs. My home has been my life, and now I have to leave it behind. But that doesn’t mean I’m not going to keep fighting.

AMY GOODMAN: Protesters, camped in tents with sleeping bags in the Puerta del Sol plaza, say they won’t leave unless meaningful government action is taken.

SARA BARROS: [translated] What we are demanding is that the rental market be regulated, because rents are unaffordable and people simply cannot afford them. There are abuses taking place that can leave vulnerable people out on the street, such as Maricarmen, an 87-year-old woman with a disability who has no alternative housing after living in her home for 70 years.

LUCAS GARCIA: [translated] We are going to stay here until things change. There’s talk of a decree on Tuesday, and we will remain here until measures that we consider sufficient are adopted.

JORGE OTXOA: [translated] We are protesting so that we could claim and so the government listens to us, listens to a society that is tired of speculation, tired of corruption and tired of a system that sidelines the vast majority of the population. This is why we are here.

title: Kocaağa: Debt brake and social cuts deepened Germany’s crisis
content:
Muhlis Kocaağa, a member of Bremen's state parliament for Die Linke (The Left), discussed the reasons behind the rise of the far right in Germany, particularly in the eastern states, and Die Linke's role in opposing this trend.


Kocaağa said shrinking state budgets, the debt brake (Schuldenbremse) and cuts to social services had disrupted social stability. He also highlighted shortcomings in infrastructure and public services related to migration policies.


He said Germany was facing global geopolitical crises, rising energy costs, challenges arising from industrial transformation and a deepening housing crisis. Kocaağa stressed the urgent need to develop public and social policies to address these problems.


There has recently been a significant rise in the far right in Germany, particularly in eastern and North-Eastern Germany. How do you interpret this situation? Do you think the state is, in a sense, paving the way for it?


I assume you are referring to the state elections and the political situation in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, one of Germany's coastal states. There are two main reasons for this situation. My view differs somewhat from that of other politicians, and I have expressed it in political discussions as well.


The rise of the far right is generally attributed to the current government's social policies, particularly its tendency to restrict pensions, healthcare and social benefits. That certainly has an impact, but it is not the main determining factor. In my view, the fundamental reason is the existence of a deep-rooted, widespread right-wing tendency in Germany. Sometimes this tendency remains hidden, while at other times it emerges when the opportunity arises.


It reveals its true face whenever an opportunity for protest presents itself. This right-wing tendency has always existed in Germany, but it was less visible because the conditions were not favourable. Some attribute the current situation solely to opposition to government policies or to protest voters. Although protest voters certainly exist, we must not overlook the influence of the widespread right-wing tendency in Germany. Their existence does not change that underlying reality.


Some figures on the left, including those who were previously part of Die Linke but later formed the Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW), have suggested that they could break the firewall (Brandmauer) against Alternative for Germany (AfD) and form a government with it. How do you assess this position?


It is not always easy to predict how people's character will develop in politics. Even when these figures were part of Die Linke, they consistently adopted problematic positions in our discussions and were among those responsible for creating internal disputes within the party.


I consider their suggestion that they could break the firewall or cooperate with the AfD extremely dangerous for two reasons.


The first is their willingness to sacrifice everything for political power. It reflects an attitude of: "As long as I am in power, it doesn't matter what I have to sacrifice."


The second is their attempt to establish an opportunistic position for themselves in those regions. Ultimately, both approaches have the potential to harm society.


There has also been a noticeable increase in support for the left, particularly in Berlin. Die Linke lost votes in the early 2020s but has since seen its support rise. How do you explain this momentum?


The first reason is that the internal disputes and divisions within the party leadership have come to an end. The party's unity and solidarity have resonated positively with voters.


The second reason is that living conditions in Germany are becoming increasingly difficult. Die Linke is one of the parties offering the most concrete and consistent policies to make people's lives easier.


There is also a third factor we should not overlook: the rise of the right naturally strengthens its opposite. There is a significant group of voters who consciously support Die Linke in order to prevent the AfD from gaining votes.


Turning to budgetary constraints at state and municipal level, what is the situation regarding budget pressures, cuts to social services and infrastructure investment, particularly in cities such as Bremen and Bremerhaven?


The problem is not so much direct budget cuts as an enormous increase in spending requirements. For example, Bremerhaven's planned budget was around €700 million in 2023. It was initially …

title: Vartinis katliamında yaşamını yitirenler anıldı
content:
Muş – Muş Demokratik Kurumlar Platformu, 33 yıl önce Vartinis beldesinde 7'si çocuk 9 kişinin yakılarak katledildiği Vartinis Katliamı'nın yıldönümü dolayısıyla, Vartinis Müzesi'ne doğru yürüyüş gerçekleştirdi. Belde merkezinden müzeye doğru gerçekleşen yürüyüşte Türkçe ve Kürtçe “Em ê komkujîya Vartînîse jibîr nekin û nedin jibîrkirin” pankartı açıldı. Yürüyüşte sık sık alkış ve zılgıtlar eşliğinde "Şehîd namirin" sloganları atılırken, çok sayıda yurttaş katıldı. Yürüyüşün ardından Vartinis Müzesi önünde basın açıklaması gerçekleştirildi.

Katliamda ailesinden 9 kişiyi kaybeden ve şans eseri kurtulan Aysel Öğüt, askerler tarafından ailesinin yakılarak katledildiğini belirtti. Zulüm ve katliamı kabul etmediğini söyleyen Aysel Öğüt, "Ailem ne yaptı? 33 yıldır acısı yüreğimde. Tüm köy halkının yüreğinde. Acımız büyük ve unutulmayacak. Vartînîs'in tarihi olan bir acı. En küçük kardeşim süt emiyordu. Ne yapmış olabilir? Katliamı kabul etmiyorum. İçimdeki acıyı ancak Allah bilir" ifadelerini kullandı.

Ardından konuşan Halkların Eşitlik ve Demokrasi Partisi Muş İl Eş Başkanı İlyas Aslan, yaşanan katliamın Kürt halkında büyük etki yarattığını belirtti. Katliamın yargılamasının gerçeğe rağmen kapatıldığını ifade eden Aslan, "Katliamın zaman aşımı olmaz. Dava bugün AYM’de. AYM’den gerçekten adil bir karar bekliyor ve faillere ceza vermesini istiyoruz. Dersîm, Zilan, Roboskî katliamlarından Vartinis’e kadar hiç bir yargılama gerçekleştirilmedi. Failler cezasız kaldı. Onurlu bir barış için bu katliamların ailelerin talebi dikkate alınarak çözüme kavuşturulmalıdır. Almanya şansölyesi Brant Polonya’da Yahudi Katliamının simge yerlerinden birine giderek burada Yahudi halkından özür dilemişti. Biz de buradan başta Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan olmak üzere tüm hükümet ve devlet yetkililerine sesleniyoruz. Bu halkın taleplerine kulak verilmeli ve bu katliamlar için özür dilenmelidir. Biz bu barışı tüm Türkiye halkları için istiyoruz. Eğer bu acıyı paylaşıyorsak buna dair karşılıklı adımlar atmalıyız. Bu katliamlar bir daha yaşanmasın diye her yıl bu anmaları yapmaya devam edeceğiz" diye konuştu.

Konuşmaların ardından kitle Vartinis Müzesini ziyaret etti. Müzede katliamda yaşamını yitirenler için dua okundu. Okunan duanın ardından müzenin bahçesinde yaşamını yitirenler için saygı duruşuna duruldu. Saygı duruşunda atılan "Şehîd namirin" sloganlarının ardından, anma sona erdi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Mobilisation des lycéens de quartiers populaires : où sont les autonomes ?
content:
Depuis une semaine, les blocages d'établissement se multiplient en région parisienne. La mobilisation lycéenne s'étend désormais à toute la France (notamment à Grenoble, Lyon, et Lille). De ce qu'ils nous disent, les jeunes dénoncent des conditions d'étude déplorables, les mettant en parallèle avec des politiques répressives au sein des établissements sur les retards alors que les élèves doivent composer avec les galères de transport, sur les vêtements (crocs, voile), et sur l'usage du téléphone (“nous n'avons pas les mêmes priorités” - cf un lycéen).


Pourtant, nous n'avons pas eu vent à ce jour de tentatives sérieuses de soutien à la mobilisation de la part des autonomes. Pourquoi

 

? Leur lutte n'est pas assez pure ou ne répond pas à nos exigences

 

? Sans doute cela résulte-t-il plutôt de notre séparation sociale et raciale, c'est-à-dire de classe, avec la jeunesse des quartiers ghettoïsées de la République.


Il s'agit pourtant simplement d'y aller et d'essayer de réellement comprendre. De quoi ont-ils besoin

 

? Allons leur demander. Comment les aider

 

? Allons voir ce qu'ils font et disent. Qu'attendons-nous

 

? Déjà une semaine que le mouvement a débuté, avec des centaines de jeunes en action et une répression policière qui n'est que trop familière aux habitants des quartiers populaires : arrestations, tirs de lacrymo et de

LBD

, saturation de l'espace public par la police.


De ce que les jeunes nous disent, ils cherchent du soutien, notamment financier et face à la répression policière et judiciaire. En parallèle, les militants professionnels type

RP


NPA

 et

LFI

 sont au rendez-vous pour les soutenir (présence médiatique mais aussi sur le terrain). Que pouvons-nous proposer de mieux est une question à discuter, même si c'est une question qui préoccupe peu les lycéens eux-mêmes. Ce qu'ils veulent, c'est du changement, et c'est la question centrale qu'ils se posent à l'heure actuelle. Nous sommes en retard, ne loupons pas le rdv.


A Utrillo, les élèves ont écrit ce communiqué, que nous transmettons tel quel pour témoigner du ras-le-bol général dans les bahuts :


"Bonjour à tous et à toutes aujourd'hui nous, élèves du lycée Maurice Utrillo, nous nous révoltons aujourd'hui pour nos droits. Toute l'année nous travaillons dans de mauvaises conditions, vous nous forcez à nous lever tôt pour au final avoir un manque de personnel. Aujourd'hui nous nous révoltons pour les bonnes causes :


 on a des profs racistes sexistes,

 les toilettes insalubres et punaise de lit,

 la cantine, on mange de la merde


et lorsque nous nous plaignons on nous dit je cite «

 

si on est pas content nous avons qu'à rester chez nous

 

».


Nos emplois du temps on n'en parle même pas des élèves assis sur une chaise de 8h à 19h vous trouver ça normal

 

? Le lycée s'effondre sous vos yeux mais vous préférez vous préoccuper de nos téléphones et comment nous nous habillons. Vous trouvez ça normal vous

 

?"

title: Blocchi nei licei in Francia: la protesta continua e si espande
content:
Da meno di una settimana in Francia tutti i licei di periferia di Parigi e di altre grandi città sono bloccati dai picchetti degli studenti che, insieme a professori e assistenti all’educazione, hanno messo al centro la questione della formazione.


Tutto è partito da Créteil dove i professori hanno organizzato uno sciopero e gli studenti si sono uniti alle rivendicazioni. 


Ciò che viene espresso è una mancanza di mezzi e di risorse per i licei di periferia, l’insufficienza di personale oltre agli edifici degradati, ma viene anche portata una feroce critica sulla qualità della formazione e sulle possibilità lavorative inesistenti a seguito del diploma. Queste proteste hanno visto immediatamente una diffusione significativa, anche le università si sono unite ai blocchi, inoltre i sindacati confederali e, ancorché il governo, sono stati obbligati a prendere in considerazione le rivendicazioni. 


La risposta muscolare delle forze di polizia non si è fatta attendere con arresti, fermi e feriti gravi, oltre a cariche all’ingresso delle scuole da parte dei CRS. E’ interessante notare anche la presenza di diversi consiglieri di La France Insoumise sui blocchi, a partire dal sindaco Bally Bagayoko di Saint Denis. 


Ne abbiamo parlato con un professore di un liceo di periferia di Parigi.

content:

Depuis mardi, iels subissent une répression féroce et brutale pour le seul motif de s'être mobilisé-e-s contre l'austérité, la sélection à l'université et l'état policier. author: labor4pal
title: Over 200 organisations across more than 60 countries unite in Global Mobilisation for Palestine on 10 October (Middle East Monitor)
content:
LONDON — More than 200 civil society organisations, trade unions, student federations, human rights networks and grassroots groups across six continents will mobilise for Palestine on Saturday, 10 October, in a coordinated day of action spanning more than 60 countries.

Convened by the Global Alliance for Palestine, with the support of the Anti-Apartheid Movement (AAM) and the Global Coalition against Occupation of Palestine (SANED), this coordinated action seeks to create a unified, direct civil intervention intended to interrupt public complicity and demand systemic accountability against Israel’s war crimes and crimes against humanity. The Global Day of Action brings together markedly different forms of mobilisation under a shared international framework.

The scale of the mobilisation is reflected not only in the number of countries taking part, but in the variety of actions being organised. From major demonstrations in cities including London, Sydney/Warrane, Cape Town, São Paulo, Rabat, Quito, Mexico City, Istanbul, Santiago, Reykjavík and Bangkok, to blockades and interventions targeting government and commercial sites, multi-day cultural programmes, teach-ins, film screenings, vigils and student-led educational actions, the mobilisation will take markedly different forms across the countries taking part.

In Athens, Modena and Kuala Lumpur programmes will extend over several days and include cultural sit-ins, public teach-ins and visual projections. Elsewhere, mass street mobilisations will take place alongside locally organised community, cultural and educational actions, from film screenings in Nigeria and commemorative vigils in the Democratic Republic of Congo to student-led educational activities in Trinidad and Tobago. Other participating groups are planning direct civil interventions around government institutions, public spaces, companies and financial institutions linked by organisers to military supply chains.

READ: Global Alliance for Palestine unveils legislative advocacy initiative ahead of October day of action

The 10 October mobilisation connects movements already organising for Palestine in their own countries, bringing ongoing local campaigns together through a coordinated global weekend of action by providing a shared framework through which organisations can act in ways that reflect their own political and social contexts. This is intended to make visible both the scale of existing Palestine solidarity organising and the connections between movements operating across different regions.

The mobilisation is organised around two linked calls: Defend the Land and End the Genocide, addressing both Israel’s ongoing assault on Gaza and escalating state-sponsored settler violence, land seizures and military raids across the occupied West Bank. Organisers cite official records showing at least 73,000 Palestinians killed in Gaza, while published independent studies have reported substantially higher estimates.

‘After three years of relentless genocide and mounting state-sponsored settler violence, the fiction of restraint and the hollow promises of international diplomacy stand completely exposed. 10 October is a decisive intervention built upon the tireless work of our global movement. We are assembling across every continent under one clear mandate: to defend the land, end the genocide, halt military supply lines, and enforce universal international law.’

Dr. Anas Altikriti, Secretary-General, Global Alliance for Palestine

Alongside public mobilisation, the Global Alliance for Palestine is also calling for coordinated legislative action. Participating organisations have taken up the campaign by calling on lawmakers to receive constituent delegations, submit parliamentary inquiries on arms exports, push for emergency debates, and support arms, energy and trade restrictions against Israel.

Participating organisations include established anti-war, Palestine solidarity, human rights and grassroots organisations from across the globe. Participants include the Stop The War Coalition and Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament in the United Kingdom; the Federation of Palestinian Entities of Latin America; the Australian Palestine Advocacy Network; Viva Palestina Malaysia and MyCare in Southeast Asia; CODEPINK and Labor for Palestine in North America; and the Palestine Solidarity Alliance in South Africa.

title: Protests for Kurdish-language education continue in Rojava
content:
The protests against restrictions on Kurdish-language education in Rojava, which have been continuing for weeks, are ongoing. In Girkê Legê and Rimêlan, students boycotted classes. In Qamişlo, Til Temir, and Dirbêsiyê, students, teachers, and education workers also protested for the right to mother-tongue education.


The protests are directed against a decision by the Education Ministry of the Islamist transitional government in Damascus to limit Kurdish in schools to three hours of instruction per week. Protesters are demanding the continuation of Kurdish-language education and constitutional recognition of Kurdish in Syria.


Trilingual statement in Qamişlo


In Qamişlo, students and staff from the Şehîd Şervan, Canşêr, Dilxwaz, Heqî, and Omîd schools gathered in front of Canşêr School. A joint statement was read out in Kurdish, Arabic, and English. Student Mêrva Emo read the Kurdish version, teacher Wasil Esaed the Arabic version, and teacher Rojîn Mihemed Mûsa the English version.


In the statement, the students referred to the decades-long repression of the Kurdish population and the achievements of the Rojava Revolution. They described the current decisions as a continuation of a policy aimed at erasing Kurdish history and identity. They said that reducing Kurdish-language instruction was a first step in this direction.


At the same time, the students emphasized that their protest was not directed against other languages. Their aim, they said, was to protect their own language. They called on the relevant authorities to make their demands public and work toward the constitutional recognition of Kurdish in Syria. “Education in the Kurdish language is our natural right,” student Hêlîn Iniz said. She called for all teaching materials to be made fully available in Kurdish.


Protests in Til Temir and Dirbêsiyê


Protests against the restriction of Kurdish-language education to three hours per week were also held in and around Til Temir. At Al-Mansaf School in the northern countryside, teachers and students demanded that the Kurdish population’s right to mother-tongue education be guaranteed. They called for Kurdish to be taught on an academic basis in educational institutions, while also protecting Kurdish literature and cultural heritage.


In the town of al-Qaracina, Kongra Star supported the demands with a separate statement. Speaking in front of the women’s organization’s center, board member Îbtîsam El Şahîn emphasized the importance of language for identity, culture, and social heritage. Kurdish children, she said, must have the right to receive their education in their mother tongue.


In Dirbêsiyê, students from Şehîd Roza Cûdî School joined the protests. In a statement read out by Leyla Îsmaîl, they reaffirmed their right to mother-tongue education and called for the protection of the Kurdish language.

author: Rana Mamdouh
title: Prisoner protests, lack of readiness delay enactment of new Criminal Procedures Law
content:
The Criminal Procedures Code’s deferred enactment,

approved

 by Parliament yesterday, was attributed by MPs and the government to a lack of preparedness.

 However, parliamentary and legal sources told Mada Masr the impact of the law’s enactment on the hundreds of detainees being held in remand could be among the reasons that led to the last-minute postponement. 


The bill to postpone the law’s enactment, brought forth by the Nation’s Future Party, which is close to state authorities, proposed an amendment to the 2025 bill to delay enforcement until October 2027, replacing an article in the original text that had set October 1 as the operative date.


According to Parliament, the decision to enforce the new bill next year was taken primarily out of concern for the readiness of the digital system, which the law stipulates be used for judicial notifications and remote court proceedings.


During yesterday’s Legislative Committee meeting ahead of the plenary session vote on the postponement draft, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Hany Hanna

said

 the ministry backed the bill in order to allow for greater preparedness ahead of implementation, noting that “some courts have been prepared, while others, such as felony appeal courts, still need preparation.”


But the Justice Ministry had issued several decisions in August which indicated its readiness to implement the digital system.

On August 30, the ministry

announced

 that the required courtroom and training facility adjustments to implement the new system were completed in coordination with the courts of appeal and the Lawyers Syndicate.

 


Later, on September 9, the ministry

announced

 that criminal court judges, clerks and lawyers within different jurisdictions were fully trained to use the digital system.


It seems the bill’s postponement had causes beyond the system’s readiness. Speaking on condition of anonymity, a source in the General Secretariat of the House of Representatives said the postponement was based on security reports and recommendations from the National Security Agency.

According to these reports, there are certain clauses within the law whose implementation needed more time, such as

Article 363

, which puts some limitations on the duration of remand detention, in accordance with

Article 124.


Article 124 of the law sets the maximum total limit for remand detention at four months for misdemeanors, 12 months for felonies and 18 months if the maximum punishment for the crime is life imprisonment or the death penalty. 


According to the source, these limits could have immediate effects on current prisoners, requiring judicial and investigative authorities to release hundreds of individuals who are being held in remand in excess of these time limits. 


Nabih al-Genady,

 human rights lawyer and founder of the

Tbian for Rights and Freedoms

, pointed to mass protests by remand detainees in terrorism cases that took place in the Badr Court last week as the reason behind the decision to postpone the bill.

 Despite calling the government and Parliament’s stated reasons for the postponement  “genuine and positive,” he said they are not the primary cause. 


Genady recounted what he personally witnessed in Badr Court at the Badr Prison Complex during a series of terrorism trial sessions last week. Over three consecutive sessions, defendants protested in court against the repeated renewal of their remand terms. Confined to their dock, defendants banged on the glass at the end of the first session, chanting “freedom,” as Judge Wagdy Abdel Moneim left the courtroom. On the second day, they smashed the cameras inside the glass dock, still chanting “freedom.” On the third day, they also banged on the glass as Abdel Moneim took the bench.


According to Genady, the judge asked the defendants to be silent for the hearing to begin, but they continued to protest. He then asked a lawyer to enter the dock and calm the prisoners down, but none stepped forward. The judge then turned to three defendants in the dock who are also lawyers and asked them to calm their fellow detainees. As lawyers, he said, they understood the gravity of disrupting proceedings and insulting the judiciary. He warned that if the others did not stop, he would sentence everyone in the dock to jail.
