author: admin
title: KIITG Report September 2026
content:
Brenna Yellowthunder (Lead Coordinator, KIITG) spoke at the Oregon Data Center Moratorium Rally on Sept. 8 in Oregon’s capitol, Salem. Alongside Governor Kotek, they emphasized the effect hyper scale data centers have on rivers and salmon, a cornerstone of local tribes culture. They also joined the lobby day, urging state legislators to support a 3-year moratorium on data centers. The event was organized by the Columbia Riverkeepers, Food and Water Watch, and more.

Following the largest pipeline spill in Wisconsin last month, by Canadian pipeline giant Embridge, the Bad River Band of Lake Superior Ojibwe declared a disaster for their reservation after the spill, and Chairperson Liz Arbuckle said, “This is what we said would happen.”

The break triggered a massive spill of 1.3 million gallons of natural gas liquids. Federal data shows the leak is the largest reported oil and gas spill ever in Wisconsin.

Michigan’s 12 federally recognized tribes led the Mackinac Bridge Walk, with several tribal chairs, chiefs, and presidents joining together to activate the ancestral Three Fires Confederacy’s first collective call to action.

On Labor Day, Sept. 7, 2026, roughly 34,000 people participated in the Mackinac Bridge Walk, with Michigan tribes leading a unified stand against Line 5.

Arbuckle said the tribe had warned that the reroute would still put their reservation at risk. “This is our UnCeded Territory,” she said. “This is where our people have always hunted, fished, gathered and lived and all of that’s at risk.” Tribal leaders say the incident underscores a truth the Anishinaabe have voiced for years: Enbridge’s safety practices rely on luck, not containment.

The Mackinac Bridge Walk was a ceremony, not just a demonstration, to honor the responsibility to the water and remind the world that Anishinaabe people are still here, still protecting their homelands.

Joe Bates, an environmental activist and member of the Bad River Band of Lake Superior Ojibwe, captured drone footage of the leak after hearing reports from community members.

We ask you to consider supporting the local community on the ground, who has asked us to share this fundraiser for an infrared drone. Observers need this equipment to document pipeline leaks and highlight the risks to Indigenous waterways. Joe Bates is one of the people who broke the story about Enbridge’s leaking pipeline with his drone footage. He has frequently used drone footage to document conditions along Enbridge’s Line 5 corridor, including construction, erosion concerns, and suspected drilling-fluid releases. But an infrared drone would let observers see what the naked eye cannot: gas plumes, thermal anomalies, and leaks that would otherwise go undetected.

The community is asking for support so that the documentation can continue. Please donate if you can. Share if you cannot.

Click here to make a secure donation to support the community.

author: Thomas Klikauer
title: German Natural Gas Politics – Profits or Ingenuity
content:
According to the IEA‘s global electricity mix, non-renewable, unsustainable and highly polluting fossil fuels still make up 57% of electricity production with the much talked about oil – Strait of Hormuz, etc. – being just 2%. Oil is used to make petrol for cars still running on combustion engines, but it is not much used to make electricity.

By contrast, renewables come in at an ever-increasing percentage with wind and solar are 17% and hydropower 14%. Not to be forgotten: the atomic power of Chernobyl and Fukushima, at 9%.

In Germany, solar makes up 33%, coal 27%, natural gas 13%, wind 11%, biomass 9% and others 7%. According to Germany’s “windmesse.de”, Germany runs on 62% renewable energy for electricity generation. Sadly, natural gas still made up 13.4%.

Worldwide, the share of natural gas in global electricity generation fell from 23.9% in 2020 to 21.8% in 2025. Still, gas remains the world’s second-largest source of electricity generation with a 22% share of total output, behind only coal at 33%. Gas makes up a much bigger slice in places like the US (40%) than in, for example, India (2%) or China (3%).

Despite all this, Germany is at a critical point in its energy transition towards renewables. While Germany’s conservative government fancies building new gas-fired power plants, this raises a fundamental question: is Germany building a bridge to a carbon-neutral age?

A recent study by the highly respected Wuppertal Institute (WI) debunks the conservative government’s fairytale of gas-fired power plants as an alternative energy source. The study proves that Germany does not need fossil-fuel power plants. The results are clear: there is a strong mandate for sustainable energy generation.

Before Germany invests billions in new gas-fired power plants, it needs energy efficiency and the systematic reduction of non-sustainable energy sources. In other words, each megawatt Germany does not have to produce is the cheapest and cleanest contribution to security of supply and to sustainability.

New capacities may only come in as a subordinate option. The conservative government’s “business as usual” reliance on fossils like gas is, as a general rule, neither necessary nor useful. Climate protection occurs where power is essentially solar, wind, biomass and green hydrogen.

In addition, any construction of new power plants must follow strict decarbonisation pathways. Whether and how many new power plants are needed depends on many mutually influencing factors and cannot be answered definitively.

It is clear that Germany needs far fewer new power plants than Katherina Reiche plans. Reiche is Germany’s staunchly conservative minister for energy, at the Bundesministerium für Wirtschaft und Energie (BMWE).

Evil heretics might be tempted to say she is Merz‘s pretty face of neoliberal fundamentalism, versed in repeating the central lines of Hayek’s catechism. Given current trends, the plans of the ultra-neoliberal Reiche are not necessary. Vast sums can be saved by not constructing new fossil-fuel power stations.

If, for example, load-reducing efficiency measures in German industry move forward, Germany avoids costs while reducing CO2.

Meanwhile, the corporate-media-engineered “debate” about the security of energy supply is, more often than not, illogical and based on fear rather than reality. It follows the logic of fear, not the logic of a sustainable energy mix.

In particular, Minister Reiche suggests that without massive construction of new gas-fired power plants in Germany, the lights will literally go out. This is first-class fearmongering of the kind that, during the 1970s, gave Germany plenty of expensive but rather unnecessary atomic power stations, whose radioactive waste is still looking for a place to be dumped.

By contrast, a modern, digital and renewable energy system, the WI argues, is highly flexible and capable of mastering virtually all future challenges. Still, bottlenecks may occur once every couple of years.

Germany still has so-called “cold dark doldrums” [Dunkelflauten], when there are many days with neither wind nor sun. For these rare cases, a cascade of flexibility options (efficiency measures, load reductions without restricting production, and green backup power plants) can be used to cover Germany’s energy needs.

Recently, the environmental NGO Greenpeace introduced a new and as yet hardly discussed proposal into the German debate: the “derating of loads” in Germany’s industry. It …

author: Frey Blake-Pijogge
title: In a warming Arctic, Inuit bear guards protect communities
content:
This story is published through the Indigenous News Alliance.


After retiring from a long career as a conservation officer with the Canadian government, Derrick Pottle devoted himself to guiding people on the land, carving, hunting, and training bear guards.


Pottle, an elder and skilled guide from the Inuit community of Tikigâksuagusik in Nunatsiavut, founded BearSafe Planning in 2005. The program trains and certifies students to guard against the polar bears and black bears found throughout northern Labrador. The three-day course is advertised as offering “safety, protection, confidence in bear country.”


More than two decades later, that work has taken on renewed urgency. As climate change reshapes the Arctic — particularly the sea ice polar bears rely on to travel and hunt — Inuit are seeing the animals at different times of year and in places they rarely encountered before. Pottle says those changes are increasing the need for people who know

how to keep people and bears safe

. That, he said, is “the whole objective of the course.”


Graduates of the program keep watch for bears to prevent encounters and learn to recognize signs that a bear is not comfortable. “They may feel threatened, they may feel intimidated, and they may even charge or attack you,” Pottle said. He teaches students “how to recognize those signs, how to prepare yourself for them, the tools you have to use to do your job.”


Canadian officials say encounters between people and polar bears

are becoming more likely

 as a lengthening ice-free season keeps bears on land longer. Inuit and Cree communities have reported polar bears appearing more frequently and in places where they were once rare. Researchers have

linked the increase to several factors

, including longer ice-free periods, changes in bear abundance and condition, and growing human activity in polar bear habitat. 


Pottle developed BearSafe Planning’s training program with input from groups that included Parks Canada, conservationists, Inuit elders, and academics. It started “out of a necessity,” Pottle said, after the creation of Tongait KakKasuangita SilakKijapvinga, (Torngat Mountains National Park) under the 2005 Labrador Inuit Land Claims Agreement. 


“They needed bear guards,” Pottle said. We didn’t have trainers in Nunatsiavut at the time. Somebody had to do it.”


Inuk elder Derrick Pottle founded BearSafe Planning in 2005 to keep people and bears safe. That work has taken on renewed urgency as climate change reshapes the Arctic and encounters with bears grow more common.


Frey Blake-Pijogge / IndigiNews


The Arctic is warming

nearly four times faster

 than the rest of the planet. As climate change remakes landscapes across the North, the need for guards is only for “all species of bears,” Pottle said. 


“We’re seeing more and more bears now in this time of our lives than we ever saw before,” he said.  “People are seeing polar bears in this part of Inuit Nunangat — where polar bears used to travel north late in the spring — and now are staying all summer long.”


The province’s Endangered Species Act lists polar bears as “vulnerable,” while the federal government deems them a “species of special concern.” Sixty to 80 per cent of the world’s polar bear population lives in Canada, according to Environment and Climate Change Canada. The massive carnivores, which can weigh as much as 1,400 pounds, rely upon sea ice to travel, mate, and hunt. “Climate change is the main threat to polar bears,” the agency notes.


Becoming a bear guard can offer employment opportunities, but also can be used for personal safety. “Lots of people just use the bear guard course for their own personal protection when they’re out on the land with their families fishing, hunting and participating in Inuit lifestyle.”


Sherri Wolfrey, a mother of four, is a trained bear guard in Tikigâksuagusik. She recounted how, in 2015, she became “interested in the program and just thought ‘OK, maybe someday I might want to try for a job that involves bear monitoring.’”


Wolfrey is the secretary of Northern Lights Academy and uses her training when she’s out on the land. Last year, she put her certification to work professionally for the first time, when she was contracted as a bear guard in Akami-Uapishkᵁ-KakKasuak (Mealy Mountains National Park Reserve). “Especially up in that area in the bottom of the Mealy’s, it was so beautiful up there,” she told IndigiNews.

author: Unknown
title: 'Aile Sağlığı Merkezleri, satılacak bina değil, sağlık merkezidir'
content:
Eylem Nazlıer [email protected]

Türkiye’de koruyucu, birinci basamak sağlık hizmetlerinin yurttaşla buluştuğu en önemli noktalardan biri olan Aile Sağlığı Merkezlerinin (ASM) geleceği, merkezlerin fiziki koşullarından kira giderlerine, deprem güvenliğinden personel eksikliğine kadar risk altında. Kamuya ait binalarda bile kiralarına yüzde 300’e varan zamlar istenen ASM’lerde aile hekimleri zor durumda.

Birlik ve Dayanışma Sendikası Genel Başkanı Dr. Ahmet Mehlepçi, ASM’lerin mümkün olduğunca kamuya ait, depreme dayanıklı ve sağlık hizmetinin gerektirdiği fiziki standartlara uygun binalarda hizmet vermesi gerektiğine vurgu yaparak “ASM’ler yalnızca hekim, ebe ve hemşirelerin görev yaptığı binalar değildi. ASM’ler; koruyucu sağlık hizmetlerinin, gebe, bebek ve çocuk izlemlerinin, bağışıklama hizmetlerinin, kronik hastalık takiplerinin ve vatandaşın sağlık sistemiyle ilk temasının gerçekleştiği temel sağlık kuruluşlarıdır” hatırlatmasını yaptı. Bu nedenle ASM’lerin geleceğine ilişkin kararların yalnızca bina, taşınmaz veya bütçe konusu olarak değerlendirilemeyeceğini dile getiren Mehlepçi, “Konu doğrudan sağlık hizmetine erişim, hizmetin sürekliliği ve kamu yararıdır” diye konuştu.

Sağlık Bakanı Kemal Memişoğlu’nun Kasım 2025’te 1000 yeni ASM yapacaklarını açıklamasından bu yana sadece 278 ASM’nin hizmete girdiğini, 370 ASM’nin inşaatının sürdüğünü ve 352 ASM’nin proje aşamasında olduğu bilgisini veren Mehlepçi, Türkiye genelinde ise yaklaşık 8 bin 300 ASM bulunduğunu söyledi.

Yeni ASM yatırımlarının elbette önemli olduğunu belirten Mehlepçi, mevcut merkezlerin ise kentsel dönüşüm, deprem riski, yüksek kiralar veya taşınmaz satışları nedeniyle hizmet dışı kalmasının önlenmesi gerektiğini vurguladı.

Bir taraftan yeni ASM’ler yapılırken diğer taraftan mevcut merkezlerin kentsel dönüşüm, deprem riski, yüksek kiralar veya taşınmaz satışları nedeniyle hizmet dışı kalma tehlikesiyle karşı karşıya olduğuna dikkati çeken Mehlpeçi “Mart 2026’da TBMM’ye sunulan soru önergesine verilen cevapta İstanbul Kadıköy’deki 33 ASM’den 7’sinin kentsel dönüşüm nedeniyle yıkıldığı ve hizmet veremez hale geldiğini söyledi. Mahlepçi kaç yeni ASM açıldığı kadar, kaç ASM’nin kapandığı, yıkıldığı, tahliye edildiği, taşındığı veya başka bir ASM’nin içine sıkıştırıldığının da kamuoyuyla paylaşılması gerektiğini aktardı.

ASM binalarının deprem güvenliğinin de önemli bir sorun olduğunu belirten Mehlepçi, 2025 yılında yapılan bir çalışmada ASM binalarının yaklaşık üçte birinin 1999 öncesinde inşa edildiğinin ortaya çıktığını söyledi. 6 Şubat 2023 yaşanan depremlerde ortaya çıkan tablonun bu konuda vahim olduğunu hatırlatan Mehlepçi “2026 yılı başında sahadan elde edilen verilere göre Hatay’da 96 ASM konteynerlerde hizmet veriyor. 103 ASM kendi binasında hizmet vermeye devam ediyor ancak bunların bir bölümü deprem güvenliği açısından risk taşıyor. Yaklaşık 56 ASM ise tahliye veya yıkım sürecinde” dedi.

Öte yandan ASM’ler için sorunun yalnızca deprem güvenliğiyle sınırlı olmadığını, ASM’lerdeki sağlık hizmetinin niteliği ve çalışanların koşullarını etkileyen başka fiziki sorunların bulunduğunu da dile getiren Mehlepçi durumu şöyle anlattı: “Penceresi, yeterli mekanik havalandırması bulunmayan kan alma odaları, lavabosu olmayan, iki veya üç sağlık çalışanının aynı odayı kullanmak zorunda kaldığı ASM’ler de var. Hatta bazı çalışma alanları hasta mahremiyetini sağlamaya da elverişli değil.”

Yıkım veya tahliye kararı verilen merkezlerde görev yapan sağlık çalışanlarının başka bir ASM’nin mutfağına, dinlenme odasına veya ortak kullanım alanına yerleştirilerek yeni bir aile hekimliği birimi oluşturulmasının kalıcı bir çözüm olmadığının altını çizen Mehlepçi, “Bir sağlık hizmetinin verilebilmesi için yalnızca bir oda bulunması yeterli değildir. O alanın sağlık hizmetinin niteliğine, çalışan güvenliğine ve hasta mahremiyetine uygun olması gerekir” dedi.

Kamusal sağlık hizmeti sunulan ASM’lerde yükün önemli bir bölümünün aile hekimlerinin üzerine yıkıldığına ve özellikle büyükşehirlerde uygun bina bulmanın giderek zorlaştığına işaret eden Mehlepçi “Kiralar da ASM’lerin sürdürülebilirliğini tehdit eden seviyelere ulaştı. Aylık 100 bin TL ve üzerinde kira ödeyen ASM örnekleri var. Elazığ’da bazı ASM’ler yüzde 350’ye varan kira artış talepleriyle karşılaştı. ASM’ler birer ticarethane değildir. Burada yürütülen faaliyet kamu sağlık hizmetidir” uyarısını yaparak buna rağmen yüksek kira bedellerinin yanı sıra elektrik, su, doğalgaz, temizlik, bakım-onarım …

author: Lisa Song
title: New Rule Would Ban the Use of Federal Grant Money for Voter Registration Drives
content:
Advocates worry that the loss of federal funding will effectively disenfranchise many voters with disabilities.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Without Amy Miller, some elderly and disabled people wouldn’t be able to vote.

The attorney for Disability Rights Nebraska travels the state, investigating the quality of nursing homes and assisted living facilities. As she reminds the residents how they can report abuse or neglect, she also offers voter registration forms. Last month, she helped a veteran with a traumatic brain injury fill out change-of-address paperwork so he could vote in the upcoming midterm elections. “He 100% knew who he wanted to vote for,” Miller said, but he struggled to write with a pen.

Congress funds her organization’s efforts to ensure that even people who might not have access to the internet or transportation have the opportunity to participate in elections.

Now a White House proposal threatens that work.

The White House Office of Management and Budget wants to change spending rules to prohibit anyone from using federal grant money for voter registration drives or what it vaguely calls “related activities.” The office is headed by Russell Vought, who has long criticized the use of taxpayer money for voter registration efforts and who more recently used his position to cancel, freeze or redirect vast amounts of federal funding in defiance of Congress’ orders.

Miller, who has worked at her nonprofit for six years, said she’s never faced regulators wanting to impede her work.

“Shutting that down and making it more difficult for these Americans to access the ballot box is bewildering to me,” she said.

The proposal is part of the Trump administration’s broader assault on federal efforts to expand access to voting, especially among groups that have historically faced discrimination and disenfranchisement.

President Donald Trump has championed the SAVE America Act, a bill that would require people to provide documents proving their citizenship when registering to vote, and that may require everyone to deliver that proof in person, which would effectively end voter registration drives.

Last year, the Trump administration banned nongovernmental organizations from conducting registration drives at naturalization ceremonies, though the agency temporarily lifted the ban amid litigation over the policy change. The Department of Education also sent a letter to colleges and universities stating that they could not use federal work-study dollars to support voting-related work. (The directive has been contested.) Previously, those funds were used to pay students who had part-time jobs to conduct voter registration on campus and in neighboring communities.

And on the first day of Trump’s second term, the president rescinded an executive order signed by Joe Biden that had directed federal agencies to expand opportunities for registration. Biden’s order acknowledged that some Americans, including Black citizens and people with disabilities, face historic and ongoing barriers to voting access.

Neither Vought nor his office responded to ProPublica’s questions about the proposed change. But in a letter sent to state officials in 2022, he condemned Biden’s executive order as a “power grab” that would “increase voter registration and turnout, especially among Democratic Party supporters.”

Vought’s proposed change, which wouldn’t go into effect until after the 2026 midterms, could have ramifications for the next presidential election well beyond voting accessibility.

Nonprofits that receive government funds to help people sign up for Medicaid benefits, food stamps or other programs subject to the National Voter Registration Act are required to provide registration forms and help people fill them out. Like Disability Rights Nebraska, these groups would be caught between contradictory federal directives if the proposed ban is finalized.

Thousands more nonprofits receive federal funds for other services but provide voter outreach using private donations. Nonprofit experts said the confusion over which groups the ban affects and the burden of proving an organization is in compliance could lead many to pause or curb registration efforts ahead of the 2028 election. Colleges and universities that help students navigate registering to vote while away from home could be similarly affected.

author: Slingshot robot #1
title: Mental Health Reminders
content:
These are dark times. It is, in fact, the world that is crazy – despair and anxiety are natural responses to watching society destroy itself for the wealthy and powerful. But by reaching out to each other, we can find the courage to stay engaged with the world, to survive, and to fight back. Mental health and mental health crises vary a lot between people, and are often intertwined with class, race, gender, and activism. These suggestions are generic, but may be useful for yourself or others. If you find yourself or someone you love having delusional thinking or consider self-harm or other violence, these suggestions probably aren’t enough. Remember that it is okay to reach out for professional help!

• Our brains are connected to our bodies, so physical health can help with mental distress. Eating healthy food on a regular schedule and getting enough sleep are necessary for mental stability and sustained activism. Exercise, dance, and physical movement help, too. So can fresh air and having a stable, calming place to stay. Try to recognize if you’re missing one of these, and if that’s causing distress.

• An important component of mental health is the ability to know ourselves, understand our needs, and be able to talk about them to the other people in our lives. This can be really challenging and can often take guidance from others who have learned how to do it with one another.

• It can help to have language for mental crisis that feels comfortable and makes more sense than the dominant medical language. Transmission of language often happens in groups. Talk to friends about the different ways you can feel “off” and develop your own shorthand to describe them.

• Joining a mutual support group of peers listening to and helping peers as equals can be validating, while not necessarily endorsing your feelings. You can form one yourself or join an ongoing group.

• If possible, find a therapist or counselor who supports your self-determination. Ask about confidentiality if someone else — such as your parents, boss, or governmental program — is paying.

• Drugs and alcohol usually make mental health problems worse.

• Psychiatric drugs such as those for depression or bipolar disorder can help some people reduce distress and maintain stability, while other people with similar symptoms may experience distress or harm from the same drugs. Figuring out what works for you can be a process because people differ.

• Nature and wilderness can be our greatest healers. Spend some time outside the city to get centered. Get away from pollution, which is in itself mind-altering. Look up “Ecopsychology” to learn more.

• Allow social, political, and environmental crises unfolding around you to radicalize you, rather than driving you to despair. Actually articulate the world you would want to be living in; work towards it. Remember change happens collectively – look for ways to plug in. Small acts like talking to neighbors or submitting art to Slingshot can help you feel political agency between larger or more radical actions.

• Many communities have 24 hour a day crisis hotlines or crisis centers. Call 800-SUICIDE if you’re thinking about killing yourself or 800 646-HOPE to reach a rape crisis line for survivors of sexual violence. Warning: if you call and say you want to kill yourself police may arrive at your door.

• Things that can help your mental health day-to-day might not be as effective when you’re in crisis. Review the above reminders, and try to eat, exercise, journal, etc., but it’s okay if that isn’t helping.

• Distracting yourself from depressed or anxious thoughts can help: listening to music, making art, washing dishes, doing a project alone or with others. Embrace sensation: use your hands or massage your fingers. Hold onto an ice cube, or take a hot or cold shower. Give yourself time to gather resources.

• Some current emotional crises may be caused by traumas from the past, which may need to be emotionally and consciously processed in order not to keep recurring; that processing might take time.

• When in crisis, it may help to realize that the feeling will eventually pass and your life will begin to feel manageable and meaningful again later. Depression may feel like lack of feelings and a lack of connection to feeling. Anxiety may feel like rapidly cycling concern for what might happen. Both inhibit your ability to perceive and understand the world correctly. Your perceptions of hopelessness are NOT …

content:

We join women, girls, and human rights defenders across Africa and the globe on this 28th day of September to commemorate the 2026 International Safe Abortion Day, reaffirming a simple truth: safe abortion is essential healthcare.

We are reminded of the transformative power of the Protocol to the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights on the Rights of Women in Africa (the Maputo Protocol), which is lauded as one of the most progressive and comprehensive legal instruments for the promotion and protection of women’s rights globally, particularly in the area of sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR). Adopted in 2003 by the African Union, the Protocol goes beyond existing international human rights standards by explicitly articulating a wide array of SRHR protections that are often left ambiguous or unstated in other international and regional human rights instruments.

Article 14 of the Maputo Protocol guarantees women’s rights to health and reproductive autonomy, including the right to control their fertility, decide on family size and spacing, and to choose their method of contraception. Most critically, Article 14 makes the Maputo Protocol the first and only binding international human rights treaty to explicitly guarantee access to safe medical abortion in specific circumstances—namely, where the continued pregnancy endangers the mental or physical health of the mother or the life of the mother or the fetus, or in cases of sexual assault, rape, or incest. This Article also mandates access to comprehensive reproductive health services, including antenatal care, safe delivery, family planning, and sexual and reproductive health education. In doing so, the Protocol moves abortion access from a matter left to state discretion to one of binding treaty obligation — a distinction that remains central to the advocacy for its full domestication across the continent.

Currently, 46 of the 55 African states have ratified the Maputo Protocol, while nine – Burundi, Chad, Egypt, Eritrea, Madagascar, Morocco, Niger, Somalia, and Sudan – are yet to ratify it. Bringing these final states on board is vital because over 150 million African women and girls currently live outside the protective legal framework of the Maputo Protocol.

Despite its progressiveness, 9 out of the 46 member states have placed reservations to various provisions of the Maputo Protocol, with Article 14 being the most reserved provision. A reservation lowers the minimum human rights standards contained in a particular treaty for the reserving states and enables the reserving states to escape accountability for human rights violations.

Currently, Africa accounts for 70% of global maternal deaths. These preventable deaths are compounded by persistent gaps in access to sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) services, which are essential to safeguarding the lives and dignity of women, children and adolescents. Unsafe abortions continue to claim the lives of thousands of African women and girls, while millions more are left with severe injuries and long-term health complications. According to the World Health Organization, nearly half of all abortions worldwide are unsafe, with Sub-Saharan Africa carrying the highest burden. The Guttmacher Institute further estimates that three-quarters of all abortions in the region are unsafe, making unsafe abortion one of the …

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Quebec Liberal Sandrine Rioux prioritizes health care, housing, cost of living
content:
Nunatsiaq News reached out to each candidate running in the Ungava riding ahead of Quebec’s Oct. 5 provincial election. Here’s what Quebec Liberal Party candidate Sandrine Rioux had to share with us.


Quebec Liberal Party candidate Sandrine Rioux said the reason she decided to run for office is simple: she wants to help people.


“My main goal is to help people, to be there, to be present, and to write good legislation at the National Assembly of Quebec,” said Rioux, speaking to Nunatsiaq News Tuesday from Chibougimou, where she was born and raised.


She’s among five candidates running in Ungava, the largest riding in the province geographically.


Her main priorities are improving access to health care, constructing more homes, addressing the cost of living and ensuring profits generated from resource development benefit communities.


Her party has a goal of building 100,000 homes per year in Quebec, she said, and wants to implement deadlines for housing authorities to encourage quicker development.


Each community, no matter how remote, should have a baseline 24-7 access to front-line health care services like doctors, nurses and pharmacists, she said. Telemedicine can fill gaps when specialists aren’t available.


At least five per cent of Quebec’s health budget should be dedicated to prevention, she said, and if elected, she wants to reduce Nunavik’s reliance on fly-in-fly-out health-care professionals.


Rioux has been involved with the Liberal party since 2019 and was president of its Ungava association.


She has a degree in business technology management from Université de Sherbrooke and a professional background in business analysis and marketing.


But she always held an interest in politics, she said, working for Élections Québec during the 2018 provincial election as an administrative assistant. It was one of her first jobs out of university and one that allowed her to visit each of Nunavik’s villages.


So far during the campaign, Rioux has visited Chapais, Chisasibi, Oujé-Bougoumou, Matagami, Mistissini, Radison, Waskaganish and Waswanipi. Travelling to Nunavik isn’t in the budget, but she said Kuujjuaq is first on her list if she gets elected.


“I really genuinely hope, if the people trust me, and invest in me, to be able to represent them at the National Assembly,” she said. “I want to make sure the lines of communication are always open.”

author: Unknown
title: Pourquoi et comment brûler la psychiatrie ? Discussion pour des perspectives antipsy anticarcérales
content:
Le mercredi 23 septembre 2026, l'Assemblée Anticarcérale Paris & Environs organise une discussion antipsychiatrie anticarcérale à la bibliothèque queer anarchiste la

BARK

, qui se trouve à la Parole Errante à Montreuil.


Mercredi 23 Septembre à 18h : Discussion antipsy anticarcérale à la

BARK

 

!


Depuis son lancement, l'Assemblée Anticarcérale Paris & Environs s'efforce de s'organiser contre l'enfermement psychiatrique. La psychiatrie nous apparaît naturellement comme un maillon important de la domination : que ce soit par les moyens par lesquels elle enferme des personnes, par son utilisation répressive et pacificatrice dans les autres lieux d'enfermement, ou par ses dispositifs carcéraux de contrôle dans la société. Dans une optique de s'informer sur les luttes contre la psychiatrie et d'y intervenir, on veut prendre en compte le fait que nous n'avons pas toustes les mêmes expériences et connaissances sur le sujet.


L'idée de cette discussion est donc de poser des bases, ensemble, sur ce qu'est l'antipsy pour nous, que ce soit pour découvrir ses courants ou pour développer ce qui nous parle dedans. Quels sont les dispositifs d'enfermement de la psychiatrie

 

? Pourquoi viser à sa destruction

 

? Quels liens faisons-nous depuis nos perspectives anticarcérales

 

? Comment la domination psychiatrique est elle étendue ces dernières années

 

? Comment s'organiser pour la brûler

 

?


Une base d'infokiosque sera aussi proposée pour approfondir certaines questions spécifiques, mais il ne faut pas hésiter à apporter toute brochure que l'on voudrait discuter, conseiller, diffuser, etc.


La discussion commencera dès 18h à la bibliothèque queer anarchiste la

BARK

 (5 rue francois debergue à la Parole Errante à Montreuil, en passant par le jardin à gauche de la librairie Michèle Firk). La permanence de la bibliothèque commence elle dès 16h, et l'infokiosque y sera installé en avance

 

!

author: Rana Mamdouh
title: Future of Egypt enters healthcare: Govt, military hospitals to serve tourist dollars
content:
In its first public move into the healthcare sector, the Future of Egypt for Sustainable Development Authority

unveiled

 last week the launch of the Future of Egypt Medical Alliance Company.


According to reports announcing the authority’s participation in this year’s Egy Health Exhibition and Conference, the company is chaired by Major General Khaled Oweida, the physician and former director of the Air Force Specialized Hospital, and is set to provide specialized medical services, training and research, digital and technological healthcare solutions, as well as medical tourism services.


In the first phase of its operations, the reports stated, the company will incorporate the International Medical Center and the Air Force Specialized Hospital, both of which are affiliated with the Armed Forces. The two facilities provide medical services to military personnel through the Armed Forces’ health insurance system, while also treating civilians for a fee or through

contracts

 with the Universal Health Insurance system or other entities.


The company plans to expand gradually by bringing additional facilities and hospitals under its umbrella.


This year’s Egy Health Exhibition and Conference, held September 15-17. Courtesy: Menassat website


Future of Egypt

also announced

 that the company was taking part in the exhibition, which was held from September 15 to 17, in order to “showcase its integrated medical system’s components and the range of specialties, services and advanced solutions it offers.”


Coverage of the exhibition focused on what media outlets described as the Future of Egypt Medical Alliance Company’s vision for developing medical tourism — mapping the international patient journey that runs from pre-travel consultations and case assessment, through travel, reception, accommodation and translation, to post-treatment follow-up.


According to media

coverage

, the company intends to pursue this by building a network of medical partners and tourism operators and establishing cooperation channels with entities involved in medical tourism and target markets.


Steps to foster a state vision for medical tourism date back to at least 2017, when Prime Minister Mostafa Madbuly

established

 the Supreme Committee for Medical Tourism by decree to be headed by the health minister. The decree set out several objectives, including implementing the medical tourism components of the Egypt Vision 2030, restoring the confidence of foreign patients, attracting Arab and foreign investment to establish projects serving medical tourism and involving civil society and the private sector.


During a committee meeting in December 2024, chaired by Madbuly, Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar

said

 the committee’s technical secretariat had begun preparing a unified national strategy for medical tourism. According to a Cabinet

statement

, the committee had contacted all relevant entities involved in health tourism in Egypt to solicit their proposals for the strategy.


At the same meeting, Madbuly said that it was agreed to establish a national council for medical tourism, with a technical secretariat tasked with following up on all matters related to this portfolio.


The council was established by a prime ministerial decree in June 2025. In its first meeting,

chaired

by the health minister, a proposal setting out criteria for service providers to join the national health tourism platform was reviewed. The providers included healthcare, hotel and hospitality, transportation and logistics services.


A senior Health Ministry official told Mada Masr on condition of anonymity that the Future of Egypt Medical Alliance Company is primarily focused on providing treatment to tourists: “[The company] is targeting Gulf nationals and foreign tourists in Egypt whose treatment costs are paid in dollars by international insurance companies.”


As an example, the official said, “if we perform open heart surgery for LE200,000 for someone insured in Egypt, [Future of Egypt’s] hospitals would perform the same operation for a foreign tourist staying in, say, Sharm el-Sheikh, and their insurance company would pay US$10,000. And we benefit from the difference in the exchange rate.”


According to the official, one of the main criteria for selecting hospitals to be transferred to Future of Egypt is having a helipad equipped to receive emergency cases, as well as facilities equipped for major surgeries and subspeciality medical care …

author: dev
title: Le sacrifice du ciel
content:
Le philosophe Mohamed Amer Meziane publie son troisième livre,

Le Sacrifice du ciel. Une autre histoire de la raison

, qui vient rouvrir, reprendre et poursuivre le cycle ouvert par

Des empires sous la terre

 (2021) et

Au bord des mondes

 (2023).


Le thème du « sacrifice du ciel » fait écho à ceux de la sécularisation, de la mort de Dieu et du « désenchantement du monde ». Ces lieux communs, au sein de l'attirail des pensées critiques, ressemblent à des enjeux à la fois familiers et méconnus.


À voir lundi 21 septembre à partir de 20h


Les « statuaires de la pensée », expression du livre renvoyant au panthéon fatigué des « grands auteurs » européens, ne nous ont légué que peu d'outils pour y faire face. Il se pourrait, en plus, que ces thèmes « biens connus » (c'est-à-dire peut-être totalement impensés) aient obscurci la compréhension qu'on a de ces grands auteurs eux-mêmes. C'est la conséquence d'un des points principaux du livre : l'

orientalisme

, sous la forme de la critique historique des textes sacrés, a joué un rôle matriciel pour la production du savoir occidentalisé.


À partir de là, l'enquête donne lieu à une autre histoire de la philosophie : au prisme de l'orientalisme, Spinoza, Kant et Hegel apparaissent sous un autre jour. Leurs façons de penser la religion, ses rapports à la pensée et à la politique, est très loin cependant de s'être cantonnée au seul domaine de la philosophie. Elles participent de mouvements qui les précèdent et leur survivent, et qui constituent le sol sur lequel se sont déployées les sciences humaines et sociales « modernes ». Un ensemble de mythes vivaces s'ancrent dans cette histoire : le christianisme comme seule religion de la sortie de la religion, le protestantisme comme religion du monde moderne, le monothéisme comme origine de la violence, le fanatisme comme caractéristique des « religions de la Loi »…


Le Sacrifice du ciel

 se présente comme une critique des savoirs, une « histoire souterraine » de la connaissance. Celle-ci ne se contente pas d'en exhumer les marges, mais entend ressaisir l'héritage d'un centre occulté en montrant que la raison n'est pas « occidentale ». Se pose alors une question simple, mais trop souvent ignorée (y compris par la critique décoloniale) : comment les « orientaux » ont-ils eux-mêmes pensé l'orientalisme ? La philosophie d'Afghāni et la « métaphysique insurrectionnelle » de l'émir Abdelkader ont été les lieux d'une résistance formulée au nom du savoir et d'une « critique traditionnelle de la tradition », et deviennent ici ceux de l'élaboration d'une « pensée-autre » (comme le disait Abdelkébir Khatibi, en partant de Fanon).

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: On The Fringes | Mentally surviving the rotten healthcare system
content:
Flower blooming outside the state mental health facility. Photo by Dominic Gutoman/Bulatlat.

I refer to the force pinning me down to the sofa. For hours, I negotiated with my own body and mind, trying to gather enough courage to leave the house and go to the public mental health facility.

The last time I was here, the queue was so long that it took seven hours to see the doctor. As the body ached in intense abdominal pain, I tried not to cave in. Today, I arrived at past seven in the morning and I was No. 40. I managed to get a seat. That is already a small victory for the expected long day.

Most patients need to be accompanied. I am fortunate that I can still do this on my own.

There is a certain kind of fortitude required to spend an entire day waiting in a public hospital. But this “strength” is a product of a decaying public healthcare, of a system designed to make people used to surviving what should never have been normal. When the system designed to care for us is also pulling us down, this “strength” is dangerous.

In this hospital, only one psychiatrist is assigned for all patients. This explains the hours of long lines of patients every day.

Based on a 2026 study of University of the Philippines, there are 409 PhilHealth-accredited psychiatrists in the country, translating to 0.38 psychiatrists per 100,000 population. It also noted that the country’s ratio of psychiatrists and population has been decreasing since 2016. This shortage is not only about numbers but also about people’s access to health services.

If people struggling with their mental health opt for private consultations, the average cost ranges from P1,500 ($23.89) to P5,000 ($79.63) per session.

For the poor who are forced to join the long lines, the cost of psychiatric care is not an incidental expense. It can deprive families of food for several days, not to mention money allocated for utility bills, transportation, and rent.

The situation is much worse for minimum wage earners or contractual employees living from paycheck to paycheck. Sacrificing one whole day to get immediate psychiatric care means income loss.

Think tank Ibon Foundation said that around 70 million Filipinos belong to the poorest and low-income classes, earning between P10,000 ($159.27) and P22,000 ($350.39) monthly.

The high cost of consultation left poor patients to rely on a rotten public mental health system. Of course, the shame and stigma tend to prevent people from seeking psychiatric help.

The 2023 data from the Department of Health (DOH) showed that more than 3.6 million Filipinos suffer from mental health conditions, neurological and substance use disorders. Among the most prevalent conditions are major depressive disorder (affecting more than 1.1 million people); bipolar disorder (520,000 people); and schizophrenia (more than 213,000 people).

Behind all these numbers is the long line right now, with me sitting on a worn out chair in the waiting area. Someone is constantly checking the clock. Someone is wondering if the doctor will see him before the day ends. And someone is trying not to give up in this dreadful wait.

I had the privilege to take a leave at work to prioritize my consultation. But an average Filipino worker does not have this privilege, especially minimum wage earners and the contractual workers trapped in a no-work-no-pay system.

It’s already 3:00 pm. The two bottles of water and three pieces of bread are gone. The cellphone battery is running low.

A first-time outpatient tells another that it took her a long time to finally bring herself here. “Because of shame,” she said.

Behind her, a woman in her 50s told her, “You shouldn’t be ashamed. We are all survivors.” Sitting in the waiting area for half a day, most of us heard several stories of survival.

We pretended not to listen. But we heard such stories. This explains why the waiting area is difficult to forget. I spent more hours here than in my consultations. Most of my conversations with the doctor took only 15 to 30 minutes.

It’s 4:00 pm now, almost nine hours of waiting. I am already next in line. I may not be a doctor and I may be struggling but it is clear that the public healthcare system is dying from decay. (RTS, DAA)

author: Forrest Wolfe
title: Meeting Persephone: A Katabasis of Bipolar Night
content:
I

n the Greek Eleusinian mysteries, Persephone was the maiden abducted by Hades. She became the ineffable queen of the underworld whose name must not be spoken. One archaic root of her name,

phónos

, means “murder.” Her abduction was also her death. Yet in the ancient Mediterranean world, pilgrims traveled to Eleusis seeking an epiphany of her that might inspire hope for the soul’s return.


Two and a half decades ago, in the crisis of my first psychotic collapse, I met Persephone.


The seeds of that encounter were prefigured by the memory of a woman—for whom I had no right to feel anything beyond the measure of our brief encounter. Just a few meetings and conversations around my hometown of East Northport, Long Island, after college. Something she said struck me, about going to nursing school because “that is the only thing I am any good at.” An intuition of a saintly meaning in her words, which would otherwise have seemed banal. Then I went away to film school in Los Angeles. I was twenty-three.


Can we live our stories forward into the unknown and recover them in the afterlife of memory—like a dying person gathering his tales? After my psychic collapse, five years later, I would write of this underestimated encounter with the woman whose name I shall encipher here as N: “In all possible worlds, I met her. In all possible worlds, I lost her. Madness is but a door to the underworld, or perhaps the casting of a spell…”


Time is a metronome counting off.


One. The disaster. Unnamable loss.


Two. It is a hole, deep and dark.


Three. The tomb is the womb.


With

whom

 was the encounter? Perhaps I was mad from this beginning, mad beyond measure. Then, all was forgotten for a while.


* * *


Fast forward a few years to life after film school, and to the night my mind shattered. Lived forward, the collapse felt like fragmented images constellating in a vortex of dark revelation. In hindsight, I see it was the beginning of

katabasis

—a descent into the underworld.


Signs of a deeply poetic nature began to speak to me: a flock of birds streaming through the tenements; a star-shaped leaf drifting on a torrent of rainwater; colors too intense to belong to the ordinary world. Then a young woman was murdered in my hometown.


At the time, I was working with the editorial staff on a documentary about

Psycho

, Gus Van Sant’s remake of Hitchcock’s film. Each evening, I watched the team rework the famous shower scene of a woman stabbed to death. In the blur of these signs, the murdered woman merged with the memory of the woman I once knew, whom I became convinced was in mortal danger.


Persephone was the maiden abducted by death. But one underworld myth weaves together with all the others, constellating together the ring of a laurel crown. I wrote in my diary of Orpheus, who lost his bride to Hades. By poetic metonymy, I became Orpheus. And Orpheus must descend to rescue her, even if his story is doomed.


So at 2 a.m., I called this woman’s house three times. She no longer lived there, but my desperate calls alarmed her parents. When her mother told me nothing was wrong, I realized I was quite mad. That moment precipitated my first psychotic free-fall—an abduction by underworld forces.


Writing for several days and nights, sleepless, in spiraling doodles on reams of notebook pages. Writing in many voices and “to the voices” —by whom I designate thoughts with an invasive agency so vivid that they did not belong to me. Writing myself to the gates of Hades. As the myth requires, Orpheus must fail. This is the brink where thoughts vanish into black. Nothing more to write. Except that the memory of this woman is a grave.


The ways we name this black can kill us. In the absence of an imaginal language, I could only imagine for myself compulsive flashes of my own death, by my own hand.


For three years I went in and out of hospitals, oscillating every few months between mania and suicidal depression. I underwent the standard regimen of medications, cognitive behavioral therapy and even a touch of Jungian therapy. One doctor advised, “Do not listen to the voices!” Yet I yearned for them—the dreams, the poetic signs, the strange illuminations where the streets shed their names, memories felt like inscriptions from a civilization that never quite existed, and people were shades in an underworld.


Another counselor advised, perhaps a little closer to the mark, “That woman was your anima” —the Jungian term for the …

author: Unknown
title: Algot Rosberg - Röda flammor
content:
Författare

: Algot Rosberg

Titel

: Röda flammor

Källa

: Tidningen Brand #5 1913


 Röda flammor heta stiga

 upp mot skyn, som färgas matt.

 Stadens kyrktorn stå och tiga

 i den mörka, svarta natt.


 Röda flammor dåvt ni spraka

 i er hårda, vreda strid.

 Nu palatsens väggar knaka,

 lossna, brista snart därvid.


 Röda flammor, ur ert fängsel

 äntligen ni sluppit ut,

 kvävda bakom mur och stängsel,

 eder frihet kom till slut.


 Röda flammor, praktfullt röda,

 hur jag längtat efter er!

 Intet kan er kraft nu döda,

 mänskor tröttnat lida mer.


 Röda flammor, härligt röda

 såsom eld och purpurfärg,

 gör nu slut på sorg och möda,

 skänk åt livet must och märg!


 Röda flammor, väl ni veta

 målet, som ni brinna för.

 I er eld, den klara, heta

 lyser hoppet, som ej dör.


 Röda flammor, nya tider,

 ni min längtans ljusa dröm!

 Nu ni brinna sent omsider,

 kämpande mot våldets ström.


 Röda flammor, flammor sköna,

 hur jag längtat efter er!

 Lycka skola alla röna,

 mänskor tröttnat lida mer.

A Synthesis: Bringing the Views Together

Ownership, according to Immanuel Kant, is “the mode of having something external to myself as my own.” As such, it is problematic, since ownership in effect means that someone has the exclusive right to control a part of the physical world. Or, in other words, someone has the right to exclude others from that part of the world. How does that fit with the ideas of the anarchism tradition?

One answer is simply that it doesn’t. Both collectivist and individualist anarchists usually agree on the importance of abolishing the privilege of private “bourgeois” property. But in general they also identify the impossibility of a society where no one has the exclusive right to anything. It would be a worldwide “tragedy of the commons,” where the natural resources soon would be exhausted simply because some people are too greedy. But still, anarchists cannot advocate regulations to stop some from using “too much” of the scarce resources. (Who would enforce such regulations?)

One solution might be a version of anarcho-communism, where everything is put under the “rule” of the communal collective. But that won’t do as a universal solution, unless one takes for granted that all people will voluntarily join a communal collective. Or that everyone would be forced to.

Instead, the anarchism tradition advocates possession rather than property. There is no consensus as to what possession really is, but the main difference between possession and property is usually that possession does not come with a never-ending right (as is the case with property). Possession is simply the right to control a piece of nature which is already in your control, i.e. an object you currently use. As soon as you let go of the object, your right to it is automatically abandoned.

These concepts might seem rather extreme versions of two opposing views on ownership. It is true that the meaning of both property and possession might vary some depending on the discussion. But in essence, the possession concept is a volatile ownership whereas property is a rather permanent, durable, and constant state of control.

The problem for anarchism is that not all anarchists agree on possession being justified, while some argue for the justification of private property. Most anarchists find themselves somewhere between these “extremes,” however with varying definitions of what is just ownership. Ownership, it must be concluded, is one of the reasons factions of anarchism seem unable to cooperate.

It should be noted that virtually all anarchists, when arguing for or against possession or property, share the same fundamental value as starting point: that the individual alone has the right to his self and that the laborer has the natural right to enjoy the full benefit of his labor. The difference in opinion regarding possession and property must consequently arise in the reasoning following this mutual anarchist standpoint. We have an equal right to ourselves and our labor. Статья Неттлау, воспроизведённая выше, — проникнутая, как она есть, широким духом свободы и солидарности и горячей любовью к делу Анархизма, — заслуживает и требует некоторых комментариев.

Неттлау утверждает, что причина или, по крайней мере, одна из причин того, что после стольких лет пропаганды, борьбы и жертв анархизм до сих пор не смог увлечь огромные массы людей и вдохновить их на восстание заключается в том, что анархисты двух течений – коммунистического и индивидуалистического – выдвинули свои собственные экономические теории как единственное решение социальной проблемы, в результате чего не сумели убедить людей, что их идеи вообще осуществимы.

Я искренне считаю, что основная причина нашей неудачи связана с тем, что в существующих условиях – то есть в данных нам материальных и моральных обстоятельствах, где массы трудящихся и нерабочие, но всё равно вовлечённые в созидание благ, страдают от одной и той же общественной организации – наша пропаганда может иметь лишь ограниченное влияние, а в некоторых крайне плачевных местах и среди наиболее терзаемых физической и моральной нищетой слоёв населения – вообще не оказывать никакого. Я убеждён, что только при изменении текущей среды, когда она станет более благоприятной для нас (подобное иногда может произойти в революционное время и только благодаря нашим собственным усилиям), наши идеи будут завоёвывать всё большее число людей и повышать вероятность их практического воплощения. Разделение на коммунистов и индивидуалистов мало относится к этому, поскольку оно интересует лишь тех, кто уже является анархистом, или незначительное меньшинство потенциальных анархистов.

Но тем не менее верно, что полемика между индивидуалистами и коммунистами часто отнимала у нас много сил. Она мешала, даже когда это было возможно, развитию искреннего и братского сотрудничества между всеми анархистами и вносила раздоры среди тех, кто, если бы они были едины, присоединился бы к нам из-за нашей страстной любви к свободе. Поэтому Неттлау не зря отстаивает достижение согласия между анархистами и показывает, что для наступления настоящей свободы, то есть анархии, должна существовать возможность выбора, где каждый имеет возможность устроить свою жизнь так, как ему удобно, будь он сторонником коммунистического или индивидуалистического анархизма, или какой угодно степени или какой угодно смеси того и другого.

Но Неттлау, на мой взгляд, ошибается, полагая, что различия между анархистами, называющими себя коммунистами, и теми, кто называет себя индивидуалистами, действительно основаны на том, как каждый из них представляет себе экономическую жизнь (производство и распределение продуктов) в анархическом обществе. В конце концов, это вопросы, касающиеся далёкого будущего; и если верно, что идеал как конечная цель – это маяк, который направляет или должен направлять поведение людей, то ещё более верно, что больше всего согласие и несогласие между людьми определяет не то, что мы хотим делать завтра, а то, что мы делаем и хотим сделать сегодня. Как правило, мы лучше ладим и больше заинтересованы в том, чтобы ладить с попутчиками, идущими тем же путём, что и мы, но преследующими другие цели, чем с теми, кто, хотя и говорит, что хочет добраться туда же, куда и мы, но идёт противоположной дорогой! Так сложилось, что анархисты разных направлений, несмотря на то, что в принципе стремятся к одному и тому же, в повседневной жизни и своей пропаганде оказываются в жесткой оппозиции друг к другу.

Учитывая основополагающий принцип анархизма, что никто не должен желать и иметь средства угнетать других и заставлять их работать на себя, то становится очевидно, что анархизм допускает все и только те формы жизненного устройства, которые уважают свободу и признают за каждым …

author: Unknown
title: Axel Holmström - Skräckväldet på Långholmen
content:
Författare

: Axel Holmström

Titel

: Skräckväldet på Långholmen

Källa

: Tidningen Brand #5 1913


 I avslagsyrkandet på nådeansökan från Tomelilla för Algot Rosberg, Anton Nilsson och Alfred Stern skriver direktör Wollin att Rosberg uppfört sig »dåligt under strafftiden».


 En stor del av bevakningspersonalen på Långholmen och flera frigivna påstå motsatsen; de säga att det i flesta fall är Wollin som brutit mot Fångvårdsstyrelsens instruktion. De beundra Rosberg att han kunnat behärska sig som han gjort. Och man måste ge dem rätt.


 Från första dagen Rosberg kom till Långholmen har Wollin uppträtt på ett brutalt, utmanande sätt mot vår kamrat. Det ser ut, som om hans avsikt vore, att genom att raffinerad grym behandling få Rosberg så bitter och uppretad att han till sist skulle »förgå sig» mot direktörn. Ty gjorde Rosberg aldrig så lite våld mot Wollin, kom han nog aldrig ut med livet. Och av allt att döma, tycks detta vara Wollins önskan. Men Rosberg har nog genomskådat dessa planer, och det är säkerligen därför han kunnat resignera och genomgå så ohyggliga lidanden som han gjort på Långholmen.


 Då Rosberg i februari 1909 kom till Långholmen hittade man som bekant en liten sågklinga i den brödkaka han hade med sig. För detta dömdes Rosberg till 30 dagar utan arbete, därav 8 dygn utan sängkläder. Under de 8 dygn, då han låg på golvet, var cellen alldeles tom. Det enda som fanns var en vattenmugg och ett nattkärl. Men man nöjde sig ej med detta, utan man stängde av värmledningen till den cell Rosberg låg eller rättare gick i. Och detta mitt i kalla vintern. Konstaplar ha sagt mig, att isblommorna antogo allt vackrare former på den lilla fönstergluggen. Ett tydligt bevis för, att värmledningen verkligen var avstängd. Själv har jag två vintrar haft tillfälle se, att det ej blir isblommor på fönstergluggarna, då cellerna äro uppvärmda.


 Det påstås, att Rosberg under dessa dagar förvägrades tala med läkaren.


 Innan denna 30 dagars tortyr var slut hostade Rosberg blod. Det dröjde ett och ett halvt år innan han repade sig efter denna knäck.


 Det första brev jag fick från Rosberg från Långholmen är skrivet 29 maj 1910 och däri skriver han:


 »Du frågar hur jag mår, om jag är frisk. Ja, käre broder jag vet det knappast själv. Under vissa tider överfalles jag av en mattighetskänsla, som gör att jag knappt kan hålla mig uppe. Tvänne gånger har jag måst lägga mig till sängs, några dagar varje gång. Nu pågår just en sådan period. Jag är så kraftlös ,att jag knappt förmår lyfta prässjärnet. Du vet väl att jag är skräddare? Så desslikes har jag emellanåt obehagliga stickningar i bröstet.»


 Är det inte dåligt, direktör Wollin, att behandla en fånge som ni har för att »uppfostra» så omänskligt grymt? Är det meningen att Ni skall ödelägga fångarnas hälsa?


 När direktör Wollin hade semester på sommaren 1910 sjukskrev Rosberg sig och frågade doktor Sällberg om han inte kunde få flytta in i en sjukcell. Detta låvade läkaren strax. Dag efter dag gick, men Rosberg fick ej flytta in i sjukcellen. Då frågade han löjtnant Vik, vilken tjänstgjorde som direktör under Wollins semester, varför läkarens order ej verkställdes. Rosberg fick det svaret, att de ej

tordes

 förrän Wollin kom hem. Detta visar väl tydligt, vilket strängt och självrådigt regemente Wollin för därute.


 När Wollin så äntligen kom hem, fick Rosberg flytta in i sjukcell. Därom skrev Rosberg i ett brev till en annan pärson den 7 augusti 1910:


 »Men först bör du veta att jag fått en cell med stort fönster. Kan du tänka dig hur det käns att komma från graven upp i ljuset? Vidare har jag fått sjukmat, en halv portion. På de sista tre veckorna har jag ej ätit annat än gröt. Nu börjar jag snart få matlust igen. Luften gör mycket.»


 Rosberg fick så sitta i sjukcell till i februari 1912. Således ett och ett halvt år. Ett ojävigt bevis för att det ej var en tillfällig sjukdom. Nej, under de åtta dygnen han låg på golvet, då värmledningen var avstängd, hade hans hälsa fullständigt brutits.


 Under den tid, Rosberg i fjor var på »gemensamheten» kryade han till sig ganska bra. Men så kom den grymma tortyren den 4 sept. med åtföljande strapatser. Detta har åter för en tid knäckt hans svaga hälsa.

¡JOVEN! Tú, a quien el Gobierno está intentando atraer al ejército y a la marina, ¡ten cuidado! Piénsalo bien antes de dar ese paso. Reflexiona sobre lo que estás a punto de hacer y el propósito al que vas a servir. Pregúntate cuál es el sentido del servicio militar y de la guerra. ¿Quieres prepararte para asesinar? ¿Quieres que te entrenen para la matanza en masa y, cuando te lo ordenen, matar a tus semejantes, hombres como tú, a quienes ni siquiera has visto y que nunca te han hecho ningún daño? Piénsalo, y si hay una chispa de hombría en tu corazón, te invadirá el horror y el asco ante la mera idea del servicio militar.

Quizá seas uno de los desempleados, sin dinero ni amigos. Pero es cien veces mejor sufrir la necesidad y el hambre que ponerte el uniforme que simboliza la obediencia cobarde y el asesinato de tus hermanos. Ten en cuenta que es precisamente este poder militar al que se te pide que te unas el que mantiene las condiciones que te mantienen a ti y a miles de personas más en la inanición y la miseria. Si te pones el uniforme, contribuyes a fortalecer y perpetuar este poder y te conviertes en la herramienta ciega de la clase que roba y mata bajo el pretexto del patriotismo. A ellos les sale muy rentable. Incluso inculcan a los niños de primaria el espíritu del chovinismo fanfarrón y el odio asesino, porque el patriotismo aumenta los beneficios y incrementa los dividendos. ¿Quieres ayudarles?

No es digno de un hombre que piensa ser una herramienta ciega y obediente. Pero aún menos digno es entrenarse para ese fin y someterse a humillaciones y tratos inhumanos con el fin de aprender a matar y asesinar.

¡Joven! Eres un hombre pobre, un hijo de los pobres. Es un espectáculo terrible y vergonzoso que, en todos los países, los hijos de los trabajadores constituyan el ejército cuyo propósito es perpetuar la esclavitud del trabajo. ¿Puedes quejarte de la opresión y la explotación si te prestas a sostener el sistema de robo económico, si tomas las armas para defenderlo? Mientras haya suficientes jóvenes que se dejen llevar al matadero como un rebaño de ovejas y que estén dispuestos a participar en expediciones de robo y asesinato (pues eso es lo que realmente es la guerra), las clases poseedoras seguirán robando y asesinando, masacrando a gran escala y exterminando países enteros. Vosotros, los hijos del pueblo, vosotros, jóvenes trabajadores de este país, solo vosotros podéis poner fin a estas cosas terribles y a sus espantosas consecuencias, negándoos a alistaros en el ejército y la marina, negándoos a que os utilicen como verdugos, cazadores de hombres y perros guardianes.

Ya los «grandes» generales y otros patriotas bien pagados hablan de reclutamiento obligatorio. Quieren introducir el servicio militar obligatorio en este país, tal y como han hecho las tiranías de Europa. Es hora de demostrarles que el pueblo ve más allá de sus infames maquinaciones. Que la generación joven se mantenga alejada de las oficinas de reclutamiento y se niegue a ser utilizada como carne de cañón.

La misión del soldado no difiere de la del asesino a sueldo que mata a un hombre por encargo, salvo que el soldado recibe una paga menor por sus servicios, aunque debe estar preparado no solo para un asesinato, sino para una matanza a gran escala. En una amarga ironía de su …

Федерико Стакельберг, русско-французский социалист, известный помимо своей политической деятельности также ценными работами по популяризации астрономии, говорит (в Le Semeur de Normandie от 25 октября), что «социализм есть не что иное, как биологический монизм наук и деяний XIX века и астрономический монизм Ренессанса, подтверждённый сегодняшними открытиями спектрального анализа».

Что означает, на бедном языке, что если бы дальнейшие открытия породили биологические теории, отличные от тех, которые возобладали в XIX веке, и если бы спектральный анализ показал, что светила состоят из материй, отличных от тех, которые составляют нашу планету, то социализм не имел бы основания существовать, а социалисты были бы неправы!!!

Однако Стакельберг – не просто астроном, который живёт с головой в небесах и который мог бы говорить о социализме из снобизма, в действительности не зная, что это такое. Он есть или был воинствующим социалистом (когда-то он даже анархиствовал), внёс свой вклад в борьбу за человеческое освобождение и продолжает ещё со страстью заниматься социальными вопросами. В самом деле, в той же статье, из которой мы взяли это ошеломляющее определение социализма, читается также:

«Программа, ближайшая цель Социализма или научного Коммунизма есть:

I) Обобществление земли и всех средств производства;

II) Освобождение женщины через установление её гражданского, политического и экономического равенства с мужчиной: что повлечёт за собой конец всей старой морали наших предков;

III) Администрирование мировым производством, основанным на эквивалентности работ, приходит на смену правлению человека над человеком».

Хорошая программа. Но какое отношение всё это имеет к спектральному анализу?!

Мы не стали бы обращать на это внимание, если бы речь шла о каком-то единичном случае, совершающимся учёными, которые, терзаемые поиском универсальной формулы, способной объяснить всё – и то, что воспринимают чувства, и то, что постигает мысль, и то, что творит жизнь, – легко дают увлечь себя рискованными утверждениями и гротескными сближениями.

Беда, к сожалению, распространена широко и, возможно, особенно среди наших.

У нас стол завален писаниями добрых товарищей, которые, желая дать «научную основу» анархизму, производят мешанину, которая была бы смешной, если бы её не делало жалким очевидность усилия, предпринятого в искренней вере в то, что они служат делу. И самое жалкое во всём этом то, что большинство извиняется, что не может сделать лучше, потому что… не имело возможности изучить что-то лучше.

Но тогда почему бы не лезть в то, чего не знаешь, чтобы потом делать такие ошибки, вместо того чтобы делать хорошую пропаганду, основанную на человеческих нуждах и чаяниях?

Конечно, не нужно быть докторами наук, чтобы быть хорошим и полезными анархистами, – напротив, иногда это вредит. Но чтобы говорить о науке, возможно, не было бы бесполезно знать в ней кое-что!

И пусть нас не обвиняют, как сделал недавно один товарищ, в том, что мы мало ценим науку. Напротив, мы знаем, какая это прекрасная, великая, могущественная и полезная вещь – наука; мы знаем, как она служит освобождению мысли и торжеству человека в борьбе против враждебных сил природы: и поэтому мы хотели бы, чтобы мы сами и все товарищи имели возможность составить себе о Науке синтетическое представление и углубить её хотя бы в одной из её бесчисленных областей.

В нашей программе написано не только хлеб для всех, но и наука для всех. Но нам кажется, что для того, чтобы говорить о науках с пользой, следовало бы сначала составить себе ясное понятие о её целях и её функции.

Наука, как и хлеб, не есть бесплатный дар Природы. Её нужно завоёвывать с трудом, и мы боремся за то, чтобы создать условия, которые сделают этот труд возможным для всех.

title: Ukraine’s genuine anti-authoritarian resistance is concentrating in certain areas and revealing internal contradictions
content:
"Beat the TRC." Early summer, on the walls of Petro Kalnyshevskyi Avenue, the city of Dnieper (Dnipro)

The activity of our media depends solely on its audience. Please support our work on this fundraising page for further coverage of topics that are forbidden or invisible to the pro-capitalist press. Many thanks everyone!

The long, hot summer has officially ended a month ago, yet its echoes continue to resonate across the country. As winter approaches—promising to be the harshest since 1991—hundreds of thousands or even millions of people have been backed into a corner and driven to such a state of utter desperation that they no longer think about the consequences.

No positive prospects: if you are not killed on the spot, you highly likely will be imprisoned—and, in all likelihood, no one will even know your name. No international solidarity; even if your name does become known, none of the foreign anti-militarists reading this overview will show up at embassies or other government missions to support you. All that remains is a desperate desire to sell your life dearly.

As early as last autumn, we noted that anti-war direct action in Ukraine becomes concentrated in some areas. This summer, that trend has intensified.

For instance, late in the evening on June 14, a mass confrontation involving patrol police and territorial recruitment center (TRC) personnel broke out on Balzac Avenue in Troieshchyna—a rough neighborhood in Kiev—following an attempt to forcibly detain a man of conscription age. According to the cops, the driver had committed a traffic violation and attempted to flee; during his detention, he struck a patrolman, and it subsequently emerged that he was also in violation of mobilization legislation. A crowd of several hundred people gathered at the scene, chanting "Shame!" and partially blocking traffic in order to interfere with the officers. Both sides used tear gas, and protesters damaged a service vehicle. Ultimately, the detained man was successfully taken away and transported to the TRC:

On July 29, the Kiev City TRC reported another high-profile incident: during the military medical examination at the Podolsky District TRC, a young man—who had been forcibly rounded up off the street—fatally stabbed a surgeon. She was 65 years old. According to the prosecutor's office, the 31-year-old man demanded a thorough examination, complained of a toothache, and asked to be released for a few days. "Upon realizing he was being declared fit for service, the man inflicted about 17 chaotic stab wounds on the doctor’s chest, neck, and arms. He had been carrying the knife in his bag. The woman died at the scene from her injuries." Following this news, many hoped that butchers in white coats might finally—at least occasionally—recall the Hippocratic Oath. It seems not; the others will keep laughing in response to talk about diagnoses until they, too, run into something sharp and pointed.

Vinnytsia has been a center of resistance against the dictatorship for over a year. On July 6, police in this regional center stopped a bus driver and sent him to an enlistment office. In response, his colleagues—specifically drivers on routes 1A, 2A, and 2B—staged a strike, refusing to operate their routes for several hours. The following day, the regional TRC announced that the driver had been released because no military unit was willing to accept him for service; operations subsequently resumed. On July 8, in the settlement of Tyvriv, an escapee from the army fought off Military Law Enforcement Service personnel with an axe, according to the service's press office. Reports indicate that the man began to resist when asked to present his documents. Three other individuals soon joined the altercation and damaged an official vehicle. The service’s representatives then called for reinforcements from the "Scorpion" rapid response unit; meanwhile, the man armed himself with an axe and injured two members of the search team. On July 25, a violator of military registration requirements pulled out a folding knife and struck one of the enlistment agents while being escorted to the recruitment center. title: Ephéméride des luttes : 3 octobre
content:
L'éphéméride des luttes du 3 octobre soutient les grèves, celles de la faim comme celle des cheminots. En bref, elle soutient celles et ceux qui luttent contre des conditions de vie toujours plus dures afin d'ouvrir la voie à une libération collective et totale.


1920 :

 En Angleterre, grève d'un million de mineurs contre l'allongement du temps de travail.


1975 :

 A Sienne en Italie, le siège du comité provincial de la Démocratie Chrétienne (le parti au pouvoir) est incendié.


1977 :

 A Rome, l'enterrement de Walter Rossi, assassiné le

30 septembre

 par les fascistes, a lieu à San Giovanni. Deux manifestations en partent pour se diriger vers un siège bien connu du MSI, le nouveau parti fasciste. Des affrontements s'y déroulent avec la police qui défend le local. Le deuxième cortège se dirige ailleurs, incendie un camion des carabinieri et attaque un bar fréquenté par les fascistes, qui est complètement détruit, tandis qu'un incendie et une charge de dynamite détruisent entièrement un autre siège du MSI. Des voitures sont incendiées et un policier est blessé par une balle reçue dans la nuque, tandis qu'une troisième antenne des fascistes est attaquée.


1981 :

 - A Belfast en Irlande du Nord, fin de la grève de la faim des prisonniers de l'IRA après 7 mois de grève tournante. Dix militants sont morts lors de cette grève de la faim.


 A Paris, une manifestation antinucléaire réunit autour de 5000 personnes. En fin de manifestation, des affrontements ont lieu entre les autonomes et la police : la porte du ministère des Transports est enfoncée et un véhicule présent dans la cour est incendié, tandis que les fenêtres sont brisées.


1984 :

 A Dilbeek (Bruxelles), les Cellules Communistes Combattantes (CCC) incendient les camions stockés dans le dépôt de la société MAN Truck, l'un des plus gros constructeurs militaires allemands. Vous pouvez retrouver le communiqué de l'action à

cette adresse

, ainsi que des photos.


1993 :

 En Allemagne, dernières actions des Cellules Révolutionnaires (RZ) contre des véhicules de la police des frontières à Francfort-sur-l'Oder et Görlitz.


2006 :

 A Silver Springs, dans le Maryland aux États-Unis, un groupe autonome revendique une nouvelle attaque contre un centre de recrutement de l'armée afin de saboter la machine de guerre américaine.


2014 :

 - Au Chili, mort de l'ancien militant du FPMR (groupe de lutte armée contre la dictature de Pinochet) Jorge Saldivia au cours d'une

attaque de fourgon bancaire

.


 A Santiago, toujours au Chili, sur un campus universitaire, le 'Groupe Anarchiste Coordonné (GAC) Bande Organisée Mauricio Morales / Cellule Incendiaire Sebastián Oversluij'

bloque les rues avec des pneus enflammés puis attaque la police au molotov

.


2017 :

 A Murcia en Espagne, des affrontements ont lieu contre la police après trois semaines de manifestions contre une nouvelle ligne de TGV. Des barricades

sont dressées et incendiées

 en travers des routes.


2018 :

 Tard le soir, une voiture de Bouygues

est incendiée

 dans le 17ème à Paris en soutien "aux anarchistes torturé-e-s et emprisonné-es en Russie, ainsi qu'aux 8 de Bâle qui passeront en procès fin octobre pour une déambulation sauvage et saccageuse un soir de juin 2016".

title: First Kurdish Film Festival kicks off in Freiburg
content:
The First Kurdish Film Festival in Freiburg, has begun at Kommunales Kino. The festival is organized by the Avesta Cultural Association, established through the joint initiative of Kurdish cinema organizations in Freiburg.


Members of the Freiburg Film Commune Organizing Committee, Newroz Sönmez and Mustafa Özel, delivered the festival’s opening speeches. They were followed by a performance by Hozan Axîn.


On the first day of the festival, “Zare,” a 1926 Armenian-language silent drama written and directed by Hamo Beknazaryan, was screened. The film, produced in the Armenian Soviet Socialist Republic, was presented on screen accompanied by a live musical performance.


The program also featured a short film by a Kurdish director born in Kirkuk who lives in Norway. The film, which tells the story of three young people living in a refugee camp in northern Norway, was screened on the festival’s opening day.


 


16 films to be screened


The three-day festival, taking place from October 2 to 4, will feature a total of 16 films: four feature films, four documentaries and eight short films.


On the second day of the festival, the documentary “Vartinis,” directed by Mehmet Ömer Biçer, will be screened at Kommunales Kino to mark the anniversary of the Vartinis Massacre.


The festival program will also feature the films Hevras, Hemo Mori, Mein Vater, der Gastarbeiter and Hevî.


The first Kurdish Film Festival to be held in Freiburg will bring audiences the work of Kurdish filmmakers from different countries and showcase a range of narratives from Kurdish cinema.
